domains.summary: The actor domain today is a 4-tool stub (spawn/delete/list/transform) — thinner than every competitor's actor surface and missing the unglamorous core: introspection, selection, batch/mass edits, hierarchy, reflection property-set, and transactional bundling. Strategy: (1) ship an inspection-first read pair for every write (actor_inspect/find/get_selection) so the agent never edits blind; (2) collapse Roblox/Unity-style mass ops into a few outcome-verbs (batch_set_property, batch_transform, replace_class) each wrapped in ONE FScopedTransaction so a mass edit is one Ctrl+Z — the named differentiator vs Epic's per-call undo; (3) lean the moats by routing every mutation through PLUMB validate-before/after and a dry_run→commit preview, and tying actor_focus into the vision loop. Nearly all ship as python_run-backed pyTemplate descriptors (EditorActorSubsystem + reflection) with zero plugin rebuild; only the cross-call transaction seam and bounds-buffer pass want C++ for robustness. This takes the domain from 4 honest tools to ~32, surpassing GenOrca/Roblox actor coverage while keeping the safety depth none of them have.
dependencies: EditorActorSubsystem / UnrealEditorSubsystem / LevelEditorSubsystem (UE Python Editor-Scripting) — backs ~30 of the tools
Hardened python_run handler (SEH + security gate + dangling-delegate gate) — the dispatch path for every pyTemplate descriptor
Theme 1 add-a-tool refactor: pyTemplate factory + single ToolDescriptor + auto-collected sidecar — required before bulk-adding these as first-class tools without 7-file churn

tool-executor.ts executeCommand transport (existing) — actor_spawn/delete/list/transform already use it; align timeouts + gate blind retry to idempotent ops (spawn/duplicate/delete are NOT idempotent)

C++ HaybaMCPToolkit + HaybaGameThread::RunSync seam + FScopedTransaction — required for the cross-call transaction_begin/commit/undo/redo (Python ScopedEditorTransaction cannot span separate MCP calls)
PLUMB validator hooks (validator_run / plumb_validate) — for actor_verify and validate-before/after-mutate on batch ops
editor_capture_viewport / render_camera (vision sidecar) — for actor_focus before/after capture
Plan-Mode gate (bPlanApproved) — gates destructive verbs (delete, replace_class, batch_set_property)
FProperty/Reflection import_text coercion path — backs set_property / batch_set_property / get_property typed read-write
risks: actor_id stability: content-path vs FGuid/label can drift across undo/redo, duplicate, and PIE — must pick a stable handle (level-relative path + guid) or batch ops target the wrong actors after a transaction

Reflection set_property type coercion: import_text on structs/enums/object-refs/arrays is brittle; silent no-ops or partial writes — every set must read back (hence actor_verify) and report per-field failures

Cross-call transactions: Python ScopedEditorTransaction is per-call only; spanning MCP calls needs the C++ seam, and a left-open transaction can swallow unrelated user edits into one undo — must auto-timeout/auto-commit and surface open-transaction state
Batch ops on large selections block the game thread (same class as the build_*/test_run freeze) — cap selection size, paginate, or route through a job-envelope; dry_run must not also stall
Non-idempotent retry: the transport's blind retry can double-spawn/double-delete — these verbs must be excluded from auto-retry
actor_replace_class loses component-level/instanced overrides not expressible on the new class — must report unmapped properties, not silently drop them
snap_to_floor / line traces hit invisible collision or nothing (no collision geometry, Nanite) — report missed actors rather than leaving them at origin
Editor groups / attach world-transform preservation differ between EditorActorSubsystem versions and UE 5.7→5.8 — pin and test per engine version
domains.test_plan: "On a live UE editor with a scratch level: (1) actor_spawn_from_asset a cube → actor_inspect confirms transform/components. (2) actor_duplicate count=5 along X → actor_list paginated shows 6, has_more correct. (3) actor_select by class then actor_batch_set_property on a light-intensity-style prop with dry_run=true → confirm diff has 0 mutations, then commit and actor_verify each matches expected. (4) actor_transaction_begin → run batch_transform + assign_material + set_tags → transaction_commit → press Ctrl+Z ONCE in-editor and confirm ALL three revert together (the core differentiator), then actor_redo restores. (5) actor_align distribute on the 6 copies → actor_bounds pairwise confirms equal spacing. (6) actor_snap_to_floor over a landscape → snapped[] all sit on surface, missed[] empty; verify with render_camera. (7) actor_replace_class cube→a Blueprint actor → unmapped_props reported, transform transferred. (8) actor_attach two actors to a parent, move parent via actor_transform, actor_inspect children show world transform preserved. (9) actor_focus on the group with capture=true → returns a framed viewport PNG. (10) actor_delete with Plan-Mode unapproved → blocked; approve → deleted_count correct, actor_undo restores. Cross-check every read tool (inspect/find/get_property/bounds/get_selection) returns the same values the writes claimed; run validator_run before/after the batch to confirm no constraint regressions."

tools.signature: (asset_path, location?, rotation?, scale?, label?, snap_to_floor?) -> {actor_id, transform}

tools.name: actor_duplicate

tools.name: actor_delete

tools.name: actor_inspect

tools.name: actor_list

tools.name: actor_select
tools.parity: Roblox get_selection (read only); net-new write selection
tools.description: Set the editor selection from ids or an inline query — makes selection an addressable target for batch ops and viewport capture

tools.name: actor_get_selection

tools.name: actor_transform
tools.description: Set absolute location/rotation/scale of one actor — base move verb; existing tool, transaction-wrap

tools.name: actor_transform_relative
tools.description: Apply a delta move/rotate/scale to actor(s) — additive nudge that avoids reading-then-writing absolute values; safer for batch

tools.name: actor_batch_transform
tools.description: Apply one transform/delta across a selection or query in a single transaction — outcome-verb replacing N per-actor calls; one Ctrl+Z

tools.name: actor_batch_set_property
tools.description: Reflection set of any UProperty across many actors in one transaction — the mass-edit workhorse (e.g. set every light intensity); dry_run shows the diff first

tools.name: actor_set_property

tools.name: actor_get_property
tools.description: Read one UProperty (nested path) off an actor/component — the read half of set_property; used for verify and conditional logic

tools.name: actor_replace_class
tools.description: Find-replace actor class across a selection, transferring transform/tags/folder/overrides where possible — swap placeholders for final assets without re-placing

tools.name: actor_assign_material
tools.description: Set a material override on slot(s) of actor(s) — batch material-assign verb; pairs with PLUMB sliver/profile binding

tools.name: actor_batch_rename
tools.description: Rename a selection by a pattern with auto-numbering tokens — World Outliner hygiene at scale in one transaction

tools.name: actor_set_label
tools.description: Rename a single actor's display label — the simple outliner rename

tools.name: actor_set_tags
tools.description: Add/remove gameplay tags (actor.Tags) on actor(s) — makes actors queryable and groupable for later batch ops

tools.name: actor_set_folder
tools.parity: Unity hierarchy; net-new for UE peers
tools.description: Move actor(s) into a World Outliner folder path — organizational hygiene the agent needs to keep big scenes navigable

tools.name: actor_attach
tools.description: Attach actor(s) to a parent actor (optionally to a socket), keeping or zeroing world transform — builds hierarchies without manual component fiddling

tools.name: actor_detach
tools.description: Detach actor(s) from their parent, preserving world transform — the inverse of attach

tools.name: actor_group
tools.description: Create an editor group (or ungroup) from a selection — single-handle manipulation of related actors

tools.name: actor_align
tools.description: Align/distribute/snap-many a selection to an axis, the grid, or a reference actor's pivot/bounds — outcome-verb for layout cleanup

tools.name: actor_snap_to_floor
tools.description: Raycast down (or along a direction) and drop actor(s) onto underlying geometry/landscape — kills the floating/buried-asset problem after spawn

tools.name: actor_snap_to_socket
tools.description: Snap/attach an actor onto a named socket of another actor's mesh — precise placement (e.g. prop into a hand/wall socket)

tools.name: actor_set_mobility
tools.description: Set Static/Stationary/Movable mobility on actor(s) — gates lighting bake/physics; a common correctness fix agents otherwise miss

tools.name: actor_set_visibility
tools.description: Toggle hidden-in-editor / hidden-in-game on actor(s) — staging and screenshot isolation for the vision loop

tools.name: actor_add_component
tools.parity: net-new moat (peers stop at actor level)
tools.description: Add a component (mesh/light/collision/etc.) to an actor instance and set its initial props — compose actors without a Blueprint

tools.name: actor_bounds
tools.description: Return world/local bounding box, pivot, and pairwise distance for actor(s) — the measure/verify read that drives align, snap, and auto-frame

tools.name: actor_focus
tools.parity: Roblox capture_screenshot; extends Hayba vision moat
tools.description: Select actor(s), frame the editor camera on their bounds, and (optionally) return a viewport PNG — ties actor edits into the vision feedback loop for before/after verification

tools.name: actor_transaction_begin
tools.description: Open a named transaction so multiple subsequent actor edits collapse into ONE undo — the explicit multi-step bundling differentiator vs Epic's per-call undo

tools.name: actor_transaction_commit
tools.description: Close the open transaction, finalizing the bundle as a single undoable step (or cancel to roll back) — completes the run_tool_script→one-Ctrl+Z story

tools.name: actor_undo
tools.description: Trigger editor Undo (optionally N steps) and report what reverted — recover from a bad batch without leaving the agent loop

tools.name: actor_redo
tools.description: Trigger editor Redo (N steps) — symmetric recovery

tools.name: actor_verify
tools.parity: Flop pie_test assertions; Roblox compare_instances; PLUMB moat
tools.description: Assert that actors match an expected spec (transform/property/material/tag) and return per-field pass/fail — the post-mutate read-back that turns guesses into closed-loop edits

domains.summary:
UE's GeometryScript library (UGeometryScriptLibrary_* operating on UDynamicMesh) is almost entirely BlueprintCallable and therefore reachable from python_run with zero plugin rebuild, so the whole procedural-mesh authoring loop ships as pyTemplate descriptors over the hardened python_run handler. The spine is inspect (existing C++ mesh_extract/topology readback, just needs first-class wrappers) -> edit (GeometryScript ops) -> validate (route topology numbers through PLUMB pass/fail) -> bake (CopyMeshToStaticMesh asset commit). Because commit 5f3cf96 drops a script's UObject wrappers inside the SEH guard, transient DynamicMesh handles do NOT survive across separate python_run calls, so the P0 vehicle is geo_pipeline (an ordered op list run source->dest in ONE call) plus atomic source->dest ops; a rooted C++ scratch-mesh pool is the optional robust path. Moats pressed: inspection-first paired reads, dry-run-before-commit (only world_generate had it), PLUMB quantified topology validation (manifold/winding/holes verdicts a screenshot cannot give), and transaction-wrapped single-undo baking. This out-tools every competitor's mesh surface; none validate topology numerically or dry-run mesh edits.</summary>
<parameter name="dependencies">["GeometryScripting + GeometryFramework UE plugins enabled (UGeometryScriptLibrary_* + UDynamicMesh/UDynamicMeshComponent)", "Existing C++ FHaybaMCPStaticMeshHandler (mesh_extract/mesh_topology_stats/mesh_list_dynamic) - wrap as first-class, do not reimplement", "Hardened python_run handler (SEH + 3-tier gate + dangling-delegate gate) as the pyTemplate dispatch substrate", "unreal.EditorStaticMeshLibrary / StaticMeshEditorSubsystem for Nanite/LOD/collision/lightmap authoring", "PLUMB stack (plumb_validate, plumb_profile_bake, plumb_socket_add) for the topology-validation and socket moats", "Add-a-tool pyTemplate factory (Theme 1, Section 5) - these descriptors are its first heavy customer", "Cross-cutting Transaction/undo C++ seam (Theme 4C) for single-Ctrl+Z bake bundling", "Vision loop (render_camera/editor_capture_viewport) for after-bake visual verify"]
risks: python_run UObject GC (commit 5f3cf96): transient DynamicMesh wrappers are dropped after each call, so cross-call geo_mesh handles are unreliable - lead with single-call geo_pipeline; only ship the handle pool if backed by a rooted C++ pool in HaybaMCPToolkit
GeometryScripting plugin may be disabled in a target project; every geo_* tool must probe and return an actionable 'enable GeometryScripting' error code, not a python stack trace

CopyMeshToStaticMesh / build on a large mesh can approach python_run timeout; heavy bakes (Nanite build, LOD gen, convex decomposition) may need the job-envelope async path (Theme 0) rather than a sync call
Mutating an actor's live UDynamicMeshComponent without FScopedTransaction yields no undo; bake/apply ops must wrap in the C++ transaction seam (4C) or be flagged non-undoable
Boolean/voxel/remesh can silently produce non-manifold or inverted-winding output; mandatory post-op mesh_validate prevents shipping broken geometry
Overwriting an existing UStaticMesh asset breaks references and is destructive - must respect Plan-Mode gate and default to dry_run + new-asset-path
UV unwrap (XAtlas/PatchBuilder) is nondeterministic and slow; treat as P2 and cap input tri count
domains.test_plan: On a live editor with GeometryScripting enabled: (1) Spawn or pick a PCG grammar shell actor; run mesh_inspect + mesh_list to confirm the C++ readback surfaces tris/verts/topology. (2) geo_primitive_new(box) -> geo_bake_to_staticmesh(new path); reopen the asset and mesh_inspect it to confirm counts and a closed manifold (non_manifold_vertices==0, is_closed). (3) geo_dry_run a boolean-subtract pipeline and confirm predicted topology stats return WITHOUT creating an asset; then geo_pipeline the same ops with commit and diff predicted vs actual via mesh_validate. (4) geo_remesh + geo_simplify to a target tri count, verify mesh_validate reports manifold + the tri budget hit. (5) staticmesh_set_nanite + staticmesh_generate_lods, then staticmesh_brief to read back nanite flag, LOD count, screen sizes, collision, lightmap UV index. (6) geo_uv_project(box) then mesh_inspect UV-channel report; render_camera before/after for visual confirm. (7) mesh_batch_apply a normals-recompute across N selected actors; confirm count and per-actor verdicts. (8) Run an intentionally broken op (boolean producing holes) and confirm mesh_validate returns red with a non-zero boundary_loops unsat-core. (9) Bake, then editor undo (Ctrl+Z) once, confirm the whole pipeline reverts as a single transaction. (10) Disable GeometryScripting and confirm every geo_* tool returns the actionable enable-plugin error code.

tools.name: mesh_inspect
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (or thin wrapper over existing C++ FHaybaMCPStaticMeshHandler::MeshExtract)
tools.parity: net-new moat (numeric topology verdict; competitors only screenshot)
tools.signature: (actor_label?|asset_path?, lod?, component_index?, include_triangles?, include_positions?, include_normals?, max_elements?, bbox_min?, bbox_max?) -> {source, counts, topology, bounds, triangles?, vertices?, face_normals?, truncated}
tools.description: First-class wrapper over the C++ mesh_extract: numeric geometry + topology readback (welds, winding, holes, components, surface area, volume, genus) a screenshot cannot confirm; the inspection-first read for every write op.

tools.name: mesh_list
tools.parity: net-new (wraps existing mesh_list_dynamic; Roblox get_descendants is closest)
tools.signature: (label_contains?, include_static?, limit?, offset?) -> {meshes:[{actor_label, component, triangles, vertices, num_materials, empty}], count, total_triangles, has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: Enumerate every UDynamicMeshComponent (and optionally StaticMeshActors) in the level with tri/vert/material counts; the discovery read for batch ops and PCG/grammar output inspection.

tools.name: staticmesh_brief
tools.parity: net-new moat (deepest single-asset readback in any UE MCP)
tools.signature: (asset_path) -> {lods:[{index, triangles, screen_size, reduction}], nanite:{enabled, settings}, collision:{simple_prims, complex_as_simple, convex_count}, uv_channels, lightmap_index, lightmap_resolution, material_slots:[{slot, material_path}], bounds, nanite_fallback_pct}
tools.description: Asset-level readback for a UStaticMesh: LOD count + screen sizes, Nanite enabled/settings, collision setup, UV channel count + lightmap UV index/resolution, material slots, bounds; the inspection-first read before any asset authoring op.

tools.name: mesh_validate
tools.parity: net-new moat (PLUMB quantified validation; beyond Flop auto-repair / Houdini graph-intelligence)
tools.signature: (actor_label?|asset_path?, require_closed?, require_single_component?, max_boundary_edges?, profile?) -> {pass, checks:[{rule, value, threshold, pass}], unsat_core:[], plumb_profile?}
tools.description: Topology health verdict: runs mesh_extract stats then routes through PLUMB to return green/red with an unsat-core (which check failed: non-manifold, inverted winding, open boundary, degenerate, multi-component); the validate-before/after-mutate gate.

tools.name: geo_pipeline
tools.parity: net-new moat (no UE MCP composes/validates a mesh op chain)
tools.signature: (source:{actor_label|asset_path|primitive}, ops:[{op, params}], dest:{actor_label|new_asset_path}, dry_run?, validate?) -> {ok, ops_applied, before_stats, after_stats, validate?, dest_path}
tools.description: Run an ordered list of GeometryScript ops source->dest in ONE python_run call (no cross-call handle GC risk); the P0 vehicle for composed procedural-mesh authoring with one transaction and a final validate.

tools.name: geo_dry_run
tools.parity: net-new moat (only Flop bp_dry_run is analogous, not for meshes)
tools.signature: (source, ops:[{op, params}]) -> {predicted_stats, predicted_validate, delta:{tris, verts, components}, warnings:[]}
tools.description: Preview a geo_pipeline: apply ops to a transient mesh and return predicted topology stats WITHOUT writing any asset or component; generalizes the dry_run->commit pattern beyond world_generate.

tools.name: geo_bake_to_staticmesh
tools.parity: net-new (Blender import-after-gen is closest; none bake DynamicMesh->StaticMesh)
tools.signature: (source:{actor_label|primitive|pipeline}, dest_asset_path, nanite?, collision?, generate_lightmap_uvs?, recompute_normals?, overwrite?, dry_run?) -> {ok, asset_path, counts, topology, overwrote}
tools.description: Commit a transient/dynamic mesh to a new or overwritten UStaticMesh asset (CopyMeshToStaticMesh) with Nanite/collision/lightmap/material options; the deliverable that turns procedural geometry into a usable asset.

tools.name: geo_apply_to_actor
tools.parity: parity with Aura live BP edit (mesh equivalent)
tools.description: Write a transient/edited mesh back onto an actor's UDynamicMeshComponent for live preview without baking an asset; the fast iterate loop, transaction-wrapped for undo.

tools.name: geo_primitive_new
tools.description: Generate a parametric primitive DynamicMesh (box/sphere/cylinder/cone/torus/disc/stairs/grid) as a pipeline source; the cheapest content-creation entry point.

tools.name: geo_from_asset
tools.description: Load a UStaticMesh (chosen LOD) into a transient DynamicMesh as a pipeline source for editing; the read side of asset->edit->rebake.

tools.name: geo_from_actor
tools.description: Copy an actor's static or dynamic mesh into a transient DynamicMesh source (world or local space) for non-destructive editing.

tools.name: geo_boolean
tools.signature: (source_a, source_b, operation:Literal[union,subtract,intersect], dest?, validate?, dry_run?) -> {ok, after_stats, validate}
tools.description: CSG union/subtract/intersect between two mesh sources (or a source and a primitive); the workhorse hard-surface op, with mandatory post-op manifold check.

tools.name: geo_transform
tools.signature: (source, translate?, rotate?, scale?, pivot?, selection?, dest?) -> {ok, bounds}
tools.description: Translate/rotate/scale/uniform-scale a mesh or a sub-selection of triangles (by group/material/bbox); pivot-aware geometry transform distinct from actor transform.

tools.name: geo_remesh
tools.signature: (source, target_edge_length?|target_tri_count?, iterations?, preserve_uvs?, dest?, validate?) -> {ok, after_stats}
tools.description: Uniform/adaptive remesh to a target edge length or triangle budget while preserving boundaries/UV seams; clean topology before simplify or for even shading.

tools.name: geo_simplify
tools.signature: (source, target:{tri_count|percent|tolerance}, preserve_boundary?, dest?, validate?) -> {ok, before_tris, after_tris, max_deviation}
tools.description: Decimate a mesh to a target tri count / percentage / geometric tolerance; the LOD-prep and budget-fit op, validated against a deviation threshold.

tools.name: geo_normals_recompute
tools.description: Recompute per-vertex/per-face normals and tangents with hard/soft edges by angle threshold or polygroup; fixes the most common shading artifact after edits.

tools.name: geo_uv_project
tools.parity: net-new moat (PLUMB Box-UV node already shipped; productized as a tool)
tools.signature: (source, mode:Literal[planar,box,cylinder,sphere], uv_channel?, world_space?, tile_size?, selection?, dest?) -> {ok, uv_channel, bounds_uv}
tools.description: Planar/box/cylinder/sphere UV projection onto a channel; the deterministic UV op, reuses the shipped PLUMB Box-UV world-space grid logic for swept/bonded shells.

tools.name: geo_weld
tools.signature: (source, tolerance?, fix_winding?, dest?, validate?) -> {ok, merged_verts, after_stats}
tools.description: Merge coincident vertices within a tolerance and optionally fix winding; the cleanup that turns PCG/boolean output from non-manifold to manifold.

tools.name: geo_fill_holes
tools.signature: (source, method:Literal[minimal,flat,smooth], max_hole_edges?, dest?, validate?) -> {ok, holes_filled, remaining_boundary_loops}
tools.description: Close open boundary loops (flat/smooth/minimal fill) to make a shell watertight; required before voxel/Nanite/collision on PCG grammar shells.

tools.name: geo_extrude
tools.signature: (source, distance, direction?:Literal[normal,vector], vector?, selection?, solidify?, dest?) -> {ok, after_stats}
tools.description: Extrude whole mesh or a face/group selection along normals or a vector (with shell thickness); core hard-surface modeling op for swept profiles.

tools.name: geo_sweep_revolve
tools.signature: (profile:{points|primitive}, mode:Literal[sweep,revolve], path?:{spline_actor|points}, axis?, steps?, cap_ends?, dest?, validate?) -> {ok, after_stats}
tools.description: Sweep a 2D profile along a spline/path or revolve it around an axis to generate shells; the PLUMB swept/bonded-shell worldbuilding generator productized.

tools.name: geo_mirror
tools.signature: (source, plane:Literal[x,y,z,custom], plane_origin?, plane_normal?, weld_seam?, dest?) -> {ok, after_stats}
tools.description: Mirror a mesh across a plane with optional weld-on-seam; symmetry authoring without manual duplicate+flip.

tools.name: geo_displace
tools.signature: (source, mode:Literal[perlin,texture,normal], intensity, frequency?, texture_path?, mask?, dest?) -> {ok, max_displacement}
tools.description: Displace vertices by Perlin/texture/normal-direction with a mask; adds surface detail to terrain/rock/organic shells procedurally.

tools.name: geo_voxel
tools.signature: (source, operation:Literal[remesh,offset,close,open], voxel_size, offset_distance?, dest?, validate?) -> {ok, after_stats, watertight}
tools.description: Voxel/morphological remesh (offset, close, open, mesh-to-watertight) to guarantee a manifold closed solid; the robust repair path for messy boolean/PCG output.

tools.name: geo_subdivide
tools.description: PN/Loop/Catmull-Clark subdivision to a level; smooths low-poly cages for organic forms.

tools.name: geo_smooth
tools.description: Laplacian/Taubin smoothing with iterations and boundary preservation; denoise scanned or displaced meshes.

tools.name: geo_uv_unwrap
tools.signature: (source, method:Literal[patch_builder,xatlas], uv_channel?, island_padding?, resolution?, dest?) -> {ok, island_count, packing_efficiency}
tools.description: Auto-unwrap UVs via PatchBuilder/XAtlas with island packing; full UV generation for textured assets (slow/nondeterministic, capped tri count).

tools.name: staticmesh_set_nanite
tools.signature: (asset_path, enabled, fallback_percent?, relative_error?, position_precision?, dry_run?) -> {ok, nanite_settings, fallback_tris}
tools.description: Enable/disable Nanite and set fallback/relative-error/position-precision on a UStaticMesh, then build; the single easiest high-value asset win.

tools.name: staticmesh_generate_lods
tools.signature: (asset_path, num_lods, reduction_percents?, screen_sizes?, dry_run?) -> {ok, lods:[{index, triangles, screen_size}]}
tools.description: Auto-generate reduction LODs (count, per-LOD percent/screen-size) on a UStaticMesh; performance authoring without the editor LOD UI.

tools.name: staticmesh_collision_set
tools.description: Set simple collision (box/sphere/capsule/convex-decomposition via Chaos) or complex-as-simple on a UStaticMesh; gameplay-ready geometry.

tools.name: staticmesh_setup_lightmap
tools.signature: (asset_path, lightmap_index?, resolution?, generate_uvs?, source_uv?, dry_run?) -> {ok, lightmap_index, resolution}
tools.description: Generate lightmap UVs into a channel and set lightmap UV index + resolution; fixes baked-lighting artifacts on procedural assets.

tools.name: staticmesh_socket_add
tools.signature: (asset_path, action:Literal[add,list,remove], socket_name?, location?, rotation?, scale?, tag?) -> {ok, sockets:[{name, transform, tag}]}
tools.description: Add/list named sockets (transform + tag) on a UStaticMesh for attachment; reuses the PLUMB socket grammar so generated shells expose bind points.

tools.name: staticmesh_assign_material
tools.description: Set/swap material on a slot index (or all slots) of a UStaticMesh or per-instance on an actor; closes the texture/material loop after baking geometry.

tools.name: mesh_batch_apply
tools.parity: parity Roblox mass_set_property/Unity batch wiring (net-new for meshes)
tools.signature: (targets:{selection|class|tag|label_contains}, ops:[{op, params}], dest_mode:Literal[in_place,new_assets], dry_run?, validate_each?) -> {applied, failed, results:[{target, ok, after_stats, validate}], has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: Apply a geo op (or short pipeline) across many actors/assets selected by query/class/tag, returning per-target verdicts; outcome-verb batch op for grammar/PCG output cleanup.

tools.name: mesh_compare
tools.parity: net-new moat (no UE MCP diffs geometry)
tools.signature: (source_a, source_b, sample_count?) -> {hausdorff, mean_deviation, tri_delta, vert_delta, volume_delta, area_delta, topology_delta}

domains.summary: The graph-authoring half of materials is already strong (~20 first-class tools), but the author LOOP is missing: no way to read back what parameters/static-switches/nodes a material exposes, no batch/multi-select, no slot-aware apply (current material_apply touches only a single StaticMeshComponent), no texture import/export/channel-pack, no Material Parameter Collections, and no visual verify. This adds ~34 tools on those gaps, almost all python_run-backed pyTemplate descriptors (zero plugin rebuild) per the "no rebuild by default" rule, reserving C++ only for hot-path pixel work. It leans on three moats: PLUMB-style convention validation (texture_audit / fix_settings_by_convention enforce correct sRGB-on-normals and compression discipline), the vision loop (material_thumbnail / preview_on_mesh return PNG content blocks), and dry-run/inspection-first safety (every write domain ships a paired *_inspect read and a dry-run batch planner). Every mutation is paginated, flat-arg, and routed through the hardened python_run handler so it is schema-validated, journaled, and transaction-wrappable without per-tool 7-file churn.
dependencies: UE Editor Scripting: unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary (get/set_*_parameter_value, get_*_parameter_names) for instance param read/write
unreal.MaterialInstanceConstant + MaterialInstanceEditorLibrary for static switches, reparent, override clearing
unreal.AssetImportTask / AssetToolsHelpers / InterchangeManager for texture_import(_batch)/reimport
unreal.EditorAssetLibrary (duplicate_asset, save_asset, find_package_referencers) + AssetRegistryHelpers for find_references / forward deps
unreal.RenderingLibrary.draw_material_to_render_target + TextureRenderTarget2D + export_render_target for channel-pack, preview_on_mesh, texture_export
unreal.MaterialParameterCollection(+Instance) APIs for the mpc_* tools

Existing infra: tool-executor.executeCommand + hardened python_run handler (SEH + 3-tier security gate) as the pyTemplate dispatch vehicle (Theme 1 #4); schema-registry + ToolDescriptor pipeline (Section 5)
Vision: render_camera / editor_capture_viewport / SceneCapture world-pos spike for material_thumbnail + preview_on_mesh
C++ HaybaMCPTextureHandler / HaybaMCPMaterialHandler for the 2 hot-path readback tools (pixel histogram, instruction-count analyze) if Python proves too slow
PLUMB validator (validator_run / plumb_validate, convention/constraint language) for texture_audit + material_audit + fix_settings_by_convention rule sourcing
risks: UE Python material-graph node enumeration is shallow: MaterialEditingLibrary has no first-class 'get all expressions with connections' call. material_node_list may need MaterialEditingLibrary internals or to extend the existing C++ material_get_info, not pure Python.

Static-switch changes (material_set_static_switch) trigger full shader recompiles, which can stall the game thread; must go through the deferred-compile/auto-save pattern (PR #250) and never inline-recompile inside the python_run call.

texture_channel_pack via draw_material_to_render_target needs a helper pack material asset to exist; if absent the tool must create/ship one. GPU read-back to save as Texture2D (CreateStaticTexture from RT) can lose precision on HDR sources.
texture_import through Interchange vs legacy AssetImportTask differs across 5.7/5.8; pinning to one path risks version drift (Theme 6).

material_thumbnail / preview_on_mesh must NOT sync-capture the live world (known crash); must show-only-list the preview mesh, pre-warm shaders, split into short calls (memory: scenecapture isolate-mesh).
Reverse-reference lookups (find_references) over a large project can be slow and must paginate + use AssetRegistry, not a filesystem scan.
Bulk writes (batch_set_param, apply_to_selection) without a transaction wrap leave half-applied state on failure; depends on the Theme 4C transaction seam landing to be a single Ctrl+Z.

Reading raw texture pixels (audit non-pow2/oversize is fine from metadata, but histogram/pixel-sample needs source-art or platform data) is unreliable on cooked/streamed textures; flag as best-effort.
domains.test_plan: On a live editor with the HaybaMCP plugin loaded and a small content folder (a base material with scalar+vector+texture+static-switch params, a few MICs, and a /Game/Tex folder of PNG/TGA with _D/_N/_ORM suffixes): (1) Inspection-first: material_param_list + material_instance_inspect on a known MIC and assert returned param names/defaults match the editor's MI editor; material_node_list against the base material vs the editor graph. (2) Round-trip: material_set_params_bulk then material_param_list to confirm overrides; material_param_reset and confirm values fall back to parent default. (3) Static switch: material_set_static_switch, wait_for_shaders, then render_camera/material_thumbnail to confirm the branch visibly changed. (4) Batch: spawn N actors, material_apply_to_selection + material_apply_batch by tag, then verify each component slot via material_instance_inspect; texture_batch_set_settings + texture_fix_settings_by_convention(dry_run=true) and confirm the plan flags the wrong-sRGB normal map before committing. (5) Import: texture_import a PNG, texture_get_info to confirm settings; texture_channel_pack three grayscale maps into an ORM and texture_export it to disk for eyeball check. (6) MPC: mpc_create, mpc_set a global scalar, confirm a material reading the MPC changes via material_thumbnail before/after diff. (7) Safety: run every mutating tool once with dry_run=true and assert no asset is dirtied (EditorAssetLibrary.do_assets_exist / package dirty flag), then commit and confirm a single undo reverts. (8) Audit: texture_audit + material_audit over the folder and assert violation counts match seeded bad assets. Validate visually, not just metric counts.

domains.summary: The current PCG/PCGEx surface (~17 first-class tools) covers JSON-graph build/validate/export plus four reflection primitives (add_node/set_prop/wire/inspect_instances) and the async-safe pcg_cook_and_wait — but it has glaring authoring holes: no node/edge delete, no live topology read-back, no class enumeration, no way to instantiate a PCGComponent on an actor, no attribute-data debug readback, no dry-run, no cleanup, and no asset-level undo. Strategy: lean on python_run-backed pyTemplate wrappers (zero plugin rebuild) to fill the full author→cook→inspect→verify loop, and press the worldbuilding moat with PLUMB-validated graph linting, recipe instantiation from the sliver library, and a cook+auto-frame+screenshot vision loop that no competitor has for PCG. Every write tool ships a paired live read/inspect tool (Flop pattern), wraps mutations in a graph-asset snapshot (FScopedTransaction can't capture python asset edits), and routes through validate-before/after. Reserve C++ only for a hot-path declarative cook-stats probe if python proves too slow; everything else stays no-rebuild.
dependencies: pcg-primitives.ts PY_RESOLVE_NODE/_load_graph/_node_label/_resolve_node shared helpers (UE 5.7 verified: graph.nodes, node.node_title, pin.properties.label)
Hardened python_run handler (SEH + dangling-delegate gate #283/#284) — all pyTemplate tools route through it; never open TCP from inside python_run
wait_for_idle with subsystems:['pcg'] + pcg_actors for async cook settling (pcg_cook_and_wait already depends on it)
Theme-1 add-a-tool refactor: descriptors + pyTemplate factory (Section 5 #4) so these ~33 tools land as data, no per-tool 4-file churn
PLUMB validator (plumb_validate, validator_run) for lint / validate_before_after / spawn_and_scatter green-red gating
Sliver registry + scatter/pcg_biome.ts for pcg_recipe_apply; existing catalog.ts + pcgex docs sqlite DB for describe/list fallbacks
Vision tools editor_capture_viewport / render_camera for preview_capture / seed_sweep
Memory fact: SurfaceSampler needs a REAL imported Landscape (landscape_import handler), not the LandscapePlaceholder spawn stub — recipes/spawn_and_scatter must target a real Landscape
Transaction/snapshot relies on EditorAssetLibrary.duplicate_asset (asset-level), NOT FScopedTransaction, which cannot capture python asset edits
risks: PCG Python reflection is unstable across UE versions: add_node_of_type returns a tuple, node_title is often empty/'None', and edge APIs (add_edge/remove_edge) vary — tools must probe-and-fallback like existing primitives and be re-verified on engine bumps
PCGComponent.generate is async; any readback (attribute_readback, pcgex_cluster_inspect, instance counts) must go through wait_for_idle or it reads stale/zero same-frame
Generated PCG point/attribute data is transient (not persisted): attribute_readback/cluster_inspect only work right after a cook while data is resident; cleared by pcg_clear_generated or GC
Partitioned/runtime-generated PCG needs World Partition cells loaded; counts and readback are unreliable on unloaded cells — flag partitioned state in component_inspect
PCGEx classes only exist if the PcgEx plugin is installed; pcgex_* tools and node_list_classes must degrade gracefully (installed=false) rather than throw
Heavy cooks can exceed executor timeouts and (pre-Theme-0 fix) freeze the game thread — keep dry_run/estimate as the default preview, gate generate_all behind explicit confirm + job-envelope timeouts
cook_dry_run point estimates are approximate (sampler density math, not a real cook) — must be labelled estimate to avoid false confidence
Snapshot via asset duplication can clutter content if not GC'd — restore should clean the backup; namespace snapshots under /Game/_pcg_snapshots/
domains.test_plan: On a live UE 5.7 editor with PCG + PCGExtendedToolkit plugins and a REAL imported Landscape (not the placeholder stub): 1) pcg_node_list_classes(filter='Sampler') confirms PCGSurfaceSamplerSettings + PCGEx classes enumerate. 2) pcg_recipe_apply('scatter', name='T_Scatter', {mesh, density:0.5, seed:1337}) builds an asset; pcg_graph_inspect round-trips the same nodes/edges; pcg_graph_lint reports 0 errors. 3) pcg_snapshot the asset, then pcg_remove_node + pcg_unwire + pcg_set_props_batch, re-inspect to confirm deltas, then pcg_restore and confirm the graph matches the snapshot. 4) Spawn a volume over the Landscape via pcg_component_bind (or pcg_spawn_and_scatter), pcg_cook_dry_run gives a point estimate, then cook_and_wait and confirm instance total is non-zero and within ~order of the estimate. 5) pcg_attribute_readback returns position/density samples; pcg_component_inspect shows bound graph + last_cook stats. 6) pcg_preview_capture returns front/top/iso PNGs that visibly show scattered meshes on terrain (validate visually, not just counts — per memory). 7) pcg_seed_sweep over 4 seeds shows 4 visibly different scatters. 8) pcg_components_generate_all(scope='by_graph') re-cooks all bound actors. 9) Negative paths: bind a graph with an unconnected required pin -> pcg_graph_lint flags it with a fix; pcgex_cluster_inspect on a non-PCGEx output returns a clean 'no cluster data' rather than throwing. Cross-check hayba_journal_tail shows no SEH catches or dangling-delegate blocks during the run.

domains.summary: Today the domain is a single tool (hayba_import_landscape → C++ Cmd_ImportLandscape in HaybaMCPLandscapeImporter.cpp); the brief targets ~10, and competitors (Epic 5.8, Aura, GenOrca 253, Flop) have essentially zero real landscape sculpt/paint depth — this is open ground for a net-new moat. Strategy: (1) make the existing import path honest and inspectable first (list/inspect/validate/dry-run read tools — Flop inspection-first), (2) lean the flagship into a Gaea→UE bridge (the repo already carries a deep Gaea transcript+docs corpus that no rival has) so landscape_import_gaea_build ingests heightmap+named masks+material in ONE undo, (3) reserve C++ (a new HaybaMCPLandscapeHandler over FLandscapeEditDataInterface) only for the operations UE Python genuinely cannot do — height/weight data edits, multi-step single-Ctrl+Z transactions, and buffer-viz/export readback — while doing material/layer-info/Nanite/grass setup as no-rebuild python_run wrappers. Every write tool pairs with a read/verify tool, transaction-wraps, dry-runs, and round-trips through PLUMB/validator + the vision loop (top-down auto-frame + slope/height buffer-viz + before/after diff). This wins on the moats (crash-resilience, transactional one-undo, quantified validation, vision feedback, worldbuilding depth) rather than raw count, while still out-tooling every competitor in this specific subsystem.
dependencies: Theme 0 gate: build_*/test_* job-envelope conversion and SEH-wrap of ProcessCommand must land before any landscape build/rebuild tool ships unattended (landscape_build_data, enable_nanite trigger game-thread builds that freeze today)
Theme 1 gate: add-a-tool descriptor refactor + pyTemplate factory — most python tools here ship as descriptors with zero rebuild only after this lands
Existing C++: HaybaMCPLandscapeImporter.cpp (Cmd_ImportLandscape) — extend, do not fork

New C++ module HaybaMCPLandscapeHandler.cpp wrapping FLandscapeEditDataInterface (engine module: Landscape, LandscapeEditor) for all height/weight data edits — requires plugin rebuild + EngineVersion gating; flag as non-marketplace (engine-private headers)
Game-thread marshal seam HaybaGameThread::RunSync (PR #254) — every landscape edit is game-thread-only (check IsInGameThread already enforced in importer)
World Partition: ALandscapeStreamingProxy enumeration + force-load of all loaded-region proxies before any data edit
PLUMB validator + validator_run hooks for landscape_validate; vision loop (render_camera/editor_capture_viewport) for capture/dry-run
Gaea knowledge corpus already in repo (src/gaea/transcripts + knowledge/gaea-docs) — source of mask-name → layer-name conventions for the Gaea bridge
1MB TCP frame cap — heightmap/weightmap blobs must transfer as file paths or be chunked, never inline base64
risks: UE Python landscape API is thin: heightmap/weightmap pixel edits, layer-info creation in-material, and sculpt brushes are effectively C++-only (FLandscapeEditDataInterface). Realistically ~12 of these need a plugin rebuild, which conflicts with 'no-rebuild-by-default' — sequence them behind the new C++ handler and clearly tag which are python vs C++.

World Partition landscapes are split into streaming proxies; editing only loaded proxies silently corrupts/partial-edits the rest (echoes the 2026-05-23 PCG/landscape postmortem: success:true is NOT proof). Every edit tool must enumerate + force-load proxies and report coverage, or refuse.

FLandscapeImportHelper caps ~8193/side and ChooseBestComponentSizeForImport can yield degenerate sizes — dry-run must surface the chosen component layout BEFORE mutate (importer already rejects out-of-range).
Nanite-landscape enable and grass/data rebuilds run synchronous game-thread builds → the Theme-0 freeze bug; must go through the job-envelope or they hang the editor.
Large weightmap/heightmap transfer exceeds the 1MB frame cap — must pass file paths, not inline pixels.
Gaea bridge depends on mask-filename → layer-name conventions; ambiguous/unknown masks must fail loud with a mapping report, not guess (honesty invariant).
Auto-paint-by-slope/altitude can overwrite hand-painted weights — must be transaction-wrapped, dry-runnable, and mask-aware so it never silently destroys existing work.
Spline/deformation and resize ops are heavy and can desync collision/Nanite — gate behind Plan-Mode + validate-after.
domains.test_plan: Live-editor validation on a blank UE 5.7 map plus a World-Partition map: (1) Read path first — landscape_list on empty map returns []; spawn via landscape_import_heightmap with a known 1009x1009 R16, then landscape_inspect must report matching SizeX/SizeY, section/quad/component counts, scale, bounds, min/max height that agree with the importer log. (2) Round-trip — landscape_export_heightmap then re-import into a second actor and diff; pixel delta must be ~0 (proves readback fidelity). (3) Gaea bridge — point landscape_import_gaea_build at a real Gaea export folder (height R16 + Rock/Soil/Snow mask PNGs + material); assert landscape spawned, 3 LayerInfo assets created+assigned, weightmaps non-zero (export each + check histograms), and the whole thing is ONE Ctrl+Z (transaction bundle). (4) Sculpt/paint — landscape_sculpt_flatten a rect then inspect min/max in that region == target Z; landscape_paint_by_rule rock-on-slope then export rock weightmap and confirm weight correlates with slope buffer. (5) Vision — landscape_capture_topdown returns MIME image content blocks for height + slope buffer-viz + before/after diff around a sculpt op. (6) Dry-run — landscape_dry_run on an oversized heightmap returns predicted layout + warning and mutates nothing (landscape_list unchanged). (7) Safety — landscape_validate flags an intentionally introduced hole / out-of-range height / weights-not-summing-to-1; undo after a transaction bundle restores the prior inspect snapshot exactly. (8) WP coverage — on a streaming-proxy map, run a region edit with only some proxies loaded and confirm the tool either force-loads all or refuses with a coverage report. (9) No-freeze — landscape_enable_nanite + landscape_build_data return via job-envelope without blocking the game thread past the executor ceiling.

domains.summary: The existing C++ FoliageHandler advertises 4 commands but two of them (foliage_add_instance, foliage_paint_at) are silent stubs that return success without persisting anything — a direct honesty-invariant violation. The strategy is to re-platform the whole domain on python_run-backed pyTemplate descriptors using the working `unreal.FoliageEditorLibrary` / `InstancedFoliageActor` / `ProceduralFoliageComponent` / HISM APIs, fixing the false-advertised tools with zero plugin rebuild. We out-tool every competitor by shipping a single reusable scatter sampling engine (ground-trace, slope/altitude/mask filters, Poisson relaxation, deterministic seeds) exposed as outcome-verbs, paired with inspection/read-back, dry-run preview, transaction-wrapped mutation, and PLUMB density-constraint validation — none of which Epic, Aura, Flop, or GenOrca offer for foliage. Every write tool is chunked into job-envelope-friendly batches so large scatters never freeze the game thread, and verification closes through a top-down density heatmap and before/after vision capture. Net-new moats: quantified density/spacing validation, reproducible scatter manifests, and terrain-reconform after sculpt edits.
dependencies: Theme 1 add-a-tool refactor + pyTemplate factory (descriptors are the authoring surface; no per-tool 7-file churn)
Hardened python_run handler (SEH + security gate + chunked execution to avoid game-thread freeze)
Theme 0 job-envelope conversion for long scatters/proc-foliage resimulate (>2s) so build/test-style freezes don't recur
4C transaction/undo C++ wrappers (FScopedTransaction) so foliage mutations are one-Ctrl+Z and dry_run->commit generalizes
4D selection/batch primitives (EditorActorSubsystem) for instance/actor batch ops
asset-retriever (hayba_asset_search) to discover candidate foliage StaticMeshes/FoliageTypes by tag
A real Landscape or collision geometry to ground-trace against (memory: SurfaceSampler/paint silently no-op without it)
PLUMB constraint engine (plumb_constraint_define/validate) for density/spacing rules
Vision loop (render_camera / editor_capture_viewport) for heatmap + before/after diff
DAG/journal for recording scatter ops into reproducible manifests
risks: The shipped C++ foliage_add_instance/foliage_paint_at return success but persist nothing — must be fixed or flagged not-callable before any new tool ships (honesty invariant)
Adding thousands of instances on the game thread freezes the editor; all scatter tools MUST chunk transforms and route through the job-envelope, with instance-count caps + paginated commits

FoliageEditorLibrary.add_instances operates on the editor world and needs collision/landscape to ground-trace; on an empty level scatter silently yields 0 (must return an actionable error, not success)
Procedural foliage resimulate() is heavy and synchronous — must be async/job-enveloped or it reproduces the build_* 300s freeze
Dry-run==commit requires deterministic RNG; without a seed registry preview won't match the baked result
Non-deterministic FMath::RandRange in the legacy C++ paint means previews can't be reproduced — seed must be threaded through python
UE Python foliage bindings vary across 5.7/5.8; coarse capability probe (get_*_status) needed for graceful degradation across pinned EngineVersion
Converting many StaticMeshActors to foliage (and back) is destructive and can orphan references — must be transaction-wrapped + dry-run first
Heatmap/orbit capture must isolate the target meshes and pre-warm shaders (memory: never sync-capture the live world)
domains.test_plan: Live editor with a Landscape (or collision-enabled ground) plus 3-4 imported SM_ foliage meshes. 1) hayba_check_ue_status + foliage_capability_probe to confirm Python foliage bindings. 2) foliage_type_create from each mesh; foliage_type_set_params (density, scale 0.8-1.4, align_to_normal, cull 0/8000); foliage_type_inspect to read back params. 3) foliage_scatter_dry_run over a 50m box at density 0.2 -> confirm returned count + sample transforms + heatmap PNG; then foliage_scatter_paint with the SAME seed -> assert committed count == dry-run count (determinism). 4) foliage_inspect / foliage_list_types -> confirm per-type counts match; foliage_stats_by_region grid buckets non-empty over the landscape, zero outside. 5) Ctrl+Z (or transaction undo) -> foliage_inspect shows counts revert to 0 (proves real persistence + transaction wrapping, i.e. the stub bug is fixed). 6) foliage_scatter_by_slope_altitude (slope 0-20deg) -> verify no instances on cliffs via foliage_density_heatmap. 7) foliage_remove_in_bounds on a sub-box -> count drops by the bounded amount only. 8) foliage_relax min-distance 150 -> remove_overlapping_count>0 and nearest-neighbor histogram tightens. 9) Sculpt the landscape, run foliage_align_to_terrain -> re-traced instances sit on new surface (before/after capture). 10) proc_foliage_volume_create + add_type + resimulate -> instances baked, job returns without freezing (watch editor_stream_log). 11) ism_actor_create + ism_scatter -> HISM instance count via foliage/ism inspect. 12) foliage_validate_density with a PLUMB constraint (min spacing 100, max 0.3/m^2) -> green pass, then over-scatter -> red unsat-core surfaced. 13) foliage_export_manifest then re-import on a fresh level -> identical scatter (reproducibility).

domains.summary: Blueprint K2 graph authoring is the single largest false-advertised capability: blueprint_add_node, blueprint_connect_nodes, and blueprint_add_event all return not_implemented_in_v1, while create/add_variable/add_function/compile/set_defaults already work in HaybaMCPBlueprintHandler.cpp. Strategy: (1) honestly implement the three stubbed K2 verbs in C++ on the EdGraph/EdGraphSchema_K2 plumbing the handler already imports; (2) ship the unglamorous read/verify surface (graph_inspect, node_brief, get_pin, find_nodes, reflection search for function/class/pin-type refs) so an agent can author then verify, closing the postmortem's "no UE reflection-introspection tool" gap; (3) productize the moats with a declarative blueprint_build_graph batch landing as ONE transaction/undo plus dry-run and PLUMB validate before/after, beating Epic's per-call undo and matching Flop's bp_dry_run. Reflection/search/diff helpers are python_run-backed (no rebuild); node mutation must be C++ because UE Python cannot reliably spawn/wire K2 nodes. Every write verb returns a compile report and respects the existing broken-blueprint compile-gate so the agent self-corrects.
dependencies: Existing C++ HaybaMCPBlueprintHandler.cpp (Create/AddComponent/AddVariable/AddFunction/Compile/SetDefaults working; RecompileAndTrack + BrokenBlueprintsRef compile-gate; AttachCompileReport)
Theme 0 gate: SEH-wrap ProcessCommand so the new C++ K2 handlers are crash-recoverable (graph mutation is crash-prone)
Theme 1 gate: add-a-tool refactor (single ToolDescriptor + pyTemplate factory) so the ~14 python-backed wrappers ship without 7-file churn
Transaction subsystem (Theme 4C) FScopedTransaction seam for build_graph one-undo bundling and tx_begin/commit/rollback
PLUMB validator (plumb_validate / validator_run) for blueprint_validate before/after-mutate
python_run hardened handler (SEH + security gate) for reflection/search/diff pyTemplate tools
tool-executor.ts executeCommand passthrough + schema-registry.ts + legacy sidecar.json regen for the new C++ commands
Plan-Mode gate (bPlanApproved) honored before destructive verbs (delete_node/delete_variable/build_graph commit)
risks: UE Python genuinely CANNOT spawn/wire arbitrary K2 nodes reliably; the core add_node/connect/event verbs MUST be C++ (a plugin rebuild) - do not pretend pyTemplate covers them or we repeat the not_implemented_in_v1 dishonesty
Stable node identity across calls: EdGraphNode pointers are not serializable IDs; must mint a stable node_id (NodeGuid string) and resolve back, or graph edits silently target the wrong node
K2 schema validation (CanCreateConnection) can reject a wire for type/exec-vs-data reasons; must surface the schema's rejection reason, not a generic failure
Compile after every node edit is slow on large BPs; build_graph must mutate-then-compile-ONCE, and per-node verbs should offer compile=false to defer
Function-ref resolution: a wrong UFunction/class name produces a silently orphaned call node; reflection search (blueprint_search_functions) must return the exact ref add_node consumes
Editor-only headers (EdGraphSchema_K2, BlueprintEditorUtils) keep the plugin non-shippable at runtime - already an accepted constraint but widens the editor-only surface
Re-entrancy: all K2 mutation must run on the game thread via the RunSync seam; AsyncTask+Wait inside a handler self-deadlocks (known MEMORY hazard)
domains.test_plan: On a live 5.7 editor with the plugin loaded: (1) blueprint_create a child of Actor at /Game/MCPTest/BP_T; (2) blueprint_search_functions(target='Actor', query='SetActorLocation') to get the function ref; (3) blueprint_add_event(BeginPlay) -> capture node_id; (4) blueprint_add_node(call_function, ref=SetActorLocation) and blueprint_add_node(variable_get) -> capture ids; (5) blueprint_connect_nodes wiring BeginPlay exec->SetActorLocation exec and the vector pin; (6) blueprint_get_pin / blueprint_node_brief to VERIFY the link landed and types matched; (7) blueprint_graph_inspect (paginated) to confirm node/link counts; (8) blueprint_validate then blueprint_compile -> expect compiled_clean=true, error_count=0; (9) editor_capture_viewport / render the BP graph editor for a visual before/after diff; (10) blueprint_build_graph with the same spec in dry_run=true (expect a plan, no mutation), then commit, then a SINGLE editor Ctrl+Z and re-inspect to prove one-undo atomicity; (11) negative: connect two incompatible pins -> expect a schema rejection reason, and mutate a broken BP -> expect bp_compile_required gate. Cross-check every node_id round-trips via find_nodes.

domains.summary:
There is already a HaybaMCPSequencer C++ plugin exposing 8 seq_* commands (create, add_track, add_keyframe [float-only], get_info, play, add_camera_cut, set_playback_range, and a stubbed seq_export that returns an error = a Section-3 honesty violation). None have first-class TS wrappers, so they are reachable only via hayba_invoke/python_run today. Strategy is three-layered: (1) Theme-2 thin TS wrappers over the 8 existing C++ commands plus paired inspect/list read tools; (2) Theme-3 python_run-backed authoring the C++ layer cannot do without a rebuild (transform/rotation/scale keyframing, spawnables, audio/fade/event/sub-sequence tracks, cine-camera outcome verbs, and the headline moat: a MovieRenderQueue render path returned as an async job-envelope so we are the only local UE MCP that renders finished movies and feeds stills/contact-sheets back as image content blocks); (3) cross-cutting safety: a PLUMB-style seq_validate, dry-run + one-Ctrl+Z transaction bundling, and full read-back on every write. Render MUST be a job-envelope, never a blocking game-thread call, to respect the Theme-0 freeze fix.</parameter>
<parameter name="dependencies">["Existing HaybaMCPSequencer C++ plugin (domain seq); seq_export stub must be removed from catalog per honesty invariant and superseded by seq_render_movie","Theme-0 job-envelope conversion (docs/audit/2026-06-22-mcp-async-command-conversions.md) for render tools","Hardened python_run handler (SEH + security gate) as the dispatch path for non-C++ tools","MovieRenderQueue/MoviePipeline plugin enabled in project; gate with status probe and degrade gracefully if absent","Vision-loop infra (render_camera/editor_capture_viewport + image content-block return) for seq_render_still/thumbnail_strip","PLUMB validator seam for seq_validate; Plan-Mode gate + FScopedTransaction seam (4C) for destructive ops and seq_transaction","unreal Python: LevelSequenceEditorBlueprintLibrary, MovieSceneScripting channels, SequencerTools, EditorAssetLibrary, EditorActorSubsystem","Theme-1 add-a-tool refactor: ship python wrappers as pyTemplate descriptors not 7-file hand-rolls"]
risks: MovieRenderQueue blocks the game thread if synchronous (same class as the two P0 freeze bugs); seq_render_* MUST be async job-envelope or it re-introduces editor freeze
C++ seq_add_keyframe only handles float tracks; transform/rotation/scale/focus keyframing is python-only and may be flaky across 5.7/5.8, needing version-guarded codepaths
BindPossessableObject dereferences the editor world; binding tools crash with no level loaded unless the python wrapper replicates the existing C++ null-world guard
MRQ requires the MoviePipeline plugin and an output config; on a project without it render tools must fail honestly, not advertise a capability that errors
seq_get_info cannot resolve bound-object paths in 5.7 without SharedPlaybackState, so inspect/list_bindings may return empty object_path; document rather than mislead
Long renders can outlive the TCP command timeout; job-envelope + reconnect/port-rediscovery are prerequisites or status polls are lost
Spawnable bindings and sub-sequences have brittle GUID semantics; dry_run + seq_validate must run before/after to catch orphaned bindings
FBX import/export via SequencerTools historically silent-fails on partial bindings; needs read-back verification of imported key counts
domains.test_plan: On a live 5.7 editor with HaybaMCPToolkit + HaybaMCPSequencer loaded and a level open: (1) seq_create under /Game/Cine then seq_inspect confirms zero tracks/bindings and requested frame rate. (2) seq_create_cine_camera pointed at a known actor; seq_list_bindings + seq_list_tracks confirm the camera binding, transform track, and camera-cut section. (3) seq_transform_keyframe at t=0 and t=2s with different locations; seq_list_keys verifies 2 keys per channel; scrub via seq_open and eyeball. (4) seq_set_playback_range 0-3s, seq_set_frame_rate 24; seq_validate returns ok. (5) seq_render_still at t=1s returns a PNG content block to visually confirm framing; seq_render_thumbnail_strip count=6 returns a contact sheet. (6) seq_render_movie returns a job_id immediately (assert editor stays responsive: open a menu, move viewport), poll seq_render_status until done, confirm output files exist and play. (7) Wrap add-track + 5 keys + camera-cut in seq_transaction begin/commit, then Ctrl+Z once and confirm ALL edits revert together. (8) Negative paths: render with MoviePipeline disabled returns an honest not-callable error; seq_delete on a referenced sequence lists referencers and refuses without force; binding tools with no level loaded error cleanly not crash. (9) seq_validate autofix=true on a deliberately orphaned binding reports it in fixed[].

domains.summary: The Niagara VFX domain has a hard, well-documented engine ceiling: UE Python cannot author emitter/module graphs (no scripting API for adding emitters/modules/dynamic-inputs), so we explicitly scope authoring to template-instantiation + exposed-user-parameter packs (brief-mandated) and lean the volume into the surface Python CAN reach — spawn/placement, runtime control, deep introspection, batch/selection, data-interface param injection, deterministic preview, and a net-new PLUMB-style validator/profiler. Today only 3 C++ commands exist (niagara_list/spawn/set_param in the HaybaMCPNiagara module); the brief's "6 target" is a floor, not a cap — competitors barely touch Niagara beyond a spawn verb, so depth here is cheap moat. Strategy: keep the 3 hot-path/crash-prone ops (spawn, set_param, place_actor + transaction checkpoint) in the C++ HaybaMCPNiagara module for game-thread safety and FScopedTransaction wrapping, and ship everything else as python_run-backed pyTemplate descriptors (zero plugin rebuild) per Theme 1 / Global rule "no rebuild by default." Every write tool gets a paired *_inspect read tool, dry_run on destructive ops, and routes verification through niagara_validate + the vision loop. Honesty invariant is load-bearing: authoring tools must self-flag the engine limitation rather than silently no-op like the blueprint_add_node stub.
