Hardened python_run handler (SEH + 3-tier gate + dangling-delegate gate) — the vehicle for all pyTemplate-backed tools
Theme 1 add-a-tool refactor: pyTemplate factory in ToolDescriptor (does not yet exist — gates these python-backed tools shipping as first-class)
FHaybaGameThread::RunSync seam + FScopedTransaction (Moat 4C transactions) for place_actor/checkpoint
Vision loop: render_camera + editor_capture_viewport + wait_for_shaders for niagara_capture_preview
PLUMB validator hooks (plumb_validate / validator_run) for niagara_validate
FNiagaraUserRedirectionParameterStore / NiagaraComponent::SetVariable* APIs (set_param coverage)
ProcessCommand SEH wrap (Theme 0) so C++ niagara handlers are recoverable
risks: HARD ENGINE CEILING: UE Python cannot author Niagara emitter/module/dynamic-input graphs — authoring tools MUST be honest (template-instantiate + exposed-user-params only) or they become a second blueprint_add_node-style false advertisement; set_emitter_enabled/set_asset_property are best-effort and must self-flag unsupported edits
Transient (auto_destroy) spawned components are GC'd / die out — component_path can dangle; read-back tools must handle stale handles gracefully (cf. dangling-delegate crash class)
GPU-sim particle counts and per-emitter cost are not cleanly readable from Python; niagara_profile estimates may be coarse vs an actual stat-niagara capture
Editor world vs PIE world: spawns target GetEditorOrGameWorld(); a transient effect is invisible at t=0, so capture_preview is meaningless without advance_simulation — easy to ship a black screenshot
Data-interface user-param API surface (array/mesh/texture DIs) is unstable across 5.7→5.8 and partly editor-only; set_data_interface_param needs version guards
NiagaraComponent SetVariable* APIs do not persist to the asset — set_user_param_default writes the asset's exposed-param store, a different code path that is easy to confuse and silently no-op
Niagara mutations from python_run won't be captured by C++ FScopedTransaction; transaction_checkpoint must route through the C++ seam, not Python's ScopedEditorTransaction (Moat 4C caveat)
Spawning/placing actors must respect Plan-Mode gate + dry_run; batch spawn can flood the level and freeze the editor if point arrays are huge — cap + paginate
domains.test_plan: Live editor with the HaybaMCPNiagara plugin loaded and a project containing template systems (Engine/Niagara content or Starter VFX). 1) Read path: niagara_list (verify pagination has_more), then niagara_system_inspect + niagara_param_list on a known system (fountain/fire) — confirm emitter names, sim targets, exposed user params match the Niagara editor. 2) Spawn path: niagara_spawn at origin → niagara_component_inspect confirms active+system_path; niagara_advance_simulation 1.0s then niagara_capture_preview → eyeball the returned PNG shows actual particles (not a black t=0 frame). 3) Control: niagara_set_param (color) + niagara_set_params_batch, re-inspect to read back applied values; niagara_set_paused true then screenshot a frozen frame; niagara_deactivate immediate=true → inspect shows inactive. 4) Placement+undo: niagara_place_actor (persistent) → confirm ANiagaraActor in World Outliner; wrap a spawn+param sequence in niagara_transaction_checkpoint begin/end → single Ctrl+Z removes ALL of it (the differentiator). 5) Authoring (honest-limit): niagara_create_from_template to a new path → niagara_set_user_param_default + save → reopen asset, confirm default persisted; confirm set_emitter_enabled returns a clear engine-limit note if unsupported. 6) Validation: niagara_validate on a deliberately unbounded-GPU / no-fixed-bounds system → expect violations with codes; fix via set_asset_property, re-validate → ok=true. 7) Batch: niagara_spawn_batch over 10 points → niagara_list_components count==10 → niagara_batch_set_param recolors all → re-inspect a sample. 8) Safety: niagara_delete dry_run=true lists referencers without deleting; confirm Plan-Mode blocks the real delete until approved. Cross-check no editor freeze (timeouts align to UE ceilings) and no AV in the journal (hayba_journal_tail) after transient components are GC'd.

tools.name: niagara_list
tools.description: List Niagara System assets (path/name) with prefix + pagination; the entry read-tool for discovery. EXISTS — extend with limit/has_more/next_offset.

tools.name: niagara_system_inspect
tools.description: Dump a system asset's structure: emitter handles (name/enabled/sim-target CPU|GPU), exposed user parameters (name/type/default), data interfaces, fixed bounds, warmup, loop behavior. Inspection-first paired read; highest-ROI introspection the domain lacks.

tools.name: niagara_param_list
tools.description: List just the exposed USER parameters of a system asset with type+current default — the contract an agent needs before niagara_set_param. Focused, cheaper variant of system_inspect.

tools.name: niagara_spawn
tools.signature: (system_path, location?, rotation?, scale?, auto_destroy=true, auto_activate=true, dry_run?) -> {component_path, actor_path, spawned_path}
tools.description: Spawn a transient (auto-destroy) Niagara system at a world location/rotation/scale; the workhorse placement verb. EXISTS — add dry_run + FScopedTransaction + return component+actor paths.

tools.name: niagara_spawn_attached
tools.signature: (system_path, target_actor, attach_socket?, location_offset?, rotation_offset?, auto_destroy=true, dry_run?) -> {component_path, attached_to}
tools.description: Spawn a system attached to a target actor/component at an optional socket with location/rotation offset (muzzle flashes, exhaust, trails) — the attachment case bare niagara_spawn can't express.

tools.name: niagara_place_actor
tools.signature: (system_path, location, rotation?, scale?, label?, dry_run?) -> {actor_path, component_path}
tools.description: Place a PERSISTENT ANiagaraActor in the level (survives save, undoable, selectable) vs the transient component spawn — for level-dressing VFX an author wants to keep and re-edit.

tools.name: niagara_spawn_batch
tools.description: Scatter many instances of one system across an array of points (or sampled actor surface) in a single call — outcome-verb for crowds/foliage-VFX, avoids N round-trips.

tools.name: niagara_set_param
tools.description: Set one user variable on a live component (float/int/bool/vec3/color/object). EXISTS — keep C++ for hot-path; broaden value_type coverage (vec2/vec4/quat/position).

tools.name: niagara_set_params_batch
tools.description: Set MANY user params on one component in a single call (typed map), then one MarkRenderStateDirty — the ergonomic bulk variant that out-tools per-param competitors.

tools.name: niagara_batch_set_param
tools.description: Set one param across EVERY live component instancing a given system (or matching a tag) — outcome-verb for 'turn all torches blue'. Pairs with niagara_select_in_level.

tools.name: niagara_component_inspect
tools.description: Read a live component's runtime state: active/paused, current user-param values, age, system asset, bounds, last-render-time — the read-back/verify tool for runtime control ops.

tools.name: niagara_list_components
tools.description: Enumerate all Niagara components in the editor/PIE world (placed actors + transient spawns) with system path + active flag; paginated. The 'what's currently in the scene' read tool.

tools.name: niagara_activate
tools.description: Activate (optionally reset) a component to (re)start the effect — needed because many template systems ship auto_activate=false.

tools.name: niagara_deactivate
tools.description: Deactivate a component, optionally killing particles immediately (DeactivateImmediate) vs letting them die out — the clean stop/teardown verb.

tools.name: niagara_set_paused
tools.description: Pause/resume a component's simulation in place — for inspecting a frozen frame before a screenshot or stepping a debug.

tools.name: niagara_advance_simulation
tools.description: Deterministically tick a component's sim by N seconds at a fixed dt (AdvanceSimulation) so screenshots are reproducible — the deterministic-preview primitive the vision loop needs (a transient effect is invisible at t=0).

tools.name: niagara_capture_preview
tools.description: Spawn a system in isolation, advance its sim to a target time, auto-frame on its bounds, and return a screenshot as an image content block — the end-to-end VFX vision-verify loop (extends Moat #5).

tools.name: niagara_validate
tools.description: PLUMB-style quantified pre/post-mutate validator: flags unbounded GPU emitters, missing fixed bounds, runaway spawn rates, missing effect-type/scalability, CPU-sim count over budget — closed-loop correctness no competitor offers for VFX.

tools.name: niagara_profile
tools.description: Report per-component perf: active particle count, sim target, GPU/CPU sim cost estimate, bounds for live components — read-back for perf tuning and the validator's budget input.

tools.name: niagara_create_from_template
tools.signature: (template_path, dest_path, name) -> {new_system_path, source_template, note:'graph authoring is a UE Python limit'}
tools.description: The HONEST authoring path: duplicate a template system asset to a new content path and rename — since UE Python cannot build emitter graphs, template-instantiation is the supported creation verb (brief-mandated, flagged with engine-limit note).

tools.name: niagara_set_user_param_default
tools.signature: (system_path, param_name, value_type, value, save=false) -> {system_path, param_name, applied}
tools.description: Set the DEFAULT value of an exposed user parameter ON the asset (persists to the saved system), not just a live component — the param-pack vehicle for customizing instantiated templates.

tools.name: niagara_set_asset_property
tools.description: Set reflection-exposed system-level properties (warmup time/tick-count, fixed bounds, effect type, loop behavior) on the asset — best-effort over UPROPERTYs that ARE scriptable; self-flags non-settable graph internals.

tools.name: niagara_set_emitter_enabled
tools.signature: (system_path, emitter_name, enabled, save=false) -> {system_path, emitter_name, enabled, supported}
tools.description: Toggle an emitter handle's enabled state on a system asset (one of the few graph-adjacent edits exposed) — best-effort, returns engine-limit note if the editor API is unavailable in the build.

tools.name: niagara_set_data_interface_param
tools.description: Inject array/object DATA INTERFACE user params on a live component (positions/vector arrays, static-mesh DI, texture/skeletal DI) — advanced control driving data-driven VFX that scalar set_param can't reach.

tools.name: niagara_set_mesh_renderer_mesh
tools.description: Swap the static mesh used by a system's mesh renderer via its exposed user param (the common 'debris uses this mesh' pattern) — convenience outcome-verb over set_data_interface_param.

tools.name: niagara_assign_system
tools.description: Swap the NiagaraSystem asset bound to an existing component/actor (retarget an existing emitter to a different effect) without respawning.

tools.name: niagara_duplicate
tools.description: Duplicate a system asset to a new path (variant authoring without touching the template) — paired sibling of create_from_template for fork-and-tweak.

tools.name: niagara_delete
tools.description: Delete a system asset with referencer check + dry_run preview; gated by Plan-Mode. The unglamorous destructive op done safely.

tools.name: niagara_save
tools.description: Save dirty Niagara system assets (single path or all) — the persist step after asset-level param/default edits; read-back lists what was saved.

tools.name: niagara_select_in_level
tools.description: Select all Niagara actors/components in the level matching a system path or tag — feeds batch ops and gives the user a visible selection (Unity/Roblox selection-management pattern).

tools.name: niagara_effect_type_set_quality
tools.description: Get/set the global Niagara scalability quality level and a system's NiagaraEffectType binding — the scalability lever letting the validator enforce platform budgets.

tools.name: niagara_transaction_checkpoint
tools.description: Bundle a sequence of Niagara mutations into ONE undo checkpoint (begin/end + restore) — surfaces the cross-cutting 4C transaction seam for VFX so multi-step spawn+param scripts collapse to a single Ctrl+Z (differentiator vs Epic per-call undo).

domains.summary: Almost entirely greenfield: today only render_camera (crash-prone, force-gated C++) and a 4-mode viewport switch exist, while Themes 3/4B name Lighting/Lumen (9), Nanite (3), MoviePipeline render, and vision buffer/orbit capture as quick high-value wins. Strategy: ship the lighting/PP/Lumen/Nanite authoring surface as python_run pyTemplate wrappers (zero rebuild, the Section-5 multiplier), reserving C++ only for genuinely hot/crash-prone paths: G-buffer visualization passes, extended show-flag view modes, and job-enveloped Movie Render Queue (which would otherwise freeze the game thread like build_*). Every write tool ships a paired *_inspect read, a dry_run preview, and outcome-verbs (lighting_preset_apply) collapsed into one Ctrl+Z to press the transaction moat vs Epic's per-call undo. The PostProcessSettings bOverride_* footgun and global rendering-cvar side-effects are wrapped with explicit override-flag handling plus readback/restore so agents can validate before/after mutate through PLUMB. Net result: the deepest dedicated lighting+render-output surface among UE MCP competitors, built mostly without plugin rebuilds.
dependencies: UE 5.7 Python editor-scripting (unreal module) via the hardened python_run handler (SEH + 3-tier security gate)
runUePythonJson + PY_PREAMBLE HAYBA_JSON contract (src/tools/ue-python.ts) for all pyTemplate wrappers
EditorActorSubsystem / LevelEditorSubsystem / UnrealEditorSubsystem for spawn, selection, and viewport camera
existing editor_capture_viewport (now returns a real inline image block) + editor_set_camera/set_level_viewport_camera_info for orbit/auto-frame loops
Theme-0 job-envelope async conversion (docs/audit/2026-06-22-mcp-async-command-conversions.md) is a hard prerequisite for movie_render and light_build_static so they do not freeze the game thread
MovieRenderPipeline + MovieRenderPipelineEditor plugins enabled for MRQ rendering
C++ HaybaMCPToolkit RenderHandler/EditorHandler rebuild for buffer_visualization_capture + viewport_set_view_mode (SceneCapture world-pos spike already exists per AI-mask Task 0 findings)
FScopedTransaction wrapping in C++ handlers (4C) for true single-undo on preset apply; python ScopedEditorTransaction for PY-only mutations
PLUMB validator + green/red plan-mode overlay for validate-before/after-mutate
ToolDescriptor/register-tool.ts descriptor path + schema-registry + code-mode/deferred routing so the ~30 new tools land behind packs without bloating the eager surface
risks: PostProcessSettings has ~100 paired bOverride_* booleans; setting a value without its override flag silently no-ops — wrappers MUST set bOverride_X=true and inspect must report override state

render_camera/SceneCapture is a documented editor-crasher; orbit_capture and thumbnail_generate must prefer viewport-capture (set camera + editor_capture_viewport) and pre-warm shaders, never sync SceneCapture the live world (per scenecapture-from-python memory)
Movie Render Queue and Lightmass static build are long (>120s) game-thread blockers — they MUST go through the Theme-0 job envelope or they reintroduce the editor-freeze P0
global rendering cvars (r.Lumen.*, r.Nanite.*, sg.*) are process-wide side-effects; render_cvar_set needs a whitelist + readback + restore-on-session-end or it silently degrades unrelated work
Lumen/Nanite/Virtual Shadow Maps require correct RHI/feature-level (SM6, DX12); enabling on an unsupported project fails opaquely — lumen_configure must probe and report capability
viewport exposure vs game/PIE exposure differ (auto-exposure metering); inspect/readback values can mislead unless the capture context is reported
buffer_visualization_capture and viewport_set_view_mode extensions require a plugin rebuild (the 4-7 file / rebuild tax) — keep them minimal and behind the Theme-1 descriptor refactor
Nanite enable rebuilds the mesh (slow, asset-dirtying); nanite_batch_enable across a folder can stall the editor — must paginate + report per-asset status
PP color-grading and exposure overlap; without outcome-verbs agents will fight conflicting low-level sets — mitigate with lighting_preset_apply and a single PPV target convention
domains.test_plan: Live editor on a scratch level with one ground plane + a couple of static meshes. (1) light_spawn directional + sky, then light_inspect and assert the returned intensity/temperature/mobility match what was set. (2) postprocess_volume_create unbound, postprocess_set bloom+vignette with dry_run=true (assert no scene change via postprocess_inspect), then dry_run=false and assert bOverride_ flags + values readback. (3) exposure_set manual EV, auto_frame_actor on a mesh + editor_capture_viewport, confirm the inline image brightens/darkens as EV changes. (4) lumen_configure enable GI+reflections, capture before/after via before_after_capture and eyeball indirect light; on an unsupported RHI assert a clean capability error not a crash. (5) orbit_capture N=8 around a mesh — assert 8 image blocks + a contact sheet returned, editor still responsive (no freeze). (6) buffer_visualization_capture world_normal + base_color — assert distinct passes returned as MIME-typed images. (7) nanite_set enable on one mesh, nanite_inspect assert enabled + fallback %, nanite_batch_enable on a 3-mesh folder assert paginated per-asset status. (8) movie_render on a 24-frame LevelSequence to a temp dir — assert job-envelope returns a job id, polls to done, files on disk, editor never blocked. (9) lighting_preset_apply golden_hour then a single Ctrl+Z (undo) — assert the whole preset (lights+PPV+sky) reverts in ONE step. (10) render_cvar_set r.Lumen.* from a whitelist with readback, then session-end restore — assert original value restored. Throughout, run validator_run / plumb_validate before and after mutations to confirm green/red plan-mode overlay fires.

tools.name: light_spawn
tools.parity: GenOrca has generic actor spawn; net-new as a typed lighting verb
tools.signature: (light_type:Literal[directional,point,spot,rect,sky], name?, location?, rotation?, intensity?, color_rgb?, temperature_k?, mobility?, attenuation_radius?, source_angle?, cast_shadows?, dry_run?) -> {ok, actor_path, applied}
tools.description: Spawn a directional/point/spot/rect/sky light with intensity, color, temperature, mobility in one call — the primary way to lay down scene lighting.

tools.name: light_set
tools.parity: net-new moat (no competitor ships a typed light editor)
tools.signature: (actor_path, intensity?, color_rgb?, temperature_k?, use_temperature?, attenuation_radius?, source_radius?, source_angle?, ies_asset?, cast_shadows?, shadow_bias?, mobility?, dry_run?) -> {ok, actor_path, changed, before, after}
tools.description: Set properties (intensity, color, temperature, attenuation, source size, IES, shadow bias, cast-shadows, mobility) on an existing light by path — the core light-tuning verb.

tools.name: light_inspect
tools.parity: Unity peer paginates hierarchy; net-new for lighting props
tools.description: Read back all lights in the level (or one by path) with their key properties — the paired inspection-first read so agents tune from real values not guesses.

tools.name: light_batch_set
tools.parity: Roblox peer mass_set_property; net-new for UE lighting
tools.description: Batch-adjust a property across many lights selected by query/class/tag (dim all, re-temperature, toggle shadows) — outcome-verb batch op vs per-light churn.

tools.name: skylight_configure
tools.signature: (actor_path?, source_type:Literal[captured_scene,specified_cubemap], cubemap?, intensity?, recapture?, lower_hemi_is_black?, dry_run?) -> {ok, actor_path, recaptured}
tools.description: Configure/recapture a SkyLight (real-time vs captured, source cubemap, intensity, lower hemisphere color) and trigger recapture — ambient/IBL control.

tools.name: postprocess_volume_create
tools.signature: (name?, unbound=true, location?, extent?, priority?, blend_weight?, blend_radius?, dry_run?) -> {ok, actor_path}
tools.description: Create a PostProcessVolume (unbound or box-bounded) with priority/blend-weight — the container every PP/exposure/Lumen tweak targets.

tools.name: postprocess_set
tools.parity: net-new moat (handles the bOverride_ footgun no competitor exposes)
tools.signature: (target_path, settings:{group->key->value}, clear_overrides?, dry_run?) -> {ok, applied, override_flags_set, before, after}
tools.description: Set any PostProcessSettings group (bloom, exposure, GI, reflections, DOF, color-grading, AO, motion-blur, vignette, film-grain, chromatic-aberration) with correct bOverride_* flags on a volume or camera — the workhorse PP verb.

tools.name: postprocess_inspect
tools.description: Read back PostProcessSettings and which bOverride_* flags are active on a volume/camera — paired read so agents see what is actually overridden.

tools.name: exposure_set
tools.signature: (target_path, method:Literal[manual,auto_histogram,auto_basic], exposure_compensation?, min_ev100?, max_ev100?, metering_mode?, dry_run?) -> {ok, applied, before, after}
tools.description: Set auto-exposure mode (manual/histogram/basic), EV compensation, min/max EV, metering mask — the single most-asked PP knob, as a focused verb.

tools.name: color_grading_set
tools.parity: GenOrca touches material graph; net-new for grading
tools.signature: (target_path, temp?, tint?, ranges:{global?,shadows?,midtones?,highlights?:{saturation?,contrast?,gamma?,gain?,offset?}}, dry_run?) -> {ok, applied, before, after}
tools.description: Set white-balance temp/tint and per-range (global/shadows/midtones/highlights) saturation/contrast/gamma/gain/offset — cinematic look control.

tools.name: depth_of_field_set
tools.signature: (target_path, focal_distance?, f_stop?, focal_region?, focus_actor?, dry_run?) -> {ok, applied, focal_distance_used}
tools.description: Configure cinematic DOF (focal distance, aperture f-stop, focal region) or auto-focus onto an actor's bounds — framing/realism control.

tools.name: lumen_configure
tools.parity: Epic baseline lacks Lumen depth; net-new moat
tools.signature: (target_path, gi_enabled?, reflections_enabled?, final_gather_quality?, scene_lighting_quality?, reflection_quality?, scene_detail?, max_trace_distance?, hardware_rt?, dry_run?) -> {ok, applied, rhi_supported, warnings}
tools.description: Enable/disable Lumen GI and reflections and set quality (final-gather, lighting/reflection quality, scene-detail, max-trace-distance, hardware-RT) on a PPV, with RHI capability probe — the headline UE5 lighting verb.

tools.name: reflection_method_set
tools.signature: (target_path?, method?:Literal[lumen,ssr,none], ssr_quality?, place_capture?:{shape,location,radius,brightness}, build_captures?, dry_run?) -> {ok, applied, captures_built}
tools.description: Set the reflection method (Lumen/SSR/None) and SSR quality on a PPV, and place/build Sphere or Box reflection captures — reflection authoring.

tools.name: fog_configure
tools.signature: (actor_path?, density?, height_falloff?, fog_color?, start_distance?, volumetric_enabled?, scattering?, extinction?, albedo?, dry_run?) -> {ok, actor_path, applied}
tools.description: Configure ExponentialHeightFog (density, height falloff, color, start distance) and volumetric fog (scattering, extinction, albedo, view distance) — atmosphere/mood.

tools.name: sky_atmosphere_configure
tools.signature: (actor_path?, rayleigh_scattering?, mie_scattering?, sun_disk?, ground_albedo?, link_sun_light?, dry_run?) -> {ok, actor_path, applied}
tools.description: Configure a SkyAtmosphere actor (rayleigh/mie scattering, sun-disk, ground albedo) and link it to the directional sun light — physically-based sky.

tools.name: shadow_configure
tools.signature: (actor_path, method?:Literal[vsm,cascaded], num_cascades?, dynamic_shadow_distance?, contact_shadow_length?, raytraced?, dry_run?) -> {ok, applied, before, after}
tools.description: Set shadow method (Virtual Shadow Maps vs cascaded SM), cascade count/distance, contact shadows, and ray-traced shadow toggle on a directional light — shadow quality.

tools.name: nanite_set
tools.parity: net-new moat (no competitor ships Nanite control)
tools.signature: (asset_path, enabled, fallback_percent?, position_precision?, dry_run?) -> {ok, asset_path, rebuilt, tri_counts}
tools.description: Enable/disable Nanite on a static-mesh asset and set fallback-triangle-percent / position precision — the easiest perf win in the brief.

tools.name: nanite_inspect
tools.description: Read back Nanite enabled-state, triangle/cluster counts, and fallback settings for one or many meshes — paired read before toggling.

tools.name: nanite_batch_enable
tools.parity: Roblox peer mass ops; net-new for Nanite
tools.signature: (folder?, selection?, min_triangles?, fallback_percent?, dry_run?, limit=25, offset=0) -> {ok, processed:[{path,status}], skipped, has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: Enable Nanite across a folder/selection of static meshes above a triangle threshold, paginated with per-asset status — bulk perf migration.

tools.name: render_cvar_set
tools.signature: (cvar, value, persist_for_session?, dry_run?) -> {ok, cvar, old_value, new_value, whitelisted}
tools.description: Set a whitelisted rendering console variable (r.Lumen.*, r.Nanite.*, r.Shadow.*, sg.*) with prior-value readback and session restore — a scoped, safe escape hatch.

tools.name: scalability_set
tools.description: Apply an engine scalability preset (low..cinematic) or set individual sg.* group levels — quick quality/perf staging for renders.

tools.name: viewport_set_view_mode
tools.description: Extend the existing 4-mode switch to the full show-flag/view-mode set (lighting-only, reflections, lumen-overview, detail-lighting, collision, lightmap-density) for diagnostic captures — vision-loop introspection.

tools.name: buffer_visualization_capture
tools.module: HaybaMCPToolkit / RenderHandler (C++; SceneCapture world-pos spike exists)
tools.parity: net-new moat (no UE MCP ships buffer-viz passes)
tools.description: Capture a G-buffer visualization pass (base-color, world-normal, roughness, metallic, depth, overdraw, shader-complexity, lumen-scene) as a MIME-typed image — the strongest-in-class vision-feedback moat (4B).

tools.name: orbit_capture
tools.signature: (target:{actor?,selection?}, num_frames=8, elevation_deg?, distance?, width?, height?, contact_sheet?) -> {ok, images:[block], contact_sheet_path}
tools.description: Turntable capture: N viewport shots around an actor/selection bounds, returned as inline image blocks plus a contact sheet — multi-angle vision loop (4B) without crash-prone SceneCapture.

tools.name: auto_frame_actor
tools.parity: Blender/Unity focus; net-new for UE MCP
tools.signature: (target:{actor?,selection?,bounds?}, padding?, pitch_deg?, yaw_deg?, capture?) -> {ok, camera_location, camera_rotation, image_block?}
tools.description: Frame/focus the editor viewport camera on an actor or current selection's bounds then capture — auto-focus vision helper (4B) so captures are never empty.

tools.name: thumbnail_generate
tools.parity: Blender asset thumbnails; net-new for UE MCP
tools.signature: (asset_paths?, folder?, size?, limit=20, offset=0) -> {ok, thumbnails:[{path,image_block}], has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: Render per-asset thumbnails for a list/folder of assets and return them as image blocks — asset triage vision loop, steal-Blender pattern.

tools.name: before_after_capture
tools.signature: (camera?, label_a?, label_b?, mutation_token?) -> {ok, before_block, after_block, diff_block}
tools.description: Capture the viewport, await a referenced mutation (or tool bundle), capture again, and return a before/after side-by-side diff — closes the validate-before/after-mutate loop visually (4B).

tools.name: high_res_screenshot
tools.parity: remiphilippe visual tests; net-new authoring depth
tools.signature: (multiplier?, width?, height?, hdr?, include_ui?, output_path?) -> {ok, path, image_block?}
tools.description: Request a high-resolution editor screenshot (resolution multiplier, include-UI, HDR/EXR) via the job envelope and return the written path — marketing/inspection stills without freezing.

tools.name: movie_render
tools.module: HaybaMCPSequencer (C++ MRQ executor) + python_run TS wrapper
tools.parity: remiphilippe headless render / Flop cloud render; local job-enveloped moat
tools.signature: (sequence_path, output_dir, resolution?, format?:Literal[png,jpg,exr,mp4], frame_range?, preset?, samples?) -> {ok, job_id} ; poll -> {state, frames_done, output_files}
tools.description: Render a LevelSequence through Movie Render Queue (resolution/format/AA/output-dir preset) as a job-enveloped async job so the game thread never blocks — the production render verb.

tools.name: render_preset_define
tools.description: Define/store a reusable render configuration (resolution, format, AA samples, MRQ settings) referenced by name from movie_render/high_res_screenshot — DRY render configs.

tools.name: lighting_preset_apply
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (ScopedEditorTransaction) — promote to C++ FScopedTransaction if mixing C++ handler mutations
tools.signature: (preset:Literal[golden_hour,overcast,studio_3point,moonlight,clear_noon], target_volume?, intensity_scale?, dry_run?) -> {ok, undo_label, actors_created, settings_applied}
tools.description: Apply a named lighting look (golden_hour, overcast, studio_3point, moonlight) that spawns+configures lights, PPV, sky and fog as ONE outcome verb collapsed into a single Ctrl+Z — the transaction/undo differentiator vs Epic per-call undo (4C).

tools.name: light_build_static

tools.parity: remiphilippe headless build; net-new safety framing
tools.description: Trigger a Lightmass static-lighting build at a quality level as a job-enveloped async job (avoids the build_* 300s game-thread freeze) — baked-lighting workflow, Theme-0 compliant.

tools.name: lighting_validate

domains.summary: Today the surface is 3 raw C++ commands (physics_set_simulate / set_collision_profile / add_impulse) plus a scene_validate_physics read — zero first-class tools, no Chaos destruction, no PhysicsAsset, no constraints, no fields, no sim-bake. The strategy: (1) make the rigid-body author loop honest and outcome-shaped via python_run wrappers (set_body_properties, set_collision, forces, constraints, physical materials, collision-mesh gen) with no plugin rebuild; (2) lean the moat into Chaos destruction (Geometry Collection create/fracture/anchor/field) and PhysicsAsset/ragdoll authoring, which NO competitor (Epic baseline, Aura, Flop, GenOrca) ships — net-new moat, accepted as C++/MIX because UE Python coverage is near-zero there; (3) reinforce the safety moats with inspect-first read tools, a dry_run on every destructive fracture, FScopedTransaction wrapping, a post-sim stability verifier (NaN/explosion/interpenetration), and batch/query verbs. Chaos fracture and simulate-and-bake must ship through the job-envelope/async seam (Theme 0) so they never block the game thread like build_*/test_run do, and through the RunSync seam to avoid task-graph re-entrancy. Honesty invariant: anything Python cannot reach (fracture, anchors, fields, phys-asset body gen) is flagged C++-gated, not advertised as working before the rebuild lands.
dependencies: Theme 0 gate: ProcessCommand SEH-wrap (so all physics handlers are crash-recoverable) + job-envelope/async conversion (fracture and simulate_and_bake are slow → must not block game thread like build_*/test_run)
Theme 1 add-a-tool refactor: single ToolDescriptor with ueCommand/pyTemplate/handler so the ~22 python_run + ~8 C++ tools land without 7-file churn or 4-place schema drift
4C transaction seam: FScopedTransaction wrapping in HaybaGameThread::RunSync — required for physics_undo, simulate_and_bake, fracture, batch_set to be one-undo
FHaybaGameThread::RunSync seam (PR #254): every C++ handler that steps the scene or touches GeometryCollection must marshal to game thread without AsyncTask(GameThread)+Wait self-deadlock

Build.cs module deps for C++ tools: GeometryCollectionEngine, GeometryCollectionEditor, FieldSystemEngine, Chaos, PhysicsCore, ChaosSolverEngine; honor EngineVersion pin (5.7.0) — these APIs churn across versions
python_run hardened handler (SEH + 3-tier gate + dangling-delegate gate) for all pyTemplate tools; StaticMeshEditorSubsystem for collision-gen
Existing HaybaMCPPhysicsHandler.cpp (extend GetCommands/Handle) for set_simulate/add_impulse first-class wrappers
Plan-Mode gate (bPlanApproved) before destructive ops: fracture, simulate_and_bake, batch_set, mesh_generate_collision(replace)
wait_for_idle / editor sim tick access for simulate_and_bake settling; render_camera/editor_capture_viewport for before/after destruction visual verify
risks: Chaos fracture, anchors, fields, GC create, and PhysicsAsset body-gen have near-zero UE Python coverage — they are editor-only C++ and REQUIRE a plugin rebuild; do not advertise as working until compiled, or we repeat the blueprint_add_node 'not_implemented_in_v1' honesty violation
Geometry Collection / Fracture / Field APIs change significantly between UE releases; pinned 5.7.0 build may break on 5.8 — flag as engine-version-sensitive

simulate_and_bake must step the physics scene in the editor world; editor world does not advance physics by default without PIE/simulate — may require a manual Chaos solver tick via RunSync, and a hard time cap to avoid the build_* 300s-freeze class of bug
Fracture on dense meshes is slow and memory-heavy → must run via async job-envelope + dry_run piece-count preview first, or it freezes the game thread
Stepping/baking physics mutates actor transforms irreversibly without transaction wrapping → batch_set and simulate_and_bake MUST be FScopedTransaction-wrapped and Plan-Mode gated

add_force/add_impulse/set_velocity only have visible effect while a body is actually simulating; in a non-simulating editor world they silently no-op — verify_stability and inspect read-backs must report 'not simulating' rather than 'applied:true' to avoid false success
Constraint creation via Python (PhysicsConstraintComponent) can register lifetime delegates — route through the dangling-delegate gate (#283/#284) to avoid the python_run AV crash class
ChaosCloth and ControlRig-driven physics are genuine UE Python limits — explicitly out of scope here; scope ragdoll to template/auto-gen + param packs and flag as engine limitation
domains.test_plan: Live-editor validation, ordered cheap-to-expensive: (1) Spawn a few static-mesh actors (cube stack) via actor tools; run physics_list_simulating (expect empty), physics_inspect on one (expect simulating:false). (2) physics_set_simulate enabled=true, then physics_set_body_properties mass_kg=50 gravity_enabled=true; re-inspect to confirm read-back matches. (3) editor_start_pie or simulate, capture viewport before; apply physics_add_force radial explosion at stack origin; capture after — confirm pieces scattered visually, then physics_verify_stability (expect ok:true, no NaN/explosion). (4) mesh_generate_collision convex on a complex mesh; drop it with simulate and confirm it no longer falls through floor. (5) physical_material_create (low friction, high restitution) + assign to a sphere; simulate and confirm visible bounce. (6) physics_add_constraint hinge between a door and frame; simulate and confirm swing limited to the configured angle. (7) physics_batch_set across selection with dry_run=true (confirm matched count, no mutation), then dry_run=false, then physics_undo and confirm reverted in one Ctrl+Z. (8) C++-gated path (after rebuild): geometry_collection_create from a cube, geometry_collection_fracture dry_run=true (confirm predicted pieces), then real fracture, geometry_collection_brief to read levels, add_anchor bottom, spawn physics_field_spawn strain at impact point, simulate and capture viewport to confirm anchored-then-shattering behavior; finish with physics_simulate_and_bake on a pile of debris (seconds=4) and confirm baked resting transforms persist after stopping sim. Verify each handler survives a forced client disconnect mid-command (SEH/late-response crash regression) and that no command exceeds the executor timeout.

tools.name: physics_inspect
tools.parity: net-new moat (Flop has inspect pattern, none for physics)
tools.signature: (actor_id, component_name?) -> {simulating, mass_kg, linear_damping, angular_damping, gravity_enabled, collision_enabled, collision_profile, ccd, com_offset, linear_velocity, angular_velocity, asleep}
tools.description: Read all physics state of an actor/component (simulate on?, mass, lin/ang damping, gravity, collision enabled+profile, CCD, COM, current lin/ang velocity, asleep?) — the inspect-first read that pairs every write verb.

tools.name: physics_list_simulating
tools.signature: (filter_class?, tag?, collision_only?, limit=50, offset=0) -> {items:[{actor_id,component,simulating,mass_kg,profile}], has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: Paginated list of actors/components with simulate-physics or collision enabled, with mass and profile — lets the agent find rigid bodies before mutating instead of guessing names.

tools.name: physics_set_simulate
tools.description: Toggle simulate-physics on a primitive component (first-class wrapper over the existing C++ command; outcome-shaped with read-back).

tools.name: physics_set_body_properties
tools.signature: (actor_id, component_name?, mass_kg?, mass_scale?, linear_damping?, angular_damping?, gravity_enabled?, max_angular_velocity?) -> {applied_fields, readback}
tools.description: One outcome verb to set mass-override-kg, mass scale, linear/angular damping, gravity-enable, max angular velocity, start-awake — collapses the most common rigid-body tuning into one call.

tools.name: physics_set_collision
tools.signature: (actor_id, component_name?, collision_enabled?, profile?, object_type?, channel_responses?, ccd?) -> {profile, collision_enabled, ccd}
tools.description: Set collision-enabled mode (NoCollision/QueryOnly/PhysicsOnly/QueryAndPhysics) + preset profile + per-channel object type & responses + CCD flag in one call; replaces the bare set_collision_profile.

tools.name: physics_batch_set
tools.description: Apply simulate/collision/body-property changes across a selection or query (by class/tag/name-glob) in one transaction — the mass-edit ergonomics verb; matches Roblox mass_set_property.

tools.name: physics_add_impulse
tools.description: Apply a one-shot impulse (or velocity-change) at COM or a world point — first-class wrapper over existing C++ command.

tools.name: physics_add_force
tools.description: Apply a continuous force/torque, or a radial force/impulse with falloff radius+strength — covers explosions, wind, attractors that impulse alone can't.

tools.name: physics_set_velocity
tools.description: Directly set linear and/or angular velocity of a body — needed for scripted throws and deterministic test setups that forces can't reproduce.

tools.name: physics_set_mass_center
tools.description: Override the center-of-mass offset of a body — controls tipping/toppling realism for stacked or weighted props.

tools.name: physics_wake_sleep
tools.description: Wake or force-sleep a body (and optionally a whole island) — unsticks settled actors after an edit and lets the agent control sim cost.

tools.name: physics_add_constraint
tools.signature: (actor_id, comp_a, comp_b, linear{x,y,z,limit}?, swing1?, swing2?, twist?, drive?, location?[3]) -> {constraint_name}
tools.description: Spawn a PhysicsConstraintComponent linking two components with linear (free/limited/locked + limit) and angular swing1/swing2/twist limits, plus drive params — the building block for hinges, doors, ropes, ragdoll joints.

tools.name: physics_constraint_inspect
tools.description: Read the limits/drives/connected components of a constraint — inspect pairing for add/remove.

tools.name: physics_remove_constraint
tools.description: Delete a physics constraint component by name — cleanup verb for the constraint loop.

tools.name: physical_material_create
tools.description: Create a PhysicalMaterial asset with friction, restitution, density, friction-combine mode (and surface type) — the asset behind realistic sliding/bouncing.

tools.name: physical_material_inspect
tools.description: Read friction/restitution/density/surface-type of a PhysicalMaterial asset — read pairing.

tools.name: physical_material_assign
tools.description: Assign a PhysicalMaterial to a static-mesh asset, a material, or a body setup, optionally across a selection — wires the asset into actual collision response.

tools.name: mesh_generate_collision
tools.description: Generate simple collision on a static mesh: box/sphere/capsule/K-DOP primitives or convex-decomposition (hull count + accuracy) — fixes the #1 cause of objects falling through the world.

tools.name: mesh_remove_collision
tools.description: Strip all simple collision from a static mesh — paired cleanup for collision iteration.

tools.name: geometry_collection_create
tools.description: Create a Chaos Geometry Collection asset+actor from one or more static meshes (the destructible source) — entry point to the destruction moat no competitor has.

tools.name: geometry_collection_fracture
tools.module: HaybaMCPToolkit C++ (FractureEditor) — C++-gated, async job-envelope, transaction-wrapped, Plan-Mode gated
tools.signature: (gc_asset_path, mode:'uniform'|'voronoi'|'clustered'|'radial'|'planar', sites, seed?, noise?, grout?, cluster_level?, dry_run=false) -> {pieces, levels, job_id}
tools.description: Fracture a Geometry Collection: uniform/Voronoi/clustered/radial/planar with site count, seed, noise, grout, and cluster level; dry_run returns predicted piece count without mutating — core destruction authoring.

tools.name: geometry_collection_set_damage
tools.description: Set per-cluster-level damage thresholds, internal/external strain, collision particles, and mass scaling on a GC — controls how easily it shatters.

tools.name: geometry_collection_add_anchor
tools.description: Mark bones anchored (or attach a static-anchor field) so the structure stays fixed until impact frees it — the difference between a building and a pile of rubble.

tools.name: geometry_collection_brief
tools.description: Read a Geometry Collection's fracture levels, bone/cluster counts, damage thresholds, anchored bones, and collision settings — inspect pairing for the destruction loop.

tools.name: physics_field_spawn
tools.description: Spawn a FieldSystemActor with a radial/uniform vector / radial-falloff / strain field to push, attract, or break Chaos bodies — programmable forces and triggered destruction.

tools.name: physics_asset_create
tools.signature: (skeletal_mesh_path, package_path, name, primitive:'capsule'|'box'|'sphere', min_bone_size?) -> {phys_asset_path, body_count, constraint_count}
tools.description: Generate a PhysicsAsset from a skeletal mesh with auto body generation (min bone size, primitive type, constraint creation) — the ragdoll foundation; Python can't reach the body-builder so this is C++.

tools.name: physics_asset_brief
tools.description: Read a PhysicsAsset's bodies (bone, shape, mass) and constraints (limits) — inspect pairing for ragdoll work; read-only so can ship as Python reflection ahead of the create tool.

tools.name: physics_simulate_and_bake
tools.module: HaybaMCPToolkit C++ (RunSync seam, async job-envelope, FScopedTransaction) — C++-gated
tools.signature: (actor_ids[]|selection, seconds?=5, settle_threshold?, dry_run=false) -> {baked_count, settled, final_transforms, job_id}
tools.description: Run the editor physics scene for N seconds (or until all bodies sleep), then bake the resting transforms back onto the actors and disable sim — 'drop these props so they settle naturally', baked into ONE undo.

tools.name: physics_verify_stability
tools.description: Post-mutation verifier: scans simulating bodies for NaN/inf transforms, exploding velocities (> threshold), and interpenetration overlaps; returns machine codes per offender — the validate-after-mutate safety check for physics.

tools.name: physics_undo
tools.parity: Unity undo/redo (steal); Epic only does per-call undo
tools.description: Undo/redo/checkpoint wrapper scoped to the physics transaction journal so destructive ops (fracture, bake, collision-gen) revert as a unit — bridges to the cross-cutting 4C transaction seam.

domains.summary: UE animation authoring is a deep, under-served surface: only GenOrca covers ControlRig + retarget at all, and Epic's baseline ships none of it. The repo already has a working C++ FHaybaMCPAnimationHandler (5 AnimBP state-machine commands) with zero first-class wrappers — Theme-2 debt we surface cheaply. Strategy: (1) lead with inspection-first read tools (Flop pattern) so the agent never edits blind; (2) wrap the existing C++ state-machine commands; (3) put the bulk of net-new authoring (notifies, curves, sync markers, sockets, virtual bones, blendspace/montage creation, IK Rig/Retargeter, ControlRig bake) on python_run via unreal.AnimationLibrary / IKRigController / IKRetargeterController / ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary — no plugin rebuild; (4) make the batch-retarget pipeline (source→target skeleton) and the bake-to-anim-sequence ops our headline moat tools, both routed through the job-envelope so they cannot freeze the editor. Every write tool is paired with an *_inspect readback and a viewport/preview-render verify, and ControlRig/BlendSpace are honestly scoped to template-instantiation + param packs (rig-graph and sample-graph authoring are genuine UE Python ceilings, flagged not net-new).
dependencies: UE 5.7 Python: unreal.AnimationLibrary (notifies/curves/sync/virtual-bones/retarget-options), unreal.IKRigController + IKRetargeterController + IKRetargetBatchOperation, unreal.ControlRigBlueprint hierarchy_controller + ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary, BlendSpaceFactory1D/BlendSpaceFactory, AnimBlueprintFactory/AnimMontageFactory/ControlRigBlueprintFactory, AssetTools/AssetRegistry, SequencerScripting
Engine plugins enabled at load: IKRig, ControlRig + ControlRigDeveloper, SequencerScripting, AnimationModifierLibrary
Existing C++ FHaybaMCPAnimationHandler (anim_blueprint_get_info/add_state/add_transition/set_condition/compile) — needs first-class TS wrappers + sidecar.json entries
Theme 0 job-envelope (async command conversion in docs/audit/2026-06-22-mcp-async-command-conversions.md) for batch retarget + bakes; RunSync seam (FHaybaGameThread) for AnimBP compile
Theme 1 add-a-tool refactor: pyTemplate descriptor factory + auto-collected descriptors[] so the python-backed tools ship with no rebuild
Theme 4C transaction/undo C++ handler (FScopedTransaction) for anim_checkpoint and to transaction-wrap the C++ state-machine + set_animation handlers
Vision loop tools (editor_capture_viewport, render_camera, auto-frame) for preview/PIE verify
PLUMB validator (validator_run) for anim_validate
risks: ControlRig rig-GRAPH (RigVM) authoring is NOT exposed to UE Python — only hierarchy + bake are scriptable. Must be flagged as engine limitation, never advertised as full ControlRig authoring (honesty invariant).
BlendSpace per-sample graph editing is partly C++-only in UE Python; blendspace_add_sample may need a C++ fallback in AnimationHandler — design returns 'deferred' rather than silently failing.

Long ops (anim_retarget_batch, control_rig_bake_to_sequence) are game-thread-heavy and WILL freeze the editor if synchronous — they MUST go through the job-envelope; do not ship them as blocking python_run calls.
AnimBP compile blocks the game thread; route via RunSync seam + align executor timeout to UE ceiling, else the Theme-0 freeze bug recurs.

Skeleton mismatch (sequence vs target skeleton, retarget root unset, name-mismatched chains) causes silent no-ops in UE — anim_validate must catch these before mutate, and every write tool returns a readback.
Montage section/next-link editing and state BoundGraph anim assignment have thin/absent Python setters; anim_state_set_animation is correctly placed in C++.
BoundGraph/state-graph edits via C++ FGraphNodeCreator can crash on malformed graphs — keep them under the ProcessCommand SEH guard (Theme 0) and transaction-wrap.
UE 5.7 enum churn already bit this handler (EAnimStateType::AST_State removed); ControlRig/IKRig Python API also drifts across 5.x — pin tested API and degrade gracefully across versions.
domains.test_plan: "Use a project with the UE5 Mannequin set (SK_Mannequin/SK_Quinn, ABP_Manny, IK_Mannequin + RTG_Manny-to-Quinn). 1) Read path: anim_blueprint_inspect(ABP_Manny), anim_sequence_inspect(MM_Run), skeleton_inspect(SK_Mannequin), ik_retargeter_inspect(RTG_*) — confirm states/curves/chains print and match the editor. 2) AnimBP edits: anim_blueprint_create a fresh ABP for SK_Mannequin, anim_state_add Idle+Run, anim_transition_add Idle->Run, anim_transition_set_condition true, anim_blueprint_compile -> assert error_count==0; re-inspect to confirm states persisted (readback). 3) Pure-python edits: blendspace_create 2D Speed/Direction, montage_create from MM_Attack on slot DefaultSlot, anim_notify_add a 'footstep' at 0.3s on MM_Run then anim_sequence_inspect to confirm the notify; anim_curve_add an IKWeight curve; skeleton_add_socket weapon_r on hand_r. 4) Retarget moat: ik_rig_create + ik_rig_add_chain on a custom mesh OR use stock rigs; anim_retarget_batch RTG_Manny-to-Quinn over [MM_Run,MM_Idle] dry_run=true (inspect plan), then commit -> assert new AnimSequences exist under dest and play on Quinn. 5) ControlRig: control_rig_create_from_template FK rig for SK_Mannequin; control_rig_bake_to_sequence on a small level sequence -> assert AnimSequence written. 6) Verify/vision: anim_preview_render(SK_Quinn, retargeted MM_Run, orbit) returns PNG blocks showing correct pose; anim_play_in_editor_test samples 4 frames in PIE. 7) Safety: anim_checkpoint begin -> make a bad edit -> anim_validate flags it -> rollback restores in ONE undo (Ctrl+Z parity). Watch editor_stream_log + hayba_journal_tail throughout to confirm no game-thread freeze on batch/bake ops and that SEH guard catches any malformed-graph crash."

tools.description: Read an AnimSequence: play length, frame rate, num frames, bone tracks, float curves, notifies, sync markers, additive settings — the prereq for every notify/curve/retarget edit.

tools.name: skeleton_inspect

tools.name: anim_blueprint_compile

tools.name: anim_blueprint_add_variable

tools.name: anim_notify_add
tools.signature: (anim_path, notify_name, time_s, duration_s?, notify_class?, track?) -> {ok, notify_id}
tools.description: Add a notify event or notify-state at a time on a sequence/montage (footsteps, VFX, combat windows) — high-value pure-python edit, no rebuild.
