tools.description: Return errors/warnings/blueprint-runtime-errors emitted during the current PIE session; turns 'it played' into a real runtime-error gate.

tools.name: pie_press_key
tools.description: Inject a key press/release/tap into the PIE viewport; lowest-level input primitive for movement and actions.

tools.name: pie_input_action
tools.description: Trigger a named Enhanced Input action (or legacy action mapping) on the player controller; tests gameplay by intent, not raw keys.

tools.name: pie_input_axis
tools.signature: (axis_name, value, duration_ms?, controller_index?) -> {dispatched, axis, value, duration_ms}
tools.description: Apply a named axis input (e.g. MoveForward=1.0) for a duration; drives continuous movement deterministically.

tools.name: pie_mouse
tools.signature: (op='move'|'click'|'drag', x, y, x2?, y2?, button?='left', held_ms?) -> {dispatched, op}
tools.description: Move/click/drag the mouse in the PIE viewport at screen or world-projected coords; covers aim, look, and UI interaction.

tools.name: pie_input_sequence
tools.description: Replay an ordered macro of timed key/axis/mouse events as one call; the ergonomic vehicle for scripted playthroughs.

tools.name: pie_get_player_state
tools.signature: (controller_index?, props?[]) -> {pawn_path, location, rotation, velocity, controller, props{}}
tools.description: Read the player pawn/controller: transform, velocity, possessed class, and selected gameplay props; inspection before/after input.

tools.name: pie_get_actors
tools.signature: (class_filter?, tag?, name_contains?, limit?, offset?) -> {actors[], count, has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: Query actors in the PIE world by class/tag/name with transforms, paginated; the runtime hierarchy read that mirrors editor introspection.

tools.name: pie_spawn_actor
tools.description: Spawn an actor into the transient PIE world at a transform; sets up test fixtures (triggers, targets, props) at runtime.

tools.name: pie_teleport_player
tools.description: Move the player pawn to a location or onto a named actor; positions the player for a specific test without manual driving.

tools.name: pie_possess
tools.description: Possess an existing pawn or spawn-and-possess a pawn class for the player controller; swaps the test subject mid-session.

tools.name: pie_line_trace
tools.signature: (start, end|direction+length, channel?, complex?) -> {hit, actor_path?, location?, normal?, distance?}
tools.description: Cast a ray in the PIE world and return the first hit (actor/component/location/normal); verifies ground, line-of-sight, weapon hits.

tools.name: pie_overlap_query
tools.description: Sphere/box overlap test at a point and return overlapping actors; confirms triggers fired and spawns landed correctly.

tools.name: pie_capture_stats
tools.signature: (samples?, interval_ms?) -> {fps, frame_ms, game_ms, render_ms, gpu_ms, mem_mb}
tools.description: Snapshot runtime perf (fps, frame_ms, game/render/gpu ms, memory) from stat unit; turns PIE into a lightweight perf gate.

tools.name: pie_screenshot_diff
tools.parity: Flop pixel-diff; moat = local + CLIP + image blocks
tools.signature: (baseline_path, threshold?, region?) -> {diff_score, passed, baseline_block, actual_block, diff_block}
tools.description: Capture the PIE viewport and pixel-diff it against a committed baseline, returning a score plus both/diff images; closed-loop visual regression.

tools.name: pie_step_frames
tools.description: Advance the PIE world by N frames (or seconds) while paused, for deterministic frame-exact assertions; tames real-time flakiness.

tools.name: pie_set_time_dilation
tools.description: Set global time dilation (slomo/fast-forward) in the PIE world for deterministic or fast test execution.

tools.name: pie_pause
tools.description: Pause or resume the PIE simulation so state can be inspected without time advancing; debugging companion to step_frames.

tools.name: pie_console_command
tools.description: Run a console command in the PIE world (stat, show, cheats, ke); reaches gameplay debug surfaces no typed tool covers.

tools.name: pie_watch_property
tools.signature: (actor_path, property_name, duration_ms, sample_hz?) -> {series:[{t,value}], min, max, last}
tools.description: Sample an actor property every frame over a window and return the timeseries; debugs gameplay values that change over time (health drain, charge).

tools.name: pie_eval
tools.description: Execute scoped python inside the PIE world context for one-off probes the typed tools miss; the hardened escape hatch.

tools.name: functional_test_run
tools.parity: remiphilippe/Flop gauntlet; matches their DevOps loop
tools.description: Load a map and run UE FunctionalTest actors (gauntlet-style in-level tests) as a polled job; covers level-driven scenarios beyond unit tests.

tools.name: test_plan_dry_run
tools.parity: Flop bp_dry_run; moat = quantified PLUMB validation
tools.description: Validate a declarative test plan (steps + assertions) through PLUMB without executing it; the dry-run-before-commit moat applied to testing.

tools.name: pie_run_scenario
tools.module: python_run-backed TS orchestrator (composes pie_* + test tools)
tools.parity: Flop pie_test_bp (one-shot); moat = non-blocking + vision diff + journaled
tools.description: One outcome verb that starts PIE, replays an input macro, evaluates an assertion list, captures before/after vision diff, stops, and returns a single journaled report; the bundled playtest differentiator.

tools.name: test_history
tools.description: Recall the last N test/scenario runs from the journal with pass/fail and timing; lessons-as-memory for flaky-test triage.

domains.domain: project-build-cook-packaging (DevOps loop: compile, cook, stage, pak, package, deploy/launch, project/config/plugin management, automation tests, and the async-job registry that makes all of it non-freezing)
domains.summary: This domain is where Hayba either matches remiphilippe's full headless DevOps loop or stays an authoring-only toy. The decisive move is to land the planned async-job registry (FHaybaAsyncJobRegistry + a *_job_status reader) FIRST: every long subprocess (UBT compile, cook, UAT BuildCookRun) must return a {job_id, status:"running"} envelope immediately instead of WaitFor-blocking the game thread (the two P0 editor-freeze bugs). Because python_run handlers also run on the game thread, long subprocess launches CANNOT live in python — build/cook/package/launch stay C++ behind the shared registry (this is the crash-resilience moat, productized). python_run is reserved for the no-rebuild config/inspection/validation tools (project settings, maps, asset validation, DDC, Live Coding compile). Every write tool ships a paired *_inspect read-back and honors dry-run + Plan-Mode + validate-before-cook (PLUMB-aligned) so the loop is verifiable, not fire-and-forget.
dependencies: FHaybaAsyncJobRegistry: a shared C++ async-job registry (TMap<FString,FJobState> + FCriticalSection + FProcHandle ownership) is the hard prerequisite for ALL P0 build/cook/package/test tools — it does not exist yet (planned in docs/audit/2026-06-22-mcp-async-command-conversions.md). Nothing in this domain ships safely until it lands.

THEME 0 unfreeze: build_project/build_cook/test_run currently WaitFor-block the game thread (HaybaMCPBuildHandler.cpp RunOrBackground ~L248, HaybaMCPTestHandler.cpp ~L221). These must be converted to job-envelope before any net-new tool here.
THEME 1 add-a-tool refactor + pyTemplate factory: required so the ~18 python_run-backed tools land as descriptors without per-tool 7-file churn / plugin rebuilds.
SEH-wrap ProcessCommand: subprocess launch + config writes touch the whole 33-handler surface; the moat depends on the one-seam SEH extension.
Plan-Mode gate (bPlanApproved) + DisabledTools filter for the destructive tools (project_set_setting, project_plugin_enable, project_set_packaging_settings, package_*, build_clean).
UE installed-platform SDKs (Win64 always; Android/iOS/Linux/console SDKs gate build_target_list output and launch_on_device).
RunUAT.bat / UnrealBuildTool.exe / UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe present in EngineDir (already resolved in HaybaMCPBuildHandler.cpp ResolveUBTPath/ResolveRunUATPath/ResolveEditorExe).
python_run hardened gate (SEH + 3-tier security + dangling-delegate gate) for the config/validation/inspection tools.
UEditorValidatorSubsystem availability for project_validate_assets; AssetRegistry fully scanned for cook_inspect/cook_validate/project_maps_list.
risks: Game-thread deadlock: python_run runs on the game thread, so a long subprocess launched from python would freeze the editor exactly like the bugs we are fixing. Mitigation: ALL long subprocess ops (build/cook/package/launch/pak/archive) stay C++ behind FHaybaAsyncJobRegistry; python_run tools are restricted to fast, in-process config/inspection/validation only.

Late-response crash (bug_haybamcp_tcpserver_late_response_crash): if a build returns synchronously and the client disconnects before reply, AV at HaybaMCPTcpServer.cpp:123. The job-envelope pattern (return job_id immediately, poll later) is precisely what avoids this — but build_job_wait must NOT reintroduce a long blocking reply.

Duplicate destructive launches: the executor's blind retry could fire two package/build jobs. build/cook/package/launch must be marked non-idempotent and excluded from auto-retry; job_id dedupe in the registry.
Orphaned child processes: a cancelled or editor-crashed job can leave detached UAT/cook processes. Registry must own FProcHandle and kill the process tree on cancel + on plugin shutdown.
UAT BuildCookRun is slow (minutes-to-tens-of-minutes) and noisy; log_excerpt must stay bounded (16KB) and tail be offset-paginated to avoid blowing the 1MB frame cap / token budget.
Config writes (project_set_setting/plugin_enable/packaging_settings) often require an editor restart to take effect — must be honestly flagged requires_restart, never silently 'applied'.
Cross-platform path/SDK assumptions: ResolveEditorExe is Win64-only today; launch_on_device / non-Win64 builds will fail confusingly without SDK presence checks (surface via build_target_list).
python-based cook_inspect/package_inspect read disk that a concurrent cook is still writing — must tolerate partial/locked files and report 'in_progress' rather than crash.
EngineVersion is pinned 5.7.0 and some handlers include engine-private headers — UAT/UBT CLI flags drift across 5.6-5.8; pin-test the command lines per engine version.
domains.test_plan: "Run against a live editor with a small real project (the worldbuilding sample). 1) Land FHaybaAsyncJobRegistry; smoke build_project -> assert it returns {job_id,status:'running'} in <2s and the editor stays responsive (issue a second cheap command like project_inspect during the build and confirm it returns). 2) Poll build_job_status until status:'done' with exit_code 0; cross-check against hayba_journal_tail. 3) build_job_cancel a fresh build -> confirm child process is gone (no orphan UnrealBuildTool.exe in task list) and status:'cancelled'. 4) build_job_list shows the running then completed job; build_job_tail returns monotonically increasing offsets, no dupes. 5) project_validate_assets on /Game -> seed one broken reference, confirm it appears in errors; cook_validate flags the same missing ref WITHOUT a full cook. 6) cook_content for Windows -> poll to done -> cook_inspect reports cooked_assets>0 and a real output_dir; build_artifacts_inspect shows the cooked_mb delta. 7) package_project dry_run=true first -> eyeball the resolved UAT command line; then real run -> package_inspect confirms executable + .pak manifest + total_size_mb; launch_standalone on the cooked build boots and capture_viewport/editor_stream_log shows it running. 8) project_set_setting with dry_run=true -> assert old/new echoed and nothing written; then real write -> project_get_setting reads back the new value and requires_restart is honest. 9) project_plugin_enable dry_run -> .uproject untouched; real -> descriptor reflects the change. 10) test_run on a known-passing + known-failing automation filter -> test_get_log returns correct pass/fail counts; confirm the editor never freezes for the old 120s window. 11) Negative: kill the editor mid-cook, reconnect, build_job_list surfaces the orphaned job state (or honestly reports it lost) and no zombie process remains. 12) ci_build_cook_package end-to-end with run_tests=true on a clean checkout -> single parent job_id walks build->cook->package stages, fail-fast verified by injecting a compile error."

tools.name: build_job_status
tools.parity: net-new moat (Aura promises Cancel but documents no job registry; Epic/Flop are game-thread-serial)
tools.description: Poll a job_id from any build/cook/package/test launch -> status, exit_code, bounded log_excerpt; the read-back half of the async-job seam that stops the editor freezing.

tools.name: build_job_list
tools.signature: (state?='all'|'running'|'done', limit?=20, offset?=0) -> {jobs:[{job_id, op, status, started_at, duration_ms}], has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: List active and recent jobs with status/age/op-name; lets the agent discover orphaned/running jobs after a reconnect instead of guessing job_ids.

tools.name: build_job_cancel
tools.parity: Aura (Cancel) — we make it real + local
tools.description: Terminate a running build/cook/package job (kill the child process tree); the Cancel() Aura advertises but Hayba can actually back with a real PID handle.

tools.name: build_job_tail
tools.description: Offset-paginated incremental log lines for a running job, so the agent streams progress without re-fetching the whole 16KB excerpt each poll.

tools.name: build_job_wait
tools.module: C++ BuildHandler (ticker-driven; reuses idle-handler deferred pattern)
tools.description: Cooperative non-blocking wait: returns the latest job state once status changes or a short deadline elapses (never blocks the game thread); convenience over manual polling.

tools.name: build_project
tools.parity: remiphilippe (headless build); Epic restarts to add C++
tools.description: Compile the C++ editor or game target via UnrealBuildTool; honest job-envelope rewrap of the existing freezing build_project (the P0 unfreeze).

tools.name: cook_content
tools.description: Cook content for a target platform (iterate/unversioned/maps), job-envelope; the honest rename of build_cook with non-freezing semantics.

tools.name: package_project
tools.parity: remiphilippe (full DevOps loop) — net-new for every authoring-only competitor
tools.signature: (platform?='Win64', configuration?='Shipping', archive_dir?, build?=true, cook?=true, stage?=true, pak?=true, dry_run?=false) -> {ok, job_id, status:'running'} | {ok, dry_run:true, command_line}
tools.description: Full BuildCookRun via RunUAT (build+cook+stage+pak+archive) — the headline shippable-build verb; supports dry_run to echo the resolved UAT command line before committing.

tools.name: project_inspect
tools.parity: chongdashu/Flop (project info) — we add packaging+platform readback
tools.signature: () -> {project_name, version, engine_version, plugins_enabled:int, target_platforms:[str], game_default_map, packaging_config}
tools.description: Read project identity in one call: name, version, engine version, enabled plugins, target platforms, default/startup maps; the inspection-first anchor for the whole domain (surfaces tier-2 project_get_info).

tools.name: test_run
tools.description: Run automation/functional tests by filter, job-envelope; fixes the 120s/test game-thread freeze and gives the agent a pollable result instead of a frozen editor.

tools.name: test_list
tools.signature: (filter_pattern?, category?, limit?=50, offset?=0) -> {tests:[{name, full_test_path, file_name, line_number}], has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: Enumerate discoverable automation tests with filter + category, paginated; inspection-first pair for test_run so the agent picks real test paths.

tools.name: test_get_log
tools.description: Read structured results of the most recent / a given test job: per-test pass/fail, errors, warnings, durations; the read-back half of test_run.

tools.name: project_validate_assets
tools.parity: net-new moat (validate-before-cook; closest is Flop auto-repair)
tools.signature: (path?='/Game', recursive?=true, fix?=false, limit?=100) -> {ok, validated:int, errors:[{asset, message}], warnings:[{asset, message}], has_more}
tools.description: Run the Editor Validation subsystem (validate_assets_with_settings) over a path before cook/package — validate-before-mutate, catches missing refs/cook-blockers cheaply; PLUMB-aligned safety gate.

tools.name: cook_inspect
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (filesystem scan of Saved/Cooked + AssetRegistry) — no rebuild
tools.parity: remiphilippe (cook status) — most competitors have none
tools.description: Read cook output without re-cooking: cooked-asset count, failures, per-platform output dir, last cook timestamp/DDC stats; verify a cook actually produced content.

tools.name: package_inspect
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (filesystem + pak manifest read) — no rebuild
tools.signature: (archive_dir?) -> {ok, platform, executable, total_size_mb, pak_files:[{name, size_mb}], staged_maps:[str]}
tools.description: Read the last packaged build: archive dir, platform, total size, .pak/.utoc manifest summary, executable path; confirms the shippable artifact exists and is sane.

tools.name: build_artifacts_inspect
tools.signature: () -> {binaries:[{name, mtime}], intermediate_mb, cooked_mb, staged_mb, archives:[{path, size_mb}]}
tools.description: Disk-level read-back of all build outputs (Binaries, Intermediate size, Saved/Cooked, Staged, archive) so the agent verifies state and spots stale/oversized artifacts before re-running.

tools.name: build_target_list
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (Source/*.Target.cs parse + unreal.get_target_platforms) — no rebuild
tools.description: Introspect available build targets, configurations and platforms by parsing *.Target.cs + installed platform SDKs; inspection-first so build/package params are never guessed.

tools.name: build_live_coding
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (console command LiveCoding.Compile) — no rebuild
tools.description: Trigger a Live Coding (hot-reload) compile of game modules without a full rebuild — the fast iteration loop Aura sells as self-correcting live-compile, here as a one-liner console invoke.

tools.name: build_generate_project_files
tools.description: Regenerate IDE/project files via RunUAT GenerateProjectFiles, job-envelope; honest rewrap of the existing freezing command.

tools.name: package_stage

tools.name: project_get_setting

tools.description: Read a typed config value by ini/section/key (Game/Engine/Editor/Input); inspection-first companion to project_set_setting, surfaces tier-2 project_get_settings.

tools.name: project_set_setting
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (GConfig write + flush) — no rebuild

tools.name: project_plugin_list

domains.summary: Revive the BYOK in-editor AI copilot as a thin-client / fat-server split: the agentic tool-calling loop lives in the Node MCP server (new chat-server.ts over the existing Express app in dashboard/api.ts, reusing the live tool registry, gating, PLUMB validator and journal), and C++ becomes a streaming SSE consumer (rework FHaybaMCPClaudeClient + SHaybaMCPChatPanel, reusing the OnToolCallRecorded seam). The surface is three layers: (1) MCP/sidecar tools for provider+key config, the streaming chat loop, plan-mode gating, and session persistence; (2) introspection/verify/dry-run tools (the unglamorous core) so an agent can configure and self-check the panel without guessing; (3) C++ commands/components for the Slate panel, DPAPI-encrypted key vault, and SSE cancel. We restore llm-client.ts from ac46d40 and the 8-provider catalog (anthropic/openai/groq/openrouter/ollama/lmstudio/mock/custom) into one providers.ts, honoring DisabledTools + archetype tool_filter + Plan-Mode before any destructive tool. Moats pressed: token economy (per-session budget accounting + Code-Mode deferred routing feeding the loop), crash-resilience (loop runs server-side, never on the game thread), secure-local BYOK (DPAPI vault vs competitors' plaintext/cloud), and the vision feedback loop (auto-attach viewport/selection context).
dependencies: llm-client.ts restored from commit ac46d40 (LLMTool/LLMToolCall/LLMResponse, stopReason 'tool_use'|'end_turn') — only correct tool-calling shape in repo history
Single providers.ts merging the 8-provider catalog from 2849a75 presets + 4d47e58 env/baseURL/model maps: mock, anthropic, groq, openrouter, openai, ollama, lmstudio, custom
npm deps @anthropic-ai/sdk and openai added to mcp-tools/hayba-mcp; SSE/streaming added to llm-client.complete
Existing Express app in src/dashboard/api.ts hosts POST /chat/stream via new src/chat/chat-server.ts (registered alongside registerApiRoutes)
Live tool registry + hayba_invoke polymorphic dispatch + Code-Mode/deferred routing — the loop calls tools through the same hardened path, not a parallel one
agents/agent-registry.ts archetype.tool_filter (globToRegex) + DisabledTools for per-session tool scoping
C++ OnToolCallRecorded multicast seam (HaybaMCPModule.h:81) bridged into the SSE trace + panel
HaybaMCPSettings vault: replace plaintext GEditorPerProjectIni ApiKey with Windows DPAPI CryptProtectData/CryptUnprotectData
FHaybaMCPClaudeClient reworked from request/response HTTP to SSE consumer + Cancel(); SHaybaMCPChatPanel wires tool-stream/validator/diff + Preview->Plan panel
PLUMB validator (plumb_validate) + validator_run invoked inside the loop for validate-before/after-mutate
Session/usage persistence store (reuse hayba-memory.db SQLite patterns) for sessions/transcripts/usage; keep DB gitignored
Theme 0/1 gates first: ProcessCommand SEH wrap + add-a-tool descriptor refactor; chat tools ship as descriptors (handler/pyTemplate), no per-tool 7-file churn
risks: Game-thread stall: the loop is server-side (locked) but its tool calls still marshal to the game thread via RunSync; a slow tool can stall UE. Mitigation: align executor timeouts to UE ceilings, gate retries to idempotent tools only, run build/test as job-envelopes (Theme 0).

Secret leakage: keys must never appear in SSE frames, journal, transcripts, or tool args. Mitigation: vault holds the only copy; sidecar reads via local IPC; copilot_key_status returns masked last-4 only.
DPAPI is Windows-only — cross-platform key storage is unsolved (matches plugin's current Win64 pinning); document as a known limitation, fall back to OS keychain later.

Plan-Mode bypass: if any destructive tool runs before bPlanApproved the safety moat is void. Mitigation: gate is enforced server-side in the loop, not in the C++ UI, so it cannot be skipped by a non-UI client.

Streaming/tool-call shape drift across 8 providers (Anthropic blocks vs OpenAI tool_calls vs ollama partial support). Mitigation: normalize in llm-client; copilot_provider_test + model.supports_tools flag gate non-tool models.
Duplicate-server confusion: the chat loop must reuse the single tool registry/gating/validator/journal — re-implementing any of these (as Aura warns) doubles maintenance and risks divergence.
SSE reconnect: editor sleep / port re-discovery can drop the stream mid-loop; client must resume by session_id + last seq, not restart the turn (avoid duplicate destructive ops).
Cost runaway in unattended loops; mitigated by copilot_budget_limit_set halt-on-exceed, but default ceilings must be sane.
domains.test_plan: Live-editor validation: (1) Start the MCP server + open the editor with HaybaMCPToolkit; call copilot_health and confirm sidecar_ok + ue_connected + tools_available>0. (2) copilot_key_set('anthropic', <key>) then copilot_key_status — verify has_key true, masked_tail only, and confirm the on-disk GEditorPerProjectIni value is DPAPI ciphertext (not plaintext); copilot_provider_test returns reachable with latency. (3) copilot_provider_list/model_list populate the panel dropdown. (4) copilot_session_new -> copilot_chat_send('spawn a cube and validate naming') over SSE: observe token frames, a tool_call (actor_spawn) frame, tool_result, and a final transcript; confirm the cube exists in the live level and the tool trace appears in the panel via copilot_tool_trace_tail. (5) Plan-Mode: with a destructive prompt, copilot_plan_preview returns steps with destructive flags + predicted PLUMB validation and requires_approval; confirm NO mutation happened; copilot_plan_approve then re-run and confirm exactly one Ctrl+Z reverts the bundle. (6) copilot_chat_cancel mid-stream — verify generation stops, partial_text returned, and no orphaned tool call. (7) Restart editor, copilot_session_resume + copilot_session_get — transcript + tool trace rehydrate; copilot_budget_get shows non-zero token/cost. (8) copilot_toolset_filter_set(['plumb_*']) then ask for an actor op — confirm the loop refuses (tool not in allowed_tools from copilot_toolset_filter_get). (9) copilot_context_attach(['viewport','selection']) — confirm an image content block reaches the model and influences the reply. (10) Loop ollama/lmstudio locally to prove BYOK/local-only path works air-gapped; copilot_emit_mcp_json produces a config Epic's client accepts.

domains.summary:
UMG is a top-3 gameplay authoring surface entirely absent from the first-class catalog, yet the plugin already ships a working-but-unsurfaced C++ tier-2 handler (HaybaMCPUIHandler.cpp: ui_create_widget / ui_add_element / ui_query) reachable only via hayba_invoke ue_legacy. Fastest moat: (1) wrap those three as honest first-class tools with zero rebuild, then (2) close the real gaps that handler leaves open — it never compiles or saves the WBP, hardcodes top-left CanvasPanel anchors, and has no widget-property/event/animation/batch/named-slot support. The headline parity play is umg_compose_tree: one transactional outcome-verb that builds an entire hierarchy from a single JSON spec (matching Roblox create_ui_tree), with a paired dry-run validator and a single-undo wrapper that beats Epic's per-call undo. Inspection-first reads plus a vision/PIE preview loop make the domain self-verifying. Tree mutation is C++-favored for robustness (WidgetTree + FScopedTransaction); lifecycle, listing, read-back, style convenience, and validation ride on python_run/TS with no rebuild.</summary>
<parameter name="dependencies">["Existing C++ handler HaybaMCPUIHandler.cpp (ui_create_widget/ui_add_element/ui_query) reachable via hayba_invoke ue_legacy — basis for thin TS wrappers","UMG/UMGEditor + Blueprint/WidgetTree + WidgetBlueprintFactory (already included in the handler)","FBlueprintEditorUtils::MarkBlueprintAsStructurallyModified + FKismetEditorUtilities::CompileBlueprint for the missing compile/save step","FScopedTransaction seam from the cross-cutting Transactions/undo domain (4C) for single-undo bundling","Vision-loop tools (editor_capture_viewport / render_camera) and PIE handler (editor_start_pie) for preview/verify","PLUMB validator_run + validator_rules for umg_validate UI checks","Add-a-tool refactor (Theme 1): one descriptor + pyTemplate factory so the python-backed tools land with no per-tool 7-file churn","Plan-Mode gate (bPlanApproved) before destructive ops (delete/remove/reparent)"]
risks: UE Python cannot reliably mutate WidgetTree structure (construct/reparent/rename widgets) — structural tools MUST be C++ in HaybaMCPUIHandler, not python_run; python attempts are flaky across 5.7/5.8
Existing handler MarksBlueprintModified but never compiles or saves — edits silently lost on editor restart; umg_compile + explicit asset save are P0 to make every other tool honest
UMG widget animation authoring and event/property bindings are genuine UE Python ceilings (like Niagara/ControlRig) — scope to template-instantiation + flag as engine limitation; do not over-promise

ApplySlotProps currently force-resets CanvasPanelSlot anchors to top-left and treats w/h as Right/Bottom offsets — naive anchored layouts break; umg_set_anchors must expose true min/max anchors + alignment
ConstructWidget name collisions and AddChild rejection (panel full / incompatible slot, e.g. Button accepts one child) need actionable error codes, not silent failure

Reflection-based set_property (ImportText_Direct) can partially-apply structs (FSlateBrush, FSlateColor, FSlateFontInfo) — needs typed convenience tools (set_brush/set_text/set_style) over raw reflection
Mutating a WBP that is open in the editor can desync the live designer; verify-after-mutate via inspect/read-back
compose_tree in one shot risks half-built trees on mid-spec failure — must run inside FScopedTransaction so a failure rolls back atomically
domains.test_plan: Live-editor loop on a scratch path /Game/UI_MCPTest. 1) umg_widget_create WBP_Test (UserWidget) -> assert asset exists + RootCanvas root; reopen-safe via umg_compile then save. 2) umg_palette_list -> confirm Button/TextBlock/Image/VerticalBox + any custom UserWidget resolve. 3) umg_compose_dry_run a 6-widget spec (Canvas>VBox>{TextBlock,Button>TextBlock,Image}) -> expect ok with resolved classes, no mutation. 4) umg_compose_tree same spec -> umg_widget_inspect and assert hierarchy + slot types match (verify-after-mutate). 5) umg_set_anchors center-stretch on the VBox -> inspect slot offsets/anchors round-trip. 6) umg_set_text + umg_set_brush + umg_set_property(Visibility) -> umg_widget_get_properties read-back confirms each. 7) umg_batch_set_property color across all TextBlocks (class glob) -> read-back count. 8) umg_rename_widget + umg_reparent_widget + umg_remove_widget -> inspect confirms tree delta. 9) umg_transaction wrapping steps 5-7 then a single undo -> inspect confirms all three reverted in ONE Ctrl+Z. 10) umg_preview_capture -> returns PNG content block of the design; umg_preview_in_pie -> add to viewport in PIE + screenshot shows widget. 11) umg_validate -> flags an intentionally off-screen / zero-size / low-contrast widget. 12) Negative: umg_add_widget a 2nd child to a Button (single-child) -> expect actionable error code, not crash; confirm SEH/ProcessCommand keeps editor alive.

domains.domain: Enhanced Input asset authoring (Input Action / Input Mapping Context / triggers / modifiers / key bindings)
domains.summary: Enhanced Input is a hard UE5 design-time gap: every competitor (and Hayba today) only does RUNTIME injection, while IA/IMC asset authoring is unautomated. Hayba already has three unwrapped C++ commands (input_create_action/mapping/add_mapping in HaybaMCPInputHandler) that are not first-class and not in the sidecar, so Step 1 is surfacing that tier-2 debt as proper TS tools; Step 2 fills the whole author loop (inspect, rebind, configure triggers/modifiers, validate, template) mostly via python_run with zero rebuilds. The load-bearing constraint: UInputMappingContext.map_key returns FEnhancedActionKeyMapping by VALUE in UE Python (it is a C++ reference), so trigger/modifier mutation must stay in C++ or rewrite the whole mappings TArray; creation, property-set, and all read-back are pure Python. We lean the crash-resilience, PLUMB-validation, and transactional-undo moats via inspection-first read tools, an input_validate conflict checker, dry-run on every batch op, and one-Ctrl+Z transaction bundling. Net-new moat: an end-to-end design-time to PIE-runtime input loop no other UE MCP closes.
dependencies: EnhancedInput plugin enabled in the target project
Existing HaybaMCPInputHandler C++ commands (input_create_action/input_create_mapping/input_add_mapping) for the reference-semantics trigger/modifier path
Hardened python_run handler (SEH + 3-tier security gate + dangling-delegate gate) for the no-rebuild tools
Theme-1 add-a-tool refactor + pyTemplate factory so these land as single descriptors, not 7-file churn
Theme-4C transaction seam (FScopedTransaction begin/end) for single-undo bundling
PLUMB validator wiring for input_validate conflict rules
EditorAssetLibrary/AssetTools + save_asset for persistence (MarkPackageDirty + PostEditChange + save)
UE 5.3+ for UPlayerMappableKeySettings and UEnhancedInputDeveloperSettings default-context array
Existing pie_input runtime injection tools to close the design->runtime test loop
risks: map_key returns FEnhancedActionKeyMapping by value in Python (C++ returns a reference) -> modifiers/triggers added via the returned struct silently do NOT persist. Gate all trigger/modifier attach to C++ (HaybaMCPInputHandler) or a whole-array rewrite of the IMC 'mappings' TArray.

NewObject for UInputModifier/UInputTrigger must be outered to the owning IMC/IA or it GCs -> dangling-UObject crash class adjacent to #283/#284. Always pass the asset as outer and re-set the array property.
FKey names and validity vary by platform and installed plugins (gamepad, touch, XR). input_list_keys must enumerate live from EKeys at runtime, never ship a static key list.

Modifier/trigger UPROPERTY names differ per class (HoldTimeThreshold, ActuationThreshold, LowerThreshold, etc.). input_list_modifiers/triggers introspection must run BEFORE any *_set_props or the agent guesses wrong names.
PlayerMappableKeySettings API changed 5.1 (FName) -> 5.3 (UPlayerMappableKeySettings object). Version-guard input_set_player_mappable and degrade gracefully.
UEnhancedInputDeveloperSettings default mapping contexts only exist 5.3+ and persist to config; must call save_config / write DefaultInput.ini or the change is lost on restart.
Edits that skip MarkPackageDirty + save_asset are lost on editor restart; every write tool must dirty and the batch tools must save once at end.
Removing/reindexing mappings shifts mapping_index; tools keyed by index must re-resolve by (action,key) to stay stable across a batch.
domains.test_plan: On a live editor, work in a scratch dir /Game/MCPTest/Input. 1) input_action_create IA_Jump(Boolean), IA_Move(Axis2D); input_action_inspect to confirm value_type round-trips. 2) input_context_create IMC_Default. 3) input_map_key IA_Jump=SpaceBar; input_map_key IA_Move for W/S/A/D with Negate + SwizzleAxis modifiers and per-key axis config. 4) input_context_inspect -> confirm 5 mappings with keys, triggers, modifiers persisted; open the IMC asset in the editor UI to visually verify the modifier stack actually saved (this is where the by-value Python bug shows). 5) input_validate -> expect zero issues, then deliberately double-bind SpaceBar and re-run to confirm the duplicate-key conflict is reported. 6) input_remap_key SpaceBar->Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom and re-inspect. 7) input_apply_template fps_kbm with dry_run=true (preview only), then commit, then open assets. 8) Wrap a input_batch_map in input_transaction, then press Ctrl+Z once and confirm the entire batch reverts in a single undo. 9) Save all, restart editor, input_context_inspect again to prove persistence. 10) Close the loop: add IMC_Default via input_set_default_contexts (or BP), enter PIE, fire IA_Jump via the existing pie_input runtime injection, and confirm the action triggers — proving design-time authoring reaches runtime.

tools.name: input_action_create
tools.module: C++ HaybaMCPToolkit/HaybaMCPInputHandler (input_create_action exists) + thin TS wrapper + sidecar entry
tools.parity: net-new moat (only runtime injection exists across all competitors)
tools.description: Create an Input Action asset with a value type (Boolean/Axis1D/2D/3D) plus optional consume/pause/description — the atom every binding references; surfaces the existing-but-unwrapped C++ command.

tools.name: input_context_create
tools.description: Create an empty Input Mapping Context asset — the container that binds actions to keys; wraps the existing unwrapped C++ command.

tools.name: input_map_key
tools.signature: (context_path, action_path, key, triggers?:string[], modifiers?:string[]) -> {mapping_index, key, triggers[], modifiers[], unresolved_classes[]}
tools.description: Bind an action to a key inside an IMC, attaching triggers + modifiers in one call — the core authoring verb; must use the C++ reference path because Python's map_key returns the mapping by value.

tools.name: input_context_inspect
tools.description: Read back every mapping in an IMC (action, key, triggers, modifiers, player-mappable) — inspection-first paired read so the agent verifies state instead of guessing; the primary verify tool.

tools.name: input_action_inspect
tools.description: Read an Input Action's value_type, consume/pause flags, asset-level default triggers/modifiers, and description — verify-before-mutate for IA edits.

tools.name: input_list
tools.signature: (dir?, kind?:Literal[action|context|all], limit?, offset?) -> {items:[{path, kind, value_type?}], has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: List Input Action and Input Mapping Context assets under a path, paginated — discovery without a project scan; default 50/page.

tools.name: input_list_keys
tools.description: Enumerate valid FKey names live from EKeys, filterable by device/category — kills the #1 agent failure of binding to an invalid key string like 'Space' vs 'SpaceBar'.

tools.name: input_validate
tools.description: PLUMB-style conflict checker: duplicate key bindings, unbound actions, key bound to mismatched value-type, missing triggers, cross-context collisions — closed-loop correctness, the worldbuilding-grade moat.

tools.name: input_list_modifiers
tools.description: Enumerate available UInputModifier subclasses with their editable UPROPERTYs and defaults — docs-as-a-tool so the agent knows DeadZone.LowerThreshold etc. before configuring; must run before *_set_props.

tools.name: input_list_triggers
tools.description: Enumerate available UInputTrigger subclasses (Pressed/Released/Hold/Tap/Chorded/Pulse) with editable props — reflection-driven discovery for trigger configuration.

tools.name: input_unmap_key
tools.description: Remove a key binding from an IMC by (action,key) — stable deletion that re-resolves indices; transaction-wrapped.

tools.name: input_remap_key
tools.description: Rebind an existing mapping from old_key to new_key while preserving its triggers/modifiers — the rebinding primitive, the most-requested input edit.

tools.name: input_add_trigger
tools.module: C++ HaybaMCPToolkit/HaybaMCPInputHandler (net-new command) preferred; TS fallback rewrites array
tools.description: Add a configured trigger (e.g. Hold with HoldTimeThreshold=0.5) to a specific mapping — must use C++ or whole-array rewrite due to the by-value map_key bug; this is where Python silently drops edits.

tools.name: input_add_modifier
tools.description: Add a configured modifier (DeadZone, Negate, SwizzleAxis, Scalar) to a mapping — the other half of axis authoring; same by-value caveat as triggers.

tools.name: input_remove_trigger
tools.description: Remove a trigger from a mapping by class or stack index — surgical cleanup of an over-configured binding.

tools.name: input_remove_modifier
tools.description: Remove a modifier from a mapping by class or stack index — surgical cleanup.

tools.name: input_set_trigger_props
tools.description: Edit UPROPERTYs of an existing trigger instance on a mapping (e.g. tweak ActuationThreshold) without rebuilding the stack — fine-grained tuning.

tools.name: input_set_modifier_props
tools.description: Edit UPROPERTYs of an existing modifier instance on a mapping (e.g. DeadZone thresholds) in place — fine-grained tuning.

tools.name: input_action_set_props
tools.description: Set Input Action asset properties (value_type, consume_input, trigger_when_paused, reserve_all_mappings, description) with save — batch property authoring for IAs.

tools.name: input_action_set_default_triggers
tools.description: Set the asset-level default triggers/modifiers carried by an Input Action itself (UE5.1+), applied to every mapping that uses it — reduces per-binding repetition.

tools.name: input_batch_map
tools.parity: matches Roblox mass_* batch verbs; net-new for Enhanced Input
tools.signature: (context_path, rows:[{action_path, key, triggers?, modifiers?}], dry_run?) -> {mapped, skipped, conflicts[], preview?}
tools.description: Map many action->key rows (each with triggers/modifiers) into an IMC in one transaction with dry_run preview — outcome-verb that authors a whole scheme in a single call and one undo.

tools.name: input_apply_template
tools.description: Scaffold a complete input scheme (fps_kbm, twin_stick_gamepad, topdown_kbm, platformer, vehicle) creating the IAs + IMC mappings + axis modifiers in one outcome call with dry_run — the 'create a working control scheme' headline verb.

tools.name: input_clone_context
tools.description: Duplicate an IMC to a new path, optionally remapping a whole device class (e.g. keyboard WASD -> gamepad stick) — fast keyboard+gamepad parity authoring.

tools.name: input_set_player_mappable
tools.description: Mark a binding as player-rebindable with a mappable name/display-name/category (UPlayerMappableKeySettings, 5.3+) — enables in-game rebind UIs, version-guarded.

tools.name: input_set_default_contexts
tools.description: Register IMCs as project default mapping contexts with priorities via UEnhancedInputDeveloperSettings (5.3+) and persist to config — the design-time hook that makes contexts active at runtime without Blueprint wiring.

tools.name: input_verify_binding
tools.signature: (context_path, action_path, expect_key, expect_triggers?, expect_modifiers?) -> {match:bool, diff:{key?, triggers?, modifiers?}}
tools.description: Assert a binding resolves exactly as expected (key + trigger set + modifier set) and return a structured diff — read-back verification primitive for agent self-correction and CI.

tools.name: input_mapping_diff
tools.description: Diff two IMCs (or before/after of one edit) returning added/removed/changed mappings — supports the vision-loop before/after pattern and review of agent edits.

tools.name: input_transaction
tools.parity: net-new moat vs Epic per-call undo
tools.description: Bundle a sequence of input edits into ONE FScopedTransaction so the entire scheme reverts with a single Ctrl+Z — the named differentiator vs Epic per-call undo, applied to the input domain.

tools.name: input_action_create_batch
tools.parity: matches Roblox mass_create_objects; net-new for Enhanced Input
tools.description: Create many Input Actions in one call (name + value_type + description rows) in a single transaction — bulk IA scaffolding before mapping.

tools.name: input_rename
tools.description: Rename/move an IA or IMC asset, fixing up references — unglamorous lifecycle housekeeping.

tools.name: input_delete
tools.description: Delete an IA or IMC with referencer check and dry_run, Plan-Mode gated — safe destructive cleanup that warns if a context still references the action.

tools.name: input_export_scheme
tools.description: Export an IMC (+ referenced IAs) to a portable JSON scheme for docs, review, or round-trip — enables versionable, diffable input design.

tools.name: input_import_scheme
tools.description: Author a full IMC + IAs from an exported/hand-written JSON scheme in one transaction with dry_run — declarative, idempotent input authoring (pairs with export).

domains.domain: AI / Navigation — Behavior Trees, Blackboards, NavMesh build/bounds, EQS, NavLink, AIController/Pawn perception
domains.summary: This domain has a buried C++ asset (HaybaMCPBehaviorTreeHandler: bt_get_info/add_node/connect/compile) with no first-class wrapper, and zero coverage for Blackboards, NavMesh, EQS, NavLink, and perception — a complete competitive gap (only GenOrca touches BT/EQS at all; nobody documents NavMesh/perception). Strategy: (1) immediately surface the 4 stranded C++ BT commands as thin executeCommand wrappers (no rebuild, Theme 2 debt) with inspection-first read tools; (2) build the rest as python_run-backed pyTemplate descriptors over NavigationSystemV1, AIBlueprintHelperLibrary, AssetTools, and EditorActorSubsystem — no plugin rebuild; (3) lead with outcome-verbs (bt_build_from_spec → ONE undo, nav_setup → bounds+build+verify) and readback/verify tools (navmesh_project_point, navmesh_find_path) that prove the AI actually navigates, which is the credibility moat here. Every write tool ships a paired *_inspect, runs through PLUMB/validator, and wraps a transaction so multi-step BT authoring collapses into a single Ctrl+Z — directly beating Epic's per-call undo. Perception and EQS run-tools close the loop by executing in PIE and returning scored/perceived results as structured data plus optional vision capture.
dependencies: NavigationSystem + AIModule plugins enabled in the project (RecastNavMesh, NavMeshBoundsVolume, AIController)
python_run hardened handler (SEH + security gate) — vehicle for ~26 of these tools with no rebuild
Existing C++ HaybaMCPBehaviorTreeHandler (bt_get_info/add_node/connect/compile) for the 4 thin wrappers + future bt_remove/set-property C++ additions
Add-a-tool refactor (Theme 1): ToolDescriptor with pyTemplate factory + auto-collected descriptors[] barrel + generated sidecar
executeCommand/tool-executor.ts (ue_command + ue_legacy dispatch) and Code-Mode/deferred routing pack registration so these land behind hayba_invoke, not the eager surface
editor_start_pie + editor_capture_viewport/render_camera for PIE-time perception/EQS/path validation and vision feedback
PLUMB validator + transaction (FScopedTransaction) seam for begin/commit/undo bundling
unreal Python: NavigationSystemV1, AIBlueprintHelperLibrary, EnvQueryManager, AssetToolsHelpers, EditorActorSubsystem, EditorAssetLibrary
risks: UE Python cannot author EQS generator/test graphs or BTService logic from scratch — like Niagara/ControlRig this is an engine limit; scope EQS/BT-service tools to template-instantiation + parameter packs and flag as engine limitation honestly (no second not_implemented_in_v1).
NavMesh build can be long-running and game-thread-bound — must go through the Theme-0 job-envelope/async pattern, not a blocking 300s call, or it freezes the editor like build_*/test_run.
Perception/EQS/path queries are only meaningful at runtime — many require PIE; editor-time calls return stale or empty results. Tools must declare requires_pie and gate accordingly.

BT node identity uses deterministic GUIDs derived from path (GuidForNode); renaming/reparenting changes the path and invalidates cached GUIDs across calls — readback after every mutation, never cache GUIDs across structural edits.

NavMeshBoundsVolume sizing wrong (too small/large) silently yields no navigable area; nav_setup must verify coverage>0 and return actionable error, mirroring the PCG SurfaceSampler-needs-Landscape footgun.

NavLinkProxy and AIPerceptionComponent often need a Blueprint/Pawn class rather than a placed actor instance to persist; component-add on a transient PIE actor won't save — target the asset/CDO where persistence is required.
Decorator-on-task attachment is constrained in the C++ handler (requires composite parent); pyTemplate authoring must mirror those rules or produce confusing failures.
domains.test_plan: On a live editor with a navigable test level: (1) blackboard_create + blackboard_add_key (Bool 'HasTarget', Object 'TargetActor', Vector 'MoveTo'); blackboard_inspect confirms keys/types. (2) bt_create bound to that blackboard; bt_build_from_spec to author Selector>Sequence>MoveTo+Wait with a Blackboard decorator in one call; bt_inspect (wraps bt_get_info) confirms node tree + parent GUIDs; bt_validate (wraps bt_compile) returns ok=true, errors=[]. Undo once — entire BT structure reverts (single-Ctrl+Z proof). (3) nav_setup over the level bounds → navmesh_inspect shows tiles>0 and area>0; navmesh_project_point on a floor point returns a near point with on_navmesh=true; navmesh_find_path between two floor points returns is_partial=false and length>0; intentionally pick an unreachable point and confirm is_partial/no_path. (4) ai_spawn_controller possessing a test pawn + ai_run_behavior_tree with the authored BT; start PIE via editor_start_pie; ai_set_blackboard_value sets HasTarget=true and the pawn moves; editor_capture_viewport screenshots motion. (5) ai_perception_configure adds a sight sense to the pawn; in PIE ai_perception_query returns the seen target actor. (6) eqs_create from a template + eqs_run at a context location returns scored items sorted by score. Cross-check every read tool's JSON against the in-editor BT/Blackboard/Nav debug views; run validator_run before/after each mutating call.

tools.name: bt_inspect
tools.parity: GenOrca (BT depth); net-new as a first-class wrapper (C++ command was stranded)
tools.description: Read a Behavior Tree's full node tree, blackboard binding, and per-node GUID/class/children — the inspection-first read every BT edit verifies against.

tools.name: bt_add_node
tools.description: Add one composite/task/decorator/service node to a BT under a parent GUID, with class+kind sanity checks — surfaces the buried C++ authoring command.

tools.name: bt_connect
tools.description: Attach an existing BT node as a child of a composite, with built-in cycle rejection — prevents the stack-overflow crash class on later walks.

tools.name: bt_validate
tools.description: Validate/compile a BT (root present, blackboard bound, kismet errors if backed by BP) and return errors/warnings — dry-run gate before relying on the tree.

tools.name: bt_create
tools.parity: net-new moat (no competitor creates BT assets)
tools.description: Create a new BehaviorTree asset, optionally creating+binding a BlackboardData in the same call — the entry point for AI authoring.

tools.name: bt_build_from_spec
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor wrapping bt_add_node/bt_connect under FScopedTransaction (HaybaMCPToolkit transaction seam)
tools.parity: net-new moat (single-undo bundling beats Epic per-call undo)
tools.description: Author an entire BT (composites/tasks/decorators/services + blackboard bindings) from one JSON spec inside a single transaction → ONE Ctrl+Z. Outcome-verb over the low-level add/connect calls.

tools.name: bt_set_node_property
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor (resolve node by deterministic GUID, set_editor_property)
tools.description: Set properties on a BT node by GUID (e.g., MoveTo acceptable radius, Wait time, blackboard key selectors) — the missing 'configure' half of node authoring.

tools.name: bt_set_decorator
tools.description: Configure a Blackboard-based decorator (observed key, key query, operation, notify-observer mode) on a node — the most common BT condition wiring.

tools.name: bt_remove_node
tools.description: Remove a BT node (and its subtree/decorators/services) by GUID inside a transaction — the destructive counterpart, Plan-Mode gated.

tools.name: bt_list_node_classes
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor (iterate UClass subclasses, paginated)
tools.description: List available BTTask/BTDecorator/BTService/BTComposite subclasses (engine + project) for use as node_class_name — introspection so the agent stops guessing class paths.

tools.name: blackboard_create
tools.description: Create a BlackboardData asset, optionally inheriting a parent blackboard — required substrate for any BT.

tools.name: blackboard_add_key
tools.description: Add a typed key (Bool/Int/Float/Vector/Rotator/Name/String/Object/Class/Enum) with optional instance-sync — the data the whole BT reads/writes.

tools.name: blackboard_remove_key
tools.description: Remove a blackboard key by name inside a transaction, warning if BT decorators reference it — destructive, Plan-Mode gated.

tools.name: blackboard_inspect
tools.description: List all keys (name/type/base-class/instance-synced) of a BlackboardData — paired read for every blackboard mutation.

tools.name: navmesh_add_bounds_volume
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor (EditorActorSubsystem.spawn_actor_from_class NavMeshBoundsVolume + brush extent)
tools.description: Spawn/resize a NavMeshBoundsVolume to cover given bounds or the whole level — without this NavMesh silently builds nothing (the AI equivalent of the PCG-needs-Landscape footgun).

tools.name: navmesh_build
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor over the Theme-0 job-envelope (NavigationSystemV1.build / Build Paths)
tools.parity: remiphilippe (headless build loop); net-new for nav
tools.description: Rebuild navigation data (dirty or full) via the async job-envelope, returning a job id — never blocks the game thread like the legacy build freezes.

tools.name: navmesh_inspect
tools.description: Report nav coverage: bounds volumes, RecastNavMesh tiles built, navigable area, agent config, and whether a probe point is reachable — proof the navmesh exists and is usable.

tools.name: navmesh_set_config
tools.signature: (agent_radius?, agent_height?, agent_max_step?, cell_size?, tile_size?, runtime_generation?) -> {ok, applied{}}
tools.description: Set RecastNavMesh agent radius/height/step/cell-size/tile-size and runtime-generation mode, then mark dirty — tunes nav to the pawn before rebuild.

tools.name: navmesh_project_point
tools.description: Project a world point onto the navmesh within a query extent and return the nearest navigable point — core readback/verify for placement and pathing.

tools.name: navmesh_find_path
tools.description: Test pathfinding between two points and return length, point list, and partial/no-path flags — verifies the navmesh is actually traversable, not just present.

tools.name: navmesh_random_reachable_point
tools.parity: Roblox character_navigation (loose analog); net-new for UE
tools.description: Sample a random navigable point reachable within a radius of an origin — spawn-point selection and reachability sanity checks.

tools.name: nav_setup
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor composing add_bounds_volume + build + inspect (transactional)
tools.description: One outcome-verb: add a bounds volume over the level, build navigation, and verify coverage>0 — fails loudly if the level produces no navmesh.

tools.name: ai_spawn_controller
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor (EditorActorSubsystem spawn + AIController.possess / AIBlueprintHelperLibrary)
tools.description: Spawn an AIController and possess a target pawn, optionally running a BT immediately — the bridge that makes a pawn act on AI.

tools.name: ai_run_behavior_tree
tools.description: Assign and start a BT on an AIController or pawn (PIE/sim), creating the blackboard component — exercises the authored tree end-to-end.

tools.name: ai_set_blackboard_value
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor (BlackboardComponent.set_value_as_* in PIE world)
tools.description: Set a runtime blackboard value (bool/int/float/vector/object/name) on a running AI during PIE — the primary AI-debug lever to drive/observe behavior.

tools.name: ai_inspect
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor (AIController + BrainComponent + BlackboardComponent introspection)
tools.description: Read AI runtime state for an actor: possessing controller, active BT + current/running task, and all blackboard values — inspection-first for AI debugging.

tools.name: ai_perception_configure
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor (AIPerceptionComponent + AISenseConfig_Sight/Hearing on the asset CDO/BP)
tools.description: Add/configure an AIPerceptionComponent on a pawn/controller class with sight/hearing/damage sense configs (radius, angle, affiliation) — wires what the AI can detect.

tools.name: ai_perception_query
tools.description: Return actors currently perceived by an AI (by sense, with last-stimulus location/age) during PIE — closes the perception loop with verifiable results.

tools.name: navlink_add
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor (spawn NavLinkProxy + PointLinks config)
tools.description: Spawn and configure a NavLinkProxy (simple or smart link) with start/end points, direction, and area class — connects disjoint navmesh regions (jumps/ledges).

tools.name: navlink_inspect
tools.description: List NavLinkProxy actors in the level with their endpoints/direction/area class — paired read + verify links are placed where intended.

tools.name: eqs_create
tools.description: Create an EnvQuery asset from a built-in template/preset (generator + test set), parameterized — works within UE Python's EQS-graph-authoring ceiling (template-scoped, flagged).

tools.name: eqs_run
tools.description: Run an EQS query at a querier/context location and return ranked items with scores — proves the query produces sensible results before BT integration.

tools.name: ai_batch_assign_bt
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor (EditorActorSubsystem query loop, transactional)
tools.parity: Roblox mass_set_property (batch analog); net-new for UE AI
tools.description: Assign one BT (and optional blackboard) to many AIControllers/pawns selected by class/tag/query in a single transaction — batch op for populating a level with behavior.

tools.name: ai_nav_validate
tools.module: python_run-backed TS descriptor feeding the PLUMB/validator pipeline
tools.parity: net-new moat (PLUMB quantified validation extended to AI)
tools.description: Domain validator: cross-checks BT/blackboard/nav/perception consistency (missing blackboard binding, decorator keys not in blackboard, no nav coverage, BT class refs unresolved) and returns an unsat-core style report — PLUMB-style validate-before-commit for AI.

domains.domain: Gameplay Ability System (GAS) — GameplayAbility / GameplayEffect / AttributeSet / AbilitySystemComponent + gameplay-tag-driven ability grants
domains.summary: GAS is "zero coverage" as first-class tools, yet a real C++ plugin already exists (unreal/HaybaMCPGAS/.../HaybaMCPGASHandler.cpp) shipping exactly 4 raw commands (gas_create_ability/grant_ability/create_effect/apply_effect) reachable only via hayba_invoke ue_legacy — so step one is honest first-class wrappers plus inspection/read-back over that surface, step two broadens to the full author loop (AttributeSets, gameplay tags, GameplayCues, ability-set data assets, runtime queries). No competitor (Aura, Flop, GenOrca, UAIP, Epic 5.8) ships GAS authoring at all, so the entire domain is net-new moat; we differentiate with PLUMB validation, transaction-wrapping, and inspection-first ergonomics. Strategy: keep the crash-prone runtime/CDO-mutation ops in C++ (extend the existing handler under the ProcessCommand SEH seam), and push everything authoring/introspection that UE Python's GameplayAbilities reflection plus EditorAssetSubsystem can reach into python_run-backed TS wrappers (no rebuild). Every write tool ships a paired *_inspect read tool and a dry_run flag; tag operations route through the native GameplayTagsManager so we never desync the project tag table.
dependencies: GameplayAbilities plugin enabled in the target project (uplugin dependency)
HaybaMCPGAS plugin module already present and compiled (HaybaMCPGASHandler.cpp ships gas_create_ability/grant_ability/create_effect/apply_effect)
AttributeSet subclasses are C++-defined in the target game (UE Python cannot author new UAttributeSet C++ classes) — attribute-creation tools scope to inspection plus a codegen-stub emitter
GameplayTagsManager + Config/DefaultGameplayTags.ini for tag CRUD
EditorAssetSubsystem / AssetRegistry for asset discovery and CDO default reads
FScopedTransaction undo seam (brief Theme 4C) for wrapping C++ mutations
PLUMB validator + validator_run + hayba_invoke ue_legacy fallthrough
Code-Mode / deferred routing + a new 'gas' pack so the surface stays off the eager context
ProcessCommand SEH wrap (Theme 0) so all GAS C++ handlers are crash-recoverable
Theme 1 add-a-tool descriptor refactor (pyTemplate factory) to land the python wrappers without 7-file churn
risks: GameplayAbilities runtime types (UAbilitySystemComponent, GiveAbility, ApplyGameplayEffectToSelf) are largely NOT exposed to UE Python — most runtime grant/apply/query ops must stay C++ in the existing handler; python wrappers there are passthroughs over ue_legacy, not real python

GAS ASCs normally only exist on PIE/runtime actors; editor-world actors rarely have a live ASC, so grant/apply/query tools must clearly state they target the PIE world or an editor actor that explicitly hosts an ASC, and fail with an actionable message otherwise

New UAttributeSet classes cannot be created from Python (need C++ + recompile) — attribute_create can only emit a C++ stub + edit config; over-promising here would be a second not_implemented_in_v1 honesty violation
Setting CDO defaults on GameplayEffect/Ability blueprints can be lost without MarkPackageDirty + save and a blueprint recompile; read-back verify is mandatory or edits silently no-op

Gameplay tag edits write Config/DefaultGameplayTags.ini and require GameplayTagsManager reload; concurrent/native tags can collide and a malformed tag can corrupt the project tag table — must validate tag strings and dry_run
SetByCaller / ScalableFloat / ModMagnitudeCalculation magnitude types are intricate; a naive float-only modifier API will mislead users into thinking complex magnitudes are supported
ApplyGameplayEffectToSelf with a long-lived ASC during editor (non-PIE) can leak ActiveGameplayEffect handles; apply tools must be PIE-gated or transaction-scoped

Blueprint-graph authoring of ability logic (ActivateAbility event graph) hits the same K2-graph limitation as the broader product — scope ability tools to class creation + CDO/property config + tag wiring, not node-graph logic
domains.test_plan: On a live editor with the GameplayAbilities plugin and a project that has at least one C++ UAttributeSet (e.g. the Lyra/ASC sample or a scratch GAS pawn): (1) gas_inspect to confirm the plugin + ASC classes resolve; (2) gas_ability_create /Game/GAS/GA_Test then gas_ability_inspect to read back the new blueprint CDO (tags, instancing policy) — assert path exists in AssetRegistry; (3) gas_attributeset_list + gas_attribute_list to enumerate the project's C++ attributes, pick Health; (4) gas_effect_create a Duration effect with an Additive Health modifier via gas_effect_add_modifier, then gas_effect_inspect to verify DurationPolicy + modifier read-back; (5) gas_tag_add 'Ability.Test.Fire', gas_tag_list to confirm it landed in DefaultGameplayTags.ini, gas_ability_set_tags to bind it as the ability's AssetTag; (6) enter PIE (editor_start_pie), find the player ASC actor, gas_ability_grant the ability and gas_effect_apply the effect, then gas_asc_inspect / gas_active_effects_list / gas_attribute_get to confirm Health changed and the granted ability spec + active GE handle appear; (7) gas_ability_try_activate by tag and confirm via gas_asc_inspect; (8) run validator_run before/after each mutate and confirm transaction wrapping by issuing an undo; (9) re-run every *_inspect with dry_run on the create tools to confirm no asset is written. Capture editor viewport / PIE screenshot where attribute changes are visible (e.g. a debug HUD) to close the vision loop.

tools.name: gas_inspect
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (EditorUtility + reflection); falls back to gas_describe in HaybaMCPGAS
tools.description: Probe the GAS subsystem: is GameplayAbilities enabled, which AttributeSet/ASC C++ classes exist, count of GA/GE assets and registered gameplay tags. Gating probe so the agent knows the domain is usable before any write.

tools.name: gas_ability_create
tools.module: HaybaMCPGAS (existing GasCreateAbility, add policy/tag params + FScopedTransaction)
tools.signature: (path, name, instancing_policy?, net_execution_policy?, dry_run?) -> {path, name, ok}
tools.description: Create a UGameplayAbility blueprint at a content path with optional instancing/net-execution policy and cost/cooldown effect refs. First-class wrapper over the existing gas_create_ability C++ command (today only via ue_legacy).

tools.name: gas_ability_inspect
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (load BP GeneratedClass CDO, reflect tag containers)
tools.description: Read back a GameplayAbility blueprint CDO: instancing policy, ability/cancel/block/activation tags, cost/cooldown GE, triggers. Paired read tool so edits are verifiable (inspection-first invariant).

tools.name: gas_ability_set_tags
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (CDO FGameplayTagContainer set + MarkPackageDirty + recompile)
tools.signature: (ability_path, ability_tags?[], cancel_tags?[], block_tags?[], activation_required_tags?[], activation_blocked_tags?[], dry_run?) -> {ability_path, tags_after}
tools.description: Set the AbilityTags / CancelAbilitiesWithTag / BlockAbilitiesWithTag / ActivationOwned/Required/Blocked tag containers on an ability CDO. The core of gameplay-tag-driven ability behavior.

tools.name: gas_ability_set_policies
tools.description: Set instancing policy (NonInstanced/InstancedPerActor/InstancedPerExecution), net execution policy, and net security policy on an ability CDO. Common config that otherwise needs hand-rolled python.

tools.name: gas_ability_set_costcooldown
tools.description: Wire an ability's Cost GameplayEffect and Cooldown GameplayEffect (the standard GAS resource pattern) by asset path. Outcome-verb covering the two most-edited ability fields together.

tools.name: gas_ability_grant
tools.description: Grant an ability to an actor's AbilitySystemComponent at a level/input-id, returning the spec handle. First-class wrapper over existing gas_grant_ability (runtime/PIE).

tools.name: gas_ability_remove
tools.description: Clear a previously granted ability from an actor's ASC by spec handle or ability class. Lifecycle completion for grant (no peer has GAS grant at all).

tools.name: gas_ability_try_activate
tools.description: Activate a granted ability on an actor by class or by gameplay tag (TryActivateAbilitiesByTag) in PIE — the only way to exercise gameplay-tag-driven activation from the agent.

tools.name: gas_ability_grants_list
tools.description: List all ability specs currently granted on an actor's ASC (class, level, input id, active flag, handle). Read-back/verify for grant + activation.

tools.name: gas_effect_create
tools.signature: (path, name, duration_policy?, duration_seconds?, period?, modifiers?[], dry_run?) -> {path, name, duration_policy}
tools.description: Create a UGameplayEffect blueprint with duration policy (Instant/Duration/Infinite), duration seconds, period, and an initial modifier list. First-class wrapper over existing gas_create_effect.

tools.name: gas_effect_inspect
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (CDO reflect Modifiers + tag containers + stacking)
tools.signature: (effect_path) -> {duration_policy, duration, period, modifiers[], granted_tags[], applied_tags[], stacking}
tools.description: Read back a GameplayEffect CDO: duration policy/magnitude, period, modifiers (attribute/op/magnitude), granted/applied tags, stacking config. Paired verify tool.

tools.name: gas_effect_add_modifier
tools.description: Add/replace a single attribute modifier (attribute, op Additive/Multiplicative/Division/Override, scalable-float magnitude) on a GameplayEffect CDO. Incremental edit alongside batch create.

tools.name: gas_effect_set_magnitude_setbycaller
tools.description: Configure a modifier to use a SetByCaller magnitude bound to a data tag (the standard dynamic-damage pattern) instead of a fixed float. Surfaces the magnitude type that the float-only path hides.

tools.name: gas_effect_set_tags
tools.signature: (effect_path, granted_tags?[], ongoing_required?[], ongoing_ignored?[], application_required?[], removal_required?[], dry_run?) -> {effect_path, tags_after}
tools.description: Set a GameplayEffect's tag containers: GrantedTags (AssetTags), OngoingTagRequirements, ApplicationTagRequirements, RemovalTagRequirements. Tag-driven effect gating.

tools.name: gas_effect_set_stacking
tools.signature: (effect_path, stacking_type, stack_limit?, refresh_policy?, period_reset_policy?, dry_run?) -> {effect_path, stacking}
tools.description: Configure stacking policy (None/AggregateBySource/AggregateByTarget), stack limit, duration-refresh and period-reset policy on a Duration/Infinite effect.

tools.name: gas_effect_apply
tools.description: Apply a GameplayEffect to an actor's ASC at a level in PIE, returning the active handle and validity. First-class wrapper over existing gas_apply_effect.

tools.name: gas_effect_remove
tools.description: Remove active GameplayEffect(s) from an actor's ASC by active-handle, by effect class, or by granted tag (RemoveActiveEffectsWithTags). Completes the apply lifecycle.

tools.name: gas_active_effects_list
tools.description: List active GameplayEffects on an actor's ASC: source, level, duration remaining, stack count, granted tags. Read-back for apply/remove and for debugging buff state.

tools.name: gas_attributeset_list
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (iterate UClass children of UAttributeSet)
tools.description: Enumerate UAttributeSet subclasses available in the project (C++ and any blueprint), with module + asset origin. Discovery step before any attribute/effect work.

tools.name: gas_attribute_list
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (reflect FProperty list on AttributeSet class)
tools.signature: (attributeset_class, limit?, offset?) -> {attributes:[{name, type, attribute_path}], has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: List the FGameplayAttribute properties on a given AttributeSet class (name, type, fully-qualified attribute path for use in effect modifiers). The attribute-path resolver effect_create needs.

tools.name: gas_attribute_get
tools.description: Read the current and base value of an attribute on an actor's ASC in PIE (GetGameplayAttributeValue). Read-back to verify an effect actually moved Health/Mana.

tools.name: gas_attribute_set_base
tools.description: Set the base value of an attribute on an actor's ASC directly (SetNumericAttributeBase) for test setup — bypasses effects. PIE/debug helper.

tools.name: gas_attributeset_inspect
tools.description: Read the CDO default values of every attribute on an AttributeSet class (the design-time defaults). Inspection-first for attribute config without entering PIE.

tools.name: gas_attributeset_create_stub
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (template codegen to disk; flagged needs_compile)
tools.signature: (module_name, class_name, attributes:[{name, default}], dest_dir?) -> {header_path, source_path, needs_compile:true}
tools.description: Emit a compilable C++ UAttributeSet header/source stub (with ATTRIBUTE_ACCESSORS macros and the requested attributes) into the project's Source dir. Honest workaround for the hard limit that Python cannot create AttributeSet classes — flagged as requiring a recompile.

tools.name: gas_tag_list
tools.description: List registered gameplay tags from GameplayTagsManager, optionally filtered by a parent prefix, paginated. Discovery for all tag-driven tools.

tools.name: gas_tag_add
tools.description: Add a gameplay tag (and implicitly its parents) to the project tag table (Config/DefaultGameplayTags.ini) with an optional dev comment; validates the tag string and dry-runs. The authoring half of tag-driven grants.

tools.name: gas_tag_remove
tools.description: Remove a gameplay tag from the project ini tag table after checking for references. Lifecycle completion + safety (warns if tag is in use by an ability/effect).

tools.name: gas_tag_validate
tools.description: Check whether one or more tag strings are well-formed and registered, returning unknown/typo candidates — prevents silently binding a misspelled tag to an ability.

tools.name: gas_asc_inspect
tools.description: Full read-back of an actor's AbilitySystemComponent in PIE: granted abilities, active effects, owned/loose gameplay tags, and key attribute values in one call. The primary debug/verify tool for the runtime side.

tools.name: gas_asc_add
tools.description: Add a UAbilitySystemComponent to an editor actor (or its blueprint) if it lacks one, so subsequent grant/apply tools have a target. Setup verb for actors that aren't GAS-ready.

tools.name: gas_asc_set_loose_tags
tools.description: Add or remove loose (non-replicated) gameplay tags on an actor's ASC at runtime (AddLooseGameplayTag/RemoveLooseGameplayTag) to test tag-gated ability activation/effect requirements.

tools.name: gas_cue_create
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (CreateBlueprint from UGameplayCueNotify_Actor/_Static + set GameplayCueTag)
tools.description: Create a GameplayCueNotify (Static or Actor) blueprint bound to a GameplayCue.* tag — the standard cosmetic-feedback half of GAS that effects trigger. Net-new authoring no peer offers.

tools.name: gas_abilityset_create
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (DataAsset create + populate arrays, if project defines the type)
tools.signature: (path, name, abilities[], effects[], attribute_sets[], dry_run?) -> {path, entry_counts}
tools.description: Create a UDataAsset 'ability set' (Lyra-style) bundling abilities + granted effects + attribute sets for one-call grants. High-leverage outcome-verb for GAS-heavy projects.

tools.name: gas_batch_grant
tools.module: HaybaMCPGAS (new iterate matched actors) over the grant/apply core
tools.parity: GenOrca/Roblox have batch ops generally; GAS batch is net-new moat
tools.signature: (actor_query, ability_paths?[], effect_paths?[], level?, dry_run?) -> {results:[{actor, granted, applied, error?}], total}
tools.description: Grant a set of abilities (or apply a set of effects) across many actors matched by class/tag/selection in one call, with per-actor results. Batch outcome-verb (matches Roblox mass_* peers).

tools.name: gas_list_assets
tools.description: List GameplayAbility / GameplayEffect / GameplayCue / AbilitySet assets in the project with filter + pagination, classifying each. Catalog/discovery tool so the agent can find what to edit.

tools.name: gas_validate
tools.module: python_run-backed TS feeding validator_run + PLUMB constraints
tools.signature: (target_path?, actor_path?, fix?) -> {ok, violations:[{code, message, severity}], fixed[]}
tools.description: PLUMB-style quantified check of a GAS asset or actor: ability references a registered cost/cooldown GE, all bound tags are registered, effect modifiers reference real attributes, no dangling class refs. Closed-loop validate-before/after-mutate moat.

domains.domain: Gameplay Framework defaults — GameMode/GameState/PlayerController/Pawn/Character/HUD/GameInstance/PlayerStart + World Settings default-class wiring
domains.summary: This domain is near-greenfield: today there is NO way to set the GameMode, configure World Settings, or wire any default class (Pawn/Controller/HUD/GameState/GameInstance) — level_info only reads. That is gating, because nothing an agent builds is playable until the framework is wired. Strategy: ship the inspection-first read pair plus the three write surfaces UE actually uses (project GameMapsSettings ini, per-level WorldSettings override, and GameMode CDO class-wiring), all python_run-backed so there is zero plugin rebuild. The moat is gameframework_verify (dry-run resolution of which classes the engine will actually pick through the world-override > project-default > engine chain) and PLUMB-style gameframework_validate (abstract pawn? no PlayerStart? unassigned controller?), which no competitor offers for the gameplay framework. Cap it with one-shot outcome verbs (scaffold, apply_preset) and a checkpoint/restore pair, since project-ini edits sit outside UE's Ctrl+Z undo and need an explicit snapshot for safety.
dependencies: Hardened python_run handler — every tool is pyTemplate/python-backed, no C++ rebuild; depends on Theme 0/1 SEH+ProcessCommand and the pyTemplate factory (Section 5 #4)
unreal.GameMapsSettings CDO (get_default_object + set_editor_property + save_config) for project wiring; GlobalDefaultGameMode/GameInstanceClass ini writes need editor restart to fully take effect
world.get_world_settings() / AWorldSettings.default_game_mode editor property + level_save for per-level overrides
AssetTools/KismetEditorUtilities (create_blueprint, compile_blueprint) + BlueprintGeneratedClass CDO mutation for class-wiring; must mark_package_dirty + compile + save_asset

Existing infra: executeCommand/tool-executor, schema-registry, hayba_asset_search (class discovery), actor_spawn + level_save (PlayerStart), validator_run + plumb_validate (gameframework_validate), Plan-Mode gate before destructive ini writes
Transaction seam (4C C++) for level-actor edits; project-ini edits are NOT in UE undo so handled via checkpoint snapshot files instead
risks: GameMapsSettings.save_config() writes DefaultEngine.ini; GameInstanceClass and (sometimes) GlobalDefaultGameMode changes only fully apply after an editor restart — tools must return a needs_restart warning, not silently imply live effect
Project-ini writes bypass UE's transaction/undo system entirely — Ctrl+Z will NOT revert them; the checkpoint/restore pair is the only rollback path and must be advertised as such
BlueprintGeneratedClass path normalization: BP classes need the _C suffix and CDO mutation; forgetting compile_blueprint + save leaves the wiring un-persisted or stale at next PIE
Setting an abstract or Deprecated class as DefaultPawnClass/PlayerControllerClass yields a silently broken PIE; validate class is concrete + correct base before writing
WorldSettings is per-persistent-level (and World Partition has one) — setting default_game_mode on a streamed sublevel actor is a no-op; must target the persistent level's WorldSettings
Resolution ambiguity: a world override masks the project default; gameframework_verify must reproduce engine precedence exactly or agents will wire the wrong layer and be confused why PIE ignores it
Auto-possess / controller-rotation defaults set on a Pawn CDO can fight an explicitly placed PlayerStart or possession logic, producing a camera that won't move — validate cross-tool consistency
domains.test_plan: On a live editor with a test level open: (1) gameframework_inspect → confirm it reports project GlobalDefaultGameMode, GameInstanceClass, the active level's WorldSettings override, and the resolved effective classes. (2) gamemode_create a BP_TestGameMode, gamemode_set_classes wiring a concrete Character + PlayerController + HUD, then gamemode_get to read back the CDO and confirm persistence after a BP recompile. (3) world_settings_set_gamemode to BP_TestGameMode on the persistent level, level_save. (4) playerstart_spawn at origin with tag 'P1'; verify via playerstart_list and an editor_capture_viewport screenshot showing the PlayerStart gizmo. (5) gameframework_verify → assert the resolution chain returns BP_TestGameMode + its pawn/controller/HUD as effective. (6) gameframework_validate → assert zero issues; then deliberately set an abstract pawn and confirm it flags it. (7) editor_start_pie → confirm the player possesses the wired pawn at the PlayerStart, capture PIE screenshot. (8) gameframework_checkpoint, change the default gamemode, gameframework_restore, re-inspect to confirm the original wiring returns. (9) project_set_default_gamemode → confirm DefaultEngine.ini diff + needs_restart warning surfaced.

tools.name: gameframework_inspect
tools.parity: net-new moat (level_info only reads; no competitor exposes framework resolution)
tools.description: Read the full effective framework wiring in one call — project GameMapsSettings (GlobalDefaultGameMode, GameInstanceClass, default maps), the active level's WorldSettings override, and the resolved effective Pawn/Controller/HUD/GameState/PlayerState classes; the inspection-first read for the whole domain.

tools.name: gameframework_verify
tools.signature: (level_path?) -> {effective_gamemode, resolved_from:'world_override'|'project_default'|'engine', pawn, controller, hud, gamestate, playerstate, warnings[]}
