tools.description: Dry-run resolver: answer 'if I hit PIE on this level right now, exactly which GameMode/Pawn/Controller/HUD/GameState will the engine instantiate' by reproducing the world-override > project-default > engine-fallback precedence; the read-back/verify safety tool.

tools.name: gameframework_validate
tools.description: Run PLUMB/validator-style checks over the framework wiring — abstract/deprecated default classes, missing PlayerStart, unassigned PlayerControllerClass, GameMode not referenced by any default, pawn auto-possess conflicts; returns actionable issues with codes.

tools.name: project_set_default_gamemode
tools.parity: Flop/GenOrca have project-settings writes; this specific wiring is net-new for Hayba
tools.description: Set GlobalDefaultGameMode in GameMapsSettings (DefaultEngine.ini) — the headline missing capability; this is how you set the GameMode project-wide.

tools.name: project_gamemaps_get
tools.description: Read-back of GameMapsSettings (GlobalDefaultGameMode, GameInstanceClass, EditorStartupMap, GameDefaultMap, ServerDefaultMap, TransitionMap); paired reader for the project-level setters.

tools.name: project_set_game_instance
tools.description: Set the GameInstanceClass in GameMapsSettings — required to wire persistent/session-level subsystems; warns that this only fully applies after an editor restart.

tools.name: project_set_default_maps
tools.signature: (editor_startup?, game_default?, server_default?, transition?, plan_approved=false) -> {ok, previous, diff}
tools.description: Set EditorStartupMap / GameDefaultMap / ServerDefaultMap / TransitionMap in one call; controls what loads on launch and PIE-from-empty.

tools.name: world_settings_set_gamemode
tools.parity: net-new (no World Settings writer exists today)
tools.description: Set DefaultGameMode override on the active (persistent) level's WorldSettings — the per-level way to configure the GameMode; the named 'configure World Settings' gap.

tools.name: world_settings_get
tools.description: Read the persistent level's WorldSettings — default GameMode override, gravity override, kill-Z, world-to-meters, world bounds checks, default physics volume; gameframework-specific read that level_info doesn't cover.

tools.name: world_settings_set
tools.description: Batch-set arbitrary WorldSettings properties (gravity override, kill-Z, world-to-meters, bounds checks, default physics volume) on the persistent level; outcome verb over many low-level prop sets.

tools.name: world_settings_clear_gamemode_override
tools.description: Clear the per-level DefaultGameMode override so the level falls back to the project GlobalDefaultGameMode; reverts mis-wiring at the world layer.

tools.name: gamemode_create
tools.parity: GenOrca/Flop create BP assets; framework-specialized here
tools.signature: (asset_path, parent='GameModeBase'|'GameMode', pawn?, controller?, hud?, gamestate?, playerstate?) -> {ok, asset_path, generated_class}
tools.description: Create a new GameMode (or GameModeBase) Blueprint asset at a target path, optionally pre-wiring default classes; the entry point for authoring a custom rules object.

tools.name: gamemode_set_classes
tools.parity: net-new moat (CDO class-wiring as a typed tool)
tools.signature: (gamemode_path, pawn?, controller?, hud?, gamestate?, playerstate?, spectator?) -> {ok, applied[], previous{}, compiled:true}
tools.description: Wire DefaultPawnClass / PlayerControllerClass / HUDClass / GameStateClass / PlayerStateClass / SpectatorClass on a GameMode BP's CDO in one batch, then compile+save; the core class-wiring verb.

tools.name: gamemode_get
tools.signature: (gamemode_path) -> {pawn, controller, hud, gamestate, playerstate, spectator, parent_class}
tools.description: Read back the wired default classes from a GameMode asset's CDO; paired reader for gamemode_set_classes to verify persistence after recompile.

tools.name: framework_create_blueprint
tools.parity: DCC peers (Maya parametric prefab); net-new for UE framework
tools.description: Create a Blueprint subclass of any framework base (Character/Pawn/PlayerController/HUD/GameState/PlayerState/GameInstance/SpectatorPawn) — one outcome verb covering the whole class family instead of N near-identical creators.

tools.name: framework_blueprint_list
tools.signature: (kind?, limit=50, offset=0) -> {items:[{asset_path, generated_class, kind, parent}], has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: List all Blueprints in the project derived from framework bases, grouped by kind (GameMode/Pawn/Controller/...); discovery for the wiring tools so agents don't guess class paths.

tools.name: character_configure_defaults
tools.signature: (character_path, max_walk_speed?, jump_z?, gravity_scale?, air_control?, rotation_rate?, orient_to_movement?) -> {ok, applied[], previous{}}
tools.description: Set CharacterMovementComponent defaults (max walk speed, jump Z velocity, gravity scale, air control, rotation rate, orient-to-movement) on a Character BP CDO; the common 'make the character feel right' verb.

tools.name: pawn_set_controller_rotation
tools.signature: (pawn_path, use_yaw?, use_pitch?, use_roll?, auto_possess_player?, auto_possess_ai?) -> {ok, applied[], previous{}}
tools.description: Set bUseControllerRotationYaw/Pitch/Roll and AutoPossessPlayer/AutoPossessAI on a Pawn or Character CDO; controls camera-follows-controller behavior that breaks silently if wrong.

tools.name: playercontroller_configure
tools.signature: (controller_path, show_mouse_cursor?, enable_click_events?, enable_touch_events?, default_mapping_context?) -> {ok, applied[], previous{}}
tools.description: Set PlayerController CDO defaults — default Enhanced Input MappingContext (added in BP-construction note), show-mouse-cursor, default input mode, click/touch events enabled; wires the input front door.

tools.name: framework_set_cdo_property
tools.parity: Roblox mass_set_property analog; net-new for UE CDOs
tools.description: Validated escape-hatch: set any editor property on any framework BP's CDO by name, type-checked against reflection before write; covers the long tail without a new tool per property.

tools.name: playerstart_spawn
tools.parity: actor_spawn exists generically; framework-typed convenience is net-new
tools.description: Place a PlayerStart actor at a transform with an optional PlayerStartTag; without one, PIE has nowhere to spawn the pawn — the most-forgotten required actor.

tools.name: playerstart_list
tools.description: List PlayerStart actors in the level with their tags and transforms; paired reader to confirm spawn points exist and are tagged for multiplayer.

tools.name: playerstart_batch_spawn
tools.description: Place multiple PlayerStarts at once (grid/ring/list of transforms) with auto-incremented tags; sets up multiplayer spawn points in one call.

tools.name: playerstart_set_tag
tools.description: Set/replace the PlayerStartTag on an existing PlayerStart so a GameMode's ChoosePlayerStart logic can target it.

tools.name: playerstart_delete
tools.description: Delete one or more PlayerStart actors (by path or all) — cleanup for re-layout; transaction-wrapped so it's one Ctrl+Z.

tools.name: gameframework_scaffold
tools.module: python_run-backed TS orchestrating the above + checkpoint: src/tools/gameframework/scaffold.ts
tools.description: One-shot outcome verb: create GameMode + Character/Pawn + PlayerController + HUD (+ optional GameState), wire them all, set as project or world default, and place a PlayerStart — a playable framework from nothing in a single transactional call.

tools.name: gameframework_apply_preset
tools.description: Instantiate a template preset (third-person, top-down, first-person, spectator/UI-only) by cloning sensible base classes and default values; steals the Maya parametric-prefab pattern for gameplay framework.

tools.name: gameframework_checkpoint
tools.description: Snapshot the current framework wiring (GameMapsSettings ini values + WorldSettings override + GameMode CDO classes) to a named restore point; required because project-ini edits are outside UE's undo.

tools.name: gameframework_restore
tools.description: Restore framework wiring from a checkpoint — reverts project ini, world override, and GameMode CDO classes together; the only rollback path for the non-undoable ini writes.

domains.domain: Source Control integration (Perforce / Git / SVN) — connect, status, checkout, mark-for-add/delete, revert, changelists, submit, sync, resolve, diff, history
domains.summary: UE ships a full provider-agnostic source control layer (ISourceControlModule + ISourceControlProvider, with Perforce/Git/Subversion/PlasticSCM providers), but Hayba exposes ZERO of it as MCP tools — only an internal Slate diff panel touches it (BuildSourceControlBadge/IsSourceControlEnabled). This is a clean net-new moat: no UE-MCP competitor (Aura, GenOrca, remiphilippe, Epic 5.8) exposes editor-side VCS as agent tools, yet it is the single biggest unblocker for unattended, team-safe agent edits — an agent that mutates 40 assets must check them out and submit a coherent changelist, not leave a team's depot in a dirty/locked state. Strategy: ship the read/checkout/add/revert/file-state core as python_run-backed wrappers over unreal.SourceControlHelpers (no rebuild), then do connect-with-credentials, async submit/changelist, resolve, diff, history, and Perforce shelve/lock as one new C++ handler (HaybaMCPSourceControlHandler) driving ISourceControlProvider async operations on the game-thread RunSync seam. Every mutation is inspection-first (paired *_state/_status read), dry-run-able (sc_submit_preview), and routed through the existing Diff panel so the agent's checkouts show up in the same review surface as its asset edits — pressing the crash-resilience + transaction + plan-mode moats directly.
dependencies: Theme 0/1 gates: ProcessCommand SEH wrap + add-a-tool descriptor refactor must land first so the ~24 new commands ship as descriptors, not 7-file churn.

UE ISourceControlModule + a configured provider plugin (PerforceSourceControl / GitSourceControl / SubversionSourceControl) enabled in the .uproject; tools must degrade gracefully (sc_provider_info reports disabled) when none is configured.
unreal.SourceControlHelpers Python API for the no-rebuild fast-path tools (status/file_state/checkout/add/delete/revert/sync_file).

New C++ handler module HaybaMCPSourceControlHandler.{h,cpp} under Private/handlers/, wired into HaybaMCPCommandHandler.cpp ProcessCommand, for async ISourceControlProvider ops (connect/submit/changelist/resolve/diff/history/shelve/lock).

Async source control operations must run on the game-thread via FHaybaGameThread::RunSync (per MEMORY: handlers run on game thread; AsyncTask(GameThread)+Wait self-deadlocks) and complete within executor timeout ceilings (submit/sync are long — use job-envelope pattern like build_*).
Existing SHaybaMCPDiffPanel (BuildSourceControlBadge/IsSourceControlEnabled/SourceControlProviderName) reused as the diff/review surface for sc_diff and as the place agent checkouts surface.
Plan-Mode gate (bPlanApproved) + DisabledTools must cover the destructive verbs: sc_submit, sc_revert*, sc_sync(force), sc_mark_for_delete, sc_unlock, sc_disconnect.
risks: Submit/sync/connect are genuinely async and can block (server round-trips, large depots) — naive synchronous waits will hit the same game-thread-freeze class as build_*/test_run; MUST use the job-envelope + RunSync seam and align timeouts, or the moat tool reintroduces a P0 freeze.

Provider behavior is NOT uniform: Perforce has changelists/shelve/exclusive-lock; Git has stash/LFS-lock and no numbered CLs; SVN differs again. Changelist/shelve/lock tools need per-provider capability flags so they fail honestly (capability_unsupported code) instead of silently no-op — violating the honesty invariant otherwise.

Irreversible/destructive ops (sc_submit, sc_revert_all, sc_sync force) can lose human teammates' work or pollute a shared depot; require dry-run-first (sc_submit_preview), Plan-Mode approval, and require_clean default true.

Credential handling for sc_connect: P4 passwords / tokens must not be logged in the journal or echoed in results; reuse the DPAPI-encrypted key-storage pattern from the BYOK panel, never plaintext ini.
Blind-retry of non-idempotent ops would double-submit or double-checkout; sc_submit/sc_mark_for_add/sc_changelist_create must be excluded from the idempotent-retry allowlist (Theme 0 transport fix).

unreal.SourceControlHelpers Python surface is narrower than ISourceControlProvider and varies across 5.x; the python fast-path tools may need fallback to the C++ handler on versions where a helper is missing.

Uasset binary diff is non-trivial — sc_diff structured object diff depends on FAssetToolsModule asset-diff support; for unmergeable binaries fall back to a property/summary diff rather than a misleading unified text diff.
Multi-agent on a shared depot can deadlock on locks/conflicts; sc_lock/sc_resolve must surface other_user and never auto-accept-theirs by default (auto_safe only).
domains.test_plan: "On a live editor connected to a throwaway test depot (spin up a local P4D and a Git+LFS repo; run the full matrix on at least Perforce + Git to prove provider-agnostic behavior): 1) sc_provider_info on a project with SC disabled -> reports enabled=false (honesty); enable a provider, re-run -> reports provider/login. 2) sc_connect with valid then invalid creds -> ok/login true, then clean error_code (no plaintext password in journal — grep the journal). 3) Create a new asset via actor/asset tools, sc_checkout_or_add -> sc_file_state confirms is_added; sc_status shows it; sc_submit_preview lists it with action=add; sc_submit -> sc_history shows the new revision. 4) Edit an existing tracked asset WITHOUT checkout, then sc_reconcile(dry_run) -> lists it under to_edit; sc_checkout -> sc_file_state is_checked_out true. 5) sc_revert on a checked-out unchanged file (only_unchanged) -> reverted; sc_file_state clean. 6) Conflict path: from a second client edit+submit the same file, sc_sync here -> reports conflict; sc_resolve(theirs) -> still_conflicted empty; sc_file_state is_conflicted false. 7) Changelist flow: sc_changelist_create -> sc_changelist_add_files -> sc_changelist_describe shows files -> sc_submit(changelist_id) -> sc_changelist_delete on the now-empty CL. 8) sc_diff a locally-edited uasset -> structured changed_props non-empty and the change appears in SHaybaMCPDiffPanel. 9) Batch: select 3 actors in the viewport, sc_checkout_selected -> all 3 source packages checked out. 10) Perforce-only: sc_lock then attempt edit from second client (denied), sc_unlock; sc_shelve a CL, sc_unshelve restores. 11) Capability honesty: run sc_shelve/sc_lock against the Git provider -> capability_unsupported, not a crash or silent success. 12) Freeze check: run sc_sync on a large path and sc_submit of 50 files while polling editor responsiveness (editor_capture_viewport / wait_for_idle) -> editor stays responsive (job-envelope, no game-thread freeze). 13) Plan-Mode: with bPlanApproved=false, sc_submit/sc_revert_all are refused before execution."

tools.name: sc_provider_info
tools.signature: () -> {enabled, available, provider, logged_in, workspace, server, user}
tools.description: Report whether source control is enabled/available, which provider is active (Perforce/Git/SVN), and connection/login state — the gating probe every other sc_* tool and the agent should call first.

tools.name: sc_connect
tools.signature: (provider, server?, user?, workspace?, password?, args_kv?) -> {ok, logged_in, provider, error_code?}
tools.description: Connect/enable a source control provider with credentials (P4 port/user/client or Git remote), persisting to the project's SourceControlSettings — required before any agent VCS op can run unattended.

tools.name: sc_disconnect
tools.description: Disconnect / disable the active provider cleanly (drops the connection without reverting work) — lets an agent tear down credentials at end of a headless session.

tools.name: sc_status
tools.module: C++ HaybaMCPSourceControlHandler (FUpdateStatus async) with python fast-path via SourceControlHelpers.status
tools.signature: (path_prefix?, only_modified?, limit=50, offset?) -> {files:[{file, state, other_user?, head_rev, have_rev, in_changelist?}], has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: List the source-control status of files under a path/changelist (added/edited/checked-out-by-other/not-current/conflicted), paginated — the inspection-first read that pairs with every mutating tool.

tools.name: sc_file_state
tools.signature: (files[] | package_paths[]) -> {states:[{file, is_checked_out, checked_out_other, is_added, is_deleted, is_current, is_conflicted, is_source_controlled}]}
tools.description: Read back the exact SC state of one or more specific files (checked out by me/other, locked, deleted, current, conflicted) — the verify/read-back primitive used to confirm a checkout/add/revert actually landed.

tools.name: sc_refresh
tools.description: Force-refresh cached SC state for a path or the whole project (FUpdateStatus, update history/modified flags) so subsequent reads aren't stale after external p4/git changes.

tools.name: sc_checkout
tools.description: Check out (open-for-edit) one or more files/asset packages so the agent can legally mutate them — the gate that prevents read-only-clobber and team conflicts on edited assets.

tools.name: sc_checkout_or_add
tools.description: Check out if tracked, else mark-for-add if new — the single outcome-verb an agent should call before saving any asset it might have just created (Roblox-style 'just make it editable').

tools.name: sc_mark_for_add
tools.description: Mark new untracked files/assets for add so they enter the next changelist — without this an agent's freshly-created assets silently never get committed.

tools.name: sc_mark_for_delete
tools.description: Mark tracked files/assets for delete (open-for-delete) so removal is recorded in VCS rather than an orphaned working-copy delete.

tools.name: sc_revert
tools.parity: net-new moat — mirrors Aura Sandbox rollback
tools.description: Revert files (discard checkout/edit, restore depot revision), optionally only-if-unchanged — the agent's undo for VCS-level mistakes and the cleanup after a failed plan.

tools.name: sc_revert_all
tools.module: C++ HaybaMCPSourceControlHandler (FRevert over enumerated open files)
tools.description: Revert every file currently open in a changelist (or the default CL) in one call — panic/cleanup verb to return a workspace to clean after an aborted agent run.

tools.name: sc_changelist_create
tools.description: Create a named changelist with a description (P4 numbered CL / staged group) so an agent groups one logical task's edits into one reviewable, atomically-submittable unit.

tools.name: sc_changelist_list
tools.signature: (limit=50, offset?) -> {changelists:[{id, description, file_count, shelved}], has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: List pending changelists with id/description/file-count/shelved-flag, paginated — inspection read for choosing where to add files or what to submit.

tools.name: sc_changelist_describe
tools.description: Show one changelist in detail: description plus every file with its action (add/edit/delete) — the pre-submit review/verify read.

tools.name: sc_changelist_add_files
tools.description: Move/assign already-open files into a target changelist so the agent can curate which edits go together before submit.

tools.name: sc_changelist_set_description
tools.description: Edit a pending changelist's description (e.g. write a generated commit message summarizing the agent's edits) before submitting.

tools.name: sc_changelist_delete
tools.description: Delete an empty pending changelist (after its files were submitted or moved) to keep the workspace tidy.

tools.name: sc_submit_preview
tools.module: C++ HaybaMCPSourceControlHandler (FUpdateStatus + conflict probe, no FCheckIn)
tools.parity: net-new moat — analog of Flop bp_dry_run
tools.description: DRY-RUN a submit: list exactly what would be committed (files, actions, CL description) and flag blockers (out-of-date, unresolved, locked-by-other) WITHOUT committing — the safety gate before the irreversible sc_submit.

tools.name: sc_submit
tools.module: C++ HaybaMCPSourceControlHandler (FCheckIn async on RunSync seam)
tools.parity: net-new moat — closes remiphilippe DevOps loop
tools.signature: (description, changelist?='default', files?[], require_clean=true) -> {ok, submitted_changelist, file_count, error_code?}
tools.description: Submit/commit a changelist (or specific files) with a description — the terminal commit op; honors Plan-Mode and refuses if sc_submit_preview reports unresolved/out-of-date blockers.

tools.name: sc_sync
tools.description: Sync/get-latest for a path or the whole workspace to a given revision (default head), the agent's 'pull before work' — reports updated/added/deleted and any sync conflicts.

tools.name: sc_get_latest
tools.description: Convenience outcome-verb: sync only the given files/asset packages to head and reload them in-editor so the agent operates on current content.

tools.name: sc_resolve
tools.module: C++ HaybaMCPSourceControlHandler (FResolve async; provider resolve flags)
tools.description: Resolve conflicted/needs-resolve files using a strategy (accept-mine / accept-theirs / auto-safe) — without this an agent stalls forever on any concurrent-edit conflict.

tools.name: sc_diff
tools.module: C++ HaybaMCPSourceControlHandler + SHaybaMCPDiffPanel reuse (asset diff via FAssetToolsModule)
tools.parity: net-new moat — extends existing Diff panel
tools.signature: (file | package_path, from_rev?='have', to_rev?='working') -> {kind, changed_props?[], unified_diff?, summary}
tools.description: Diff a file against its depot/have revision (or two revisions): for uassets returns a structured object/property diff and feeds the existing Diff panel; for text returns a unified diff — the review primitive before submit.

tools.name: sc_history
tools.signature: (file | package_path, limit=20, offset?) -> {revisions:[{rev, changelist, user, date, action, description}], has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: Show revision history/log for a file (rev, CL, user, date, description) paginated — answers 'who changed this and why' for the agent's reasoning and rollback choices.

tools.name: sc_blame
tools.description: Annotate/blame a text file line-by-line with the last-changing revision and author — diagnostic read for code/config conflicts.

tools.name: sc_lock
tools.description: Take an exclusive lock (P4 lock / Git LFS lock) on binary uassets so concurrent agents/humans can't both edit unmergeable files — critical for multi-agent safety on a shared depot.

tools.name: sc_unlock
tools.description: Release locks taken via sc_lock so others can edit — cleanup pair for sc_lock.

tools.name: sc_shelve
tools.description: Shelve a changelist's edits (P4 shelve / Git stash) so an agent can park WIP, hand off for review, or unblock a sync without losing or submitting work.

tools.name: sc_unshelve
tools.description: Restore shelved edits back into the workspace/changelist — pair for sc_shelve, lets an agent resume parked WIP.

tools.name: sc_checkout_selected
tools.description: Batch outcome-verb: check-out-or-add every asset referenced by the current editor selection (and optionally their dependencies) in one call — the practical entry point before a multi-actor agent edit.

tools.name: sc_reconcile
tools.description: Reconcile offline work: detect files edited/added/deleted on disk while the agent ran without checkouts, and open them for the correct action — recovers a workspace into a submittable state.

tools.name: sc_settings
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (read SourceControlSettings ini + provider current settings)
tools.description: Read/inspect the project's source control settings and per-provider config (P4 port/user/workspace, Git remote/branch, auto-checkout-on-modify) — config introspection without round-tripping the UI.

domains.domain: Localization — String Tables, culture/locale set, text gather/compile, .po import/export, localization dashboard targets
domains.summary: Localization is a total greenfield: no UE MCP competitor (Epic 5.8, Aura, Flop, GenOrca, UAIP) ships any localization tooling, so nearly every tool here is a net-new moat that ties directly into Hayba's existing PLUMB "validate before/after mutate" engine. The strategy is three layers: (1) cheap, no-rebuild python_run wrappers for the author loop — String Table CRUD, CSV round-trip, culture config, preview-culture switching — which cover ~80% of value with zero plugin churn; (2) job-envelope-wrapped commandlet runs (GatherText/compile/.po export-import) that MUST go through the Theme-0 async infra because the GatherText commandlet is a multi-second-to-minute external process that would freeze the editor exactly like build_*/test_run; (3) quantified-validation tools (placeholder-integrity, .po round-trip safety, namespace/key collision audit, unlocalized-text scan, dashboard completion %) that productize the PLUMB moat into the localization correctness loop. Every write tool ships a paired *_get/*_inspect read-back, is FScopedTransaction- or dry_run-guarded, and surfaces a real per-culture completion dashboard — turning "did my localization actually land?" from a blind commandlet into a closed loop. We deliberately accept that String Table entry mutation and ULocalizationTarget config have version-variable Python coverage, and fall back to CSV-import and direct Config/Localization/*.ini editing where the reflected API is thin.
dependencies: Theme 0 job-envelope async infra (docs/audit/2026-06-22-mcp-async-command-conversions.md) — REQUIRED for loc_gather_text/loc_compile_text/loc_pipeline_run; the GatherText commandlet is a long external process and would freeze the editor exactly like build_*/test_run if run synchronously
Theme 1 add-a-tool refactor + pyTemplate factory — these 36 tools should land as descriptors, not 36x7-file wrappers
Hardened python_run handler (SEH + security gate) for all non-commandlet tools
UE Python reflection coverage: unreal.StringTable mutable API, unreal.LocalizationSettings/LocalizationTarget, unreal.InternationalizationLibrary, AssetTools StringTableFactory (pinned 5.7)
UnrealEditor-Cmd binary path + project .uproject resolution for commandlet spawning
PLUMB validator + validator_run seams for loc_po_validate/loc_validate_target
Vision-capture (editor_capture_viewport/render_camera) to visually confirm preview-culture switches
PortableObject (.po) parser library or UE's PortableObjectFormatDOM via commandlet
risks: String Table entry MUTATION from Python is version-variable and may be read-mostly in 5.7; set_entry/batch_set may have to route through CSV-import or a small C++ handler in HaybaMCPToolkit — fallback designed in but adds a possible rebuild

GatherText/compile commandlets are long-running external processes; running them on the game thread WILL freeze the editor (the exact Theme-0 P0 bug) — these tools are blocked until the job-envelope lands
ULocalizationTarget/LocalizationSettings Python surface is incomplete; loc_target_* fall back to direct Config/Localization/*.ini editing, which can desync from in-memory dashboard state until reload
Live preview-culture switching (loc_preview_culture_set) can destabilize editor UI / Slate text; must always offer loc_preview_culture_reset and avoid leaving the editor in a non-default culture
PO round-trip is encoding- and placeholder-fragile; non-UTF-8 or reordered {0}/%s args silently corrupt builds — mitigated by loc_po_validate as a hard pre-import gate
Commandlet spawn must use the correct engine/editor binary and not collide with a running editor instance (file locks on manifest/archive)
Word-count/translated-% in dashboard depend on freshly gathered manifest; reporting stale data without a gather warning would mislead — report last-gather timestamp explicitly
Deleting targets/cultures touches on-disk archives; must be Plan-Mode gated and dry_run-first to avoid irreversible translation-data loss
domains.test_plan: "On a live editor with a sample project: (1) loc_string_table_create a table, loc_string_table_set_entry several keys, loc_string_table_get to confirm read-back, loc_string_table_export_csv and diff; loc_string_table_import_csv with mode=merge and re-verify counts. (2) loc_project_cultures_get baseline, loc_project_culture_add 'fr'/'ja', confirm via get. (3) Bind a UMG widget to the String Table, loc_preview_culture_set 'fr', then editor_capture_viewport to visually confirm the text re-resolved; loc_preview_culture_reset and re-capture. (4) loc_target_create a Game target with gather paths, loc_target_get to verify config; loc_gather_text returning a job_id, poll loc_job_status until done, confirm manifest/archive written. (5) loc_po_export fr -> .po, hand-edit a msgstr (and deliberately break one placeholder), loc_po_validate to confirm the placeholder error is caught, fix it, loc_po_import (dry_run then commit), loc_compile_text, loc_locres_inspect the resulting .locres to confirm the translation shipped, then loc_preview_culture_set fr again to see it in-editor. (6) loc_validate_target and loc_dashboard_report to confirm per-culture translated_% moved and no conflicts; loc_namespace_key_audit and loc_find_unlocalized_text on the sample assets to confirm audits return sane findings. Throughout: verify dry_run returns a before-image and no mutation, and that every write was undoable (Ctrl+Z) where transaction-wrapped."

tools.name: loc_string_table_create
tools.description: Create a UStringTable asset with a namespace at a content path; the foundation asset for all in-game localizable text.

tools.name: loc_string_table_set_entry
tools.signature: (asset_path, key, source_string, metadata?, dry_run?) -> {ok, key, created|updated, before?}
tools.description: Add or update a single key->source-string entry (with optional translator metadata/context) in a String Table; the core write op of the author loop.

tools.name: loc_string_table_batch_set
tools.signature: (asset_path, entries[], dry_run?) -> {ok, set_count, created, updated, conflicts[]}
tools.description: Set/update many key->value entries in ONE undo transaction; outcome-verb to avoid N round-trips when seeding a table.

tools.name: loc_string_table_remove_entry
tools.description: Remove a key from a String Table; destructive, dry_run-able, returns the removed value for undo/verify.

tools.name: loc_string_table_rename_key
tools.description: Rename a key while preserving source string and metadata; avoids the delete+recreate footgun that orphans translations.

tools.name: loc_string_table_get
tools.signature: (asset_path, limit?, offset?, filter?) -> {namespace, entries[], total, has_more, next_offset}
tools.description: Read back all entries (key, source, metadata) from a String Table, paginated; the mandatory inspect/verify pair for the write tools.

tools.name: loc_string_table_list
tools.description: List all UStringTable assets in the project with entry counts and namespaces; project-wide localization inventory.

tools.name: loc_string_table_import_csv
tools.signature: (asset_path, csv_path, mode=merge|replace, dry_run?) -> {ok, imported, skipped, conflicts[]}
tools.description: Bulk-import entries from a Key,SourceString[,Comment] CSV into a String Table; the reliable high-volume seeding path when the reflected setter is thin.

tools.name: loc_string_table_export_csv
tools.description: Export a String Table to CSV for external editing/diff; read-back + interchange tool.

tools.name: loc_culture_list
tools.description: List ICU cultures available in the engine (code, display name, plural form) with a filter; lets the agent pick valid locale codes instead of guessing.

tools.name: loc_culture_info
tools.description: Get ICU detail for one culture code: native/English name, parent/fallback chain, plural categories, RTL flag; informs translator and plural-form handling.

tools.name: loc_project_cultures_get
tools.description: Read the project's currently configured supported/cooked cultures and default culture; inspect pair before any culture mutation.

tools.name: loc_project_culture_add
tools.description: Add a supported (and optionally cooked) culture to project settings; expands which locales the packaged game ships.

tools.name: loc_project_culture_remove
tools.description: Remove a supported/cooked culture from project settings; destructive, dry_run-able.

tools.name: loc_preview_culture_set
tools.description: Switch the live editor/runtime current culture so UI text re-resolves immediately; pairs with vision-capture to visually verify a translation landed.

tools.name: loc_preview_culture_get
tools.description: Read the current editor/runtime culture and language; read-back for the preview switcher.

tools.name: loc_preview_culture_reset
tools.description: Reset preview culture back to the editor default; recovers from a preview switch that destabilized the UI.

tools.name: loc_target_list
tools.description: List localization dashboard targets (Game/Engine/plugin) with native culture, supported cultures, and last-gather word counts; the dashboard root view.

tools.name: loc_target_get
tools.description: Get one target's full config: gather search paths, file extensions, native culture, cultures, dependencies, and gather settings; inspect pair for configure.

tools.name: loc_target_create
tools.signature: (target_name, native_culture, cultures[], gather_paths[], dry_run?) -> {ok, target, config_path}
tools.description: Create a new localization target with native culture and initial supported cultures; net-new target for a feature/plugin.

tools.name: loc_target_configure
tools.signature: (target_name, gather_paths?, extensions?, native_culture?, dependencies?, dry_run?) -> {ok, changed[], before}
tools.description: Update a target's gather paths, file extensions, native culture, or dependencies in one call; outcome-verb over editing raw .ini.

tools.name: loc_target_add_culture
tools.description: Add a translation culture to a target (creates its archive dir); grows coverage without touching unrelated config.

tools.name: loc_target_remove_culture
tools.description: Remove a culture from a target; destructive, dry_run-able, reports archive files affected.

tools.name: loc_target_delete
tools.description: Delete a localization target and its config; destructive, Plan-Mode gated, lists data that will be removed.

tools.name: loc_gather_text
tools.description: Run the GatherText commandlet for a target as an async job-envelope (never blocks the game thread, unlike build_*); collects new/changed source text into the manifest/archive.

tools.name: loc_compile_text
tools.description: Compile a target's archives into .locres (the shipped binary translations) as an async job; the 'make it real in-game' step.

tools.name: loc_pipeline_run
tools.description: Run the full gather->export->import->compile sequence for a target as one tracked job; one-call end-to-end localization refresh.

tools.name: loc_job_status
tools.description: Poll a long-running localization job (gather/compile/pipeline) for state, progress, and log tail; the get_*_status gating probe required before consuming results.

tools.name: loc_po_export
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (GatherText ExportPO step / commandlet, job-envelope if large)
tools.description: Export a target+culture to a PortableObject .po file for translators; the standard interchange hand-off.

tools.name: loc_po_import
tools.signature: (target_name, culture_code, po_path, dry_run?) -> {ok, imported, changed, conflicts[]}
tools.description: Import a translated .po back into the target's archive for a culture; the return leg of the translator round-trip, dry_run-able.

tools.name: loc_po_validate
tools.description: Validate a .po file pre-import: placeholder/format-arg mismatch vs source, empty msgstr, encoding, duplicate msgid; net-new PLUMB-style quantified gate that stops corrupt translations shipping.

tools.name: loc_validate_target
tools.description: Quantified health check of a target: stale/missing translations, unresolved source changes, placeholder-integrity per culture, untranslated counts; productizes the PLUMB validate-before/after moat for localization.

tools.name: loc_dashboard_report
tools.description: Aggregate dashboard across all targets: per-culture word counts, translated %, conflicts, and last-gather timestamp; the single 'where is localization at' read-out competitors have nothing like.

tools.name: loc_find_unlocalized_text
tools.signature: (scan_paths?, limit?, offset?) -> {findings[{asset, property, text}], total, has_more}
tools.description: Scan Blueprints/UMG/DataAssets for hardcoded non-localizable strings and FText literals missing a key; net-new audit that surfaces text the gather would never catch.

tools.name: loc_namespace_key_audit
tools.description: Audit String Tables and gathered manifest for duplicate keys, namespace collisions, and orphaned keys; net-new correctness tool preventing silent translation clobbering.

tools.name: loc_locres_inspect
tools.module: python_run-backed TS (locres reader, C++ fallback in HaybaMCPToolkit if API thin)
tools.description: Read a compiled .locres back into key/value entries; verifies what actually shipped per culture, closing the compile loop.

domains.domain: Networking / replication / multiplayer testing (multiplayer PIE, replication graph, RPC/property-replication assertion harness)
domains.summary: UE drives multiplayer testing through ULevelEditorPlaySettings (PlayNumberOfClients, PlayNetMode, RunUnderOneProcess, bLaunchSeparateServer) which is a Python-editable CDO, plus FRequestPlaySessionParams overrides at launch — so the bulk of this domain ships as python_run wrappers with one small C++ extension to the existing StartPIE seam (HaybaMCPEditorHandler.cpp:81 currently builds an empty FRequestPlaySessionParams). The headline moat is a closed-loop RPC/property-replication assertion harness: configure single-process multi-client PIE, mutate on the authority world, tick, and assert convergence on every client world within a latency budget — no competitor (Epic baseline, Aura, Flop pie_test_bp, GenOrca, remiphilippe PIE control) does cross-world replication verification. We pair every write tool with an inspection/read-back tool (Flop pattern), wrap all replication-config mutations in FScopedTransaction, expose a dry-run for launch config, and layer NetEmulation (lag/jitter/loss) so assertions run under degraded network. Single-process (RunUnderOneProcess=true) is the load-bearing constraint: separate-process and true dedicated-server PIE spawn child processes the editor Python cannot introspect, so the harness gates on it and the assert tools refuse to run otherwise. Replication-graph and BP-variable-replication authoring are scoped as lower-priority with explicit engine-ceiling flags.
dependencies: THEME 0 job-envelope conversion: net_assert_* and net_replication_harness_run run tick loops; they MUST be async job-envelopes, not blocking calls, or they re-introduce the test_run game-thread freeze
Hardened python_run handler (SEH + security gate) — most tools are pyTemplate descriptors dispatched through it; ProcessCommand SEH wrap (Theme 0) so a bad reflection call cannot crash the editor
C++ extension of HaybaMCPEditorHandler::StartPIE (currently builds empty FRequestPlaySessionParams at line 86) for net_pie_start overrides
FScopedTransaction begin/end seam from 4C for the net_*_set_* mutators and undo_id return
Multi-world PIE access from editor Python — requires RunUnderOneProcess=true so server + client worlds coexist in the editor process (GEditor world contexts)
UE 4.26+ NetEmulation console subsystem for net_emulation_*
Project-level UReplicationGraph enabled for the two graph tools (otherwise they return engine_limited)
Add-a-tool refactor (Theme 1) pyTemplate factory so ~24 of these ship with zero plugin rebuild
Vision loop (4B) optional: PIE screenshot per client world for before/after replication diffs
risks: Single-process gate is load-bearing: separate-process PIE and true dedicated-server PIE spawn CHILD PROCESSES the editor Python cannot introspect — the assertion harness must hard-refuse (clear machine code) when run_under_one_process=false, or assertions silently pass against a non-existent world

RPC interception (net_assert_rpc_received) has no clean Python hook — relies on temp delegate/counter injection or BP-event instrumentation; reliable only for BP-exposed RPCs, native C++ RPCs may be unobservable (flag as limitation)
Ticking PIE worlds from a command handler risks game-thread re-entrancy / the test_run freeze class; assertions must yield via the ticker dispatch, never spin-wait
Convergence-window assertions are timing-sensitive: under net_emulation lag the default timeout_ms can false-fail; budgets must scale with applied lag

net_property_set_replication (BP variable replication flags) is genuinely hard via UE Python — likely needs C++ FBPVariableDescription edits + BP recompile; high churn, flag engine ceiling and ship P2
Replication-graph reflection is fragile across engine versions and only valid if the project ships a graph driver — gate behind a get-status probe
Driving client input / possession across worlds can desync the editor selection and PIE focus; isolate to the target client world context
domains.test_plan: On a live editor with a sample replicated project (replicated Character with a Health float + a Server RPC): 1) net_pie_configure(num_clients=2, net_mode='listen_server', run_under_one_process=true); net_pie_config_get to confirm; net_pie_config_dry_run to preview 1 server + 2 client worlds. 2) net_pie_start; net_pie_status shows server + 2 clients in-process. 3) net_replicated_actors_list(world='server') finds the characters; net_actor_replication_inspect on one shows Health replicated + the RPC with kind='server'. 4) net_assert_authority (server=authority, clients=simulated_proxy) passes. 5) net_assert_property_replicated(Health, 50) — clients converge within budget; record latency_ms. 6) net_emulation_set(lag_ms=200, packet_loss_pct=5) then re-run the Health assert with a scaled timeout — still converges. 7) net_assert_rpc_received for the Server RPC after net_drive_client_input fires it. 8) net_assert_relevancy after moving an actor far from a client. 9) net_replication_harness_run with a 4-assert suite, confirm aggregated pass/fail. 10) net_simulate_disconnect(client_index=1); net_connection_list shows one remaining. 11) net_emulation_clear; net_pie_stop; net_pie_status shows zero worlds. Negative test: net_pie_configure(run_under_one_process=false) then net_assert_property_replicated must return a clear 'single_process_required' error, not a false pass.

domains.domain: Unreal Insights / Trace Profiling (Trace.Start/Stop, channels, .utrace capture/open, CSV profiler, FrameTrace/MemTrace, stat-to-trace)
domains.summary: UE exposes all trace control through console commands (`Trace.*`, `csvProfile`, `stat startfile`, `MemReport`) executed via `GEngine->Exec(..., *GLog)` — which the plugin already does via `editor_run_console_command`. So ~80% of this domain ships as python_run/console-backed TS wrappers with NO plugin rebuild, where the real value is outcome-verbs (one-call "capture 10s of CPU+GPU+frame trace to a .utrace") and readback/analysis (parse the .utrace/.csv/.memreport artifacts in `Saved/Profiling/`) that no competitor offers. Console commands return nothing to the caller, so status/verify is done by log-file scrape or filesystem polling of the growing artifact; for production-grade status/channel enumeration I propose ONE small C++ seam over `FTraceAuxiliary`/`UE::Trace` in HaybaMCPToolkit. This is net-new moat territory: no UE MCP (Epic, Aura, Flop, GenOrca, remiphilippe) ships trace-session capture at all — pairing capture with artifact analysis and the vision loop makes Hayba the only "measure-before/after-you-mutate" UE agent. Everything lands behind Code-Mode/packs with inspection-first read tools and a dry_run on the only destructive op (capture deletion).
dependencies: editor_run_console_command (existing C++ handler — GEngine->Exec into GLog) is the backbone for every Trace.*/csvProfile/stat command
editor_stream_log / GetOutputLog (existing) for scraping console-command output since Exec returns nothing to the caller

Theme 0 job-envelope/async fix: frame_trace_quick & perf_capture_pie run for N seconds and MUST NOT block the game thread — depend on the async command conversion (docs/audit/2026-06-22-mcp-async-command-conversions.md)
python_run hardened handler (SEH + security gate) for filesystem ops on Saved/Profiling and subprocess launch of UnrealInsights.exe
Theme 1 add-a-tool refactor + pyTemplate factory so these ~34 wrappers ship as descriptors without 7-file churn
editor_start_pie + wait_for_idle (existing) for perf_capture_pie orchestration
ONE optional C++ seam in HaybaMCPToolkit over FTraceAuxiliary / UE::Trace::EnumerateChannels + TraceServices reader for robust trace_status/trace_channels_list/trace_analyze (python fallbacks exist)
UnrealInsights.exe + UnrealTraceServer binaries shipped in EngineDir/Binaries/Win64 (path discovery)
Code-Mode/deferred routing + a new 'trace' pack in packs.yaml so the 34 tools stay off the eager surface
risks: Console commands return nothing to the caller (Exec writes only to GLog) — every readback (status/channels/hitches/gpu passes) relies on log-file scraping, which is timing/format-fragile across UE versions; mitigate with the C++ FTraceAuxiliary/TraceServices seam for the load-bearing reads

Several deep captures require LAUNCH-TIME args that can't be toggled at runtime: memalloc callstacks need -trace=memory/-statnamedevents, LLM needs -llm — memtrace_start/llm_snapshot must detect-and-warn when the editor wasn't launched with them rather than silently producing empty traces
Timed captures (frame_trace_quick, perf_capture_pie) are exactly the game-thread-blocking pattern Theme 0 bans — they MUST use the async job envelope or they reintroduce editor freezes

Parsing .utrace is non-trivial: the binary format is internal; trace_analyze likely needs the TraceServices C++ analysis API or shelling trace utilities — pure-python parsing may only reach header metadata (flag the analysis depth honestly, no false advertising)
Starting a trace while one is already active, or with the network/file dest mismatched, can error or split files — trace_start must check trace_status first and surface a clear machine code
CSV/stat file locations vary (Saved/Profiling vs Saved/Profiling/CSV) and large captures can fill disk — trace_delete_captures and quota awareness needed; dry_run on delete is mandatory
UnrealInsights.exe / UnrealTraceServer may not be present in a packaged/minimal install — trace_open_insights/trace_store_status must degrade gracefully
Profiling overhead itself perturbs measurements (observer effect) — preset choices should warn when 'full' channels are enabled for steady-state perf claims
domains.test_plan: Live-editor validation on the pinned 5.7 build with HaybaMCPToolkit loaded: 1) trace_channels_list -> assert known channels (cpu,gpu,frame,memory,loadtime) appear and 'enabled' flags toggle after trace_channel_set/trace_preset_apply. 2) frame_trace_quick(duration_s=5, open_after=false) on a populated map -> assert a .utrace appears in Saved/Profiling with non-zero bytes and trace_status showed active during the window then inactive after; confirm editor did NOT freeze (concurrent wait_for_idle responds). 3) trace_analyze(latest) -> assert frame.avg_ms/p99_ms are plausible (>0, p99>=avg) and top_timers non-empty; cross-check by trace_open_insights and eyeballing the same timeline in the GUI. 4) csv_profile_start -> spawn/destroy actors via batch tools -> csv_profile_event('spawned') -> csv_profile_stop -> csv_profile_analyze: assert hitch count rises around the event row and worst_columns lists a renderer/gamethread stat. 5) mem_report(full=true) -> assert summary physical_mb matches 'stat memory' order-of-magnitude; memtrace_start with -trace not set -> assert it returns a clear 'launch-arg-missing' warning rather than an empty trace. 6) gpu_trace_frame -> assert passes[] includes BasePass/Lumen/Shadows with ms>0. 7) trace_list_captures pagination (limit=2) -> has_more/next_offset correct; trace_delete_captures(older_than_days=999, dry_run=true) -> would_delete lists files, deletes nothing; dry_run=false removes them and freed_bytes>0. 8) Negative: trace_start while already tracing -> structured error code; trace_open_insights with missing binary -> graceful {launched:false}. Compare a before/after capture across a known-heavy edit to prove the closed measure-mutate-measure loop.

domains.domain: Virtual Textures — Runtime Virtual Texture (RVT) assets/volumes/material I-O + Streaming Virtual Texture (SVT) conversion/build
domains.summary: VT today is a single read (texture_streaming_report) plus generic texture_set_settings that can flip one bool — there is no way for an agent to author the RVT pipeline end-to-end (asset → volume → bounds-align to landscape → producers writing → material sample/output → build streaming mips), nor to safely bulk-convert textures to SVT. This is a net-new moat domain: no competitor (Epic baseline, Aura, Flop, GenOrca, UAIP) ships VT authoring, and it is high-value for the worldbuilding/landscape story. Strategy: ship the whole RVT loop and SVT batch-convert as python_run-backed pyTemplate wrappers (zero plugin rebuild — UE EditorAssetLibrary/MaterialEditingLibrary cover all of it), reserve only the long-running build/streamed-mip generation for a C++ job-envelope so it never freezes the game thread. Lean hard on the moats: every mutator gets a paired *_inspect read, a dry_run preview, transaction-wrapping, and a PLUMB-style vt_validate that quantifies pipeline correctness (content-type ↔ material output match, writers present, bounds aligned, pool sized) before/after mutate, plus vision-loop debug-viz capture so the agent can see the VT actually rendering.
dependencies: Theme 0 transport/SEH fixes: rvt_volume_build_streamed_mips and svt_build MUST run as job-envelopes (HaybaMCPBuildHandler async pattern) or they re-introduce the build_* 300s game-thread freeze
Theme 1 add-a-tool refactor: all python_run-backed tools ship as pyTemplate descriptors (zero rebuild) — depends on the pyTemplate factory landing
Hardened python_run (SEH + 3-tier gate + dangling-delegate gate) — the execution substrate for ~28 of these 32 tools
Existing texture handler (HaybaMCPTextureHandler.cpp) + texture_streaming_report — svt_report/svt_enable build on its size-tag reads and the virtual_texture_streaming alias
Vision loop (editor_capture_viewport / wait_for_shaders) for vt_debug_capture
PLUMB validator harness for vt_validate (green/red plan-mode overlay, unsat-core surfacing)
Transaction seam (FScopedTransaction / shared begin/commit) so vt_pipeline_setup bundles into one Ctrl+Z
UE modules: RuntimeVirtualTexture / VirtualTexturing must be enabled; r.VirtualTextures project setting (vt_check_support gates this)
risks: Streamed-mip / SVT builds are genuinely long and DDC-bound — if not job-enveloped they freeze the editor (the named P0 bug class); must poll via rvt_build_status, never block
Enabling r.VirtualTextures / RVT support is a RESTART-required project setting — vt_enable_project_support can only flag needs_restart, not hot-apply; agents may wrongly assume it took effect
Material content-type ↔ output-pin mismatch silently produces black RVT; vt_validate must catch it but pin-name reflection across UE versions (5.7→5.8) is brittle

RVT volume bounds-align is rotation+bounds sensitive (level-set memory: landscape spawn quirks); set_bounds via Python may not exactly match the editor 'Set Bounds' button — needs live verification against C++ BuildBounds
Bulk svt_batch_convert can balloon DDC/cook time and convert normal maps that shouldn't be VT — dry_run default + exclude_normal_maps mitigations are mandatory, not optional
VirtualTextureStreaming change requires UpdateResource()/recompile; mass conversion may stall the asset registry — chunk the batch and respect frame budget

RuntimeVirtualTextureComponent / material-expression Python APIs are partially editor-only and version-locked (pinned 5.7.0); some setters may need legacy ue_invoke fallback or a thin C++ shim if reflection gaps appear
domains.test_plan: On a live editor with a real ALandscape (per memory, must be a true Landscape, not the spawn placeholder): 1) vt_check_support → confirm support flags; if off, vt_enable_project_support and restart. 2) rvt_asset_create(/Game/VT/RVT_Terrain, BaseColor_Normal_Roughness) then rvt_asset_inspect to verify content_type + zero refs. 3) rvt_volume_spawn bound to the landscape, rvt_volume_set_bounds(snap_to_landscape=true); rvt_volume_inspect → bounds_min/max non-degenerate and aligned_to == landscape. 4) rvt_landscape_bind → rvt_audit_writers shows the landscape as a writer with RuntimeVirtualTexture pass. 5) On the landscape material: rvt_material_add_output(auto) and a consumer rvt_material_add_sample(RVT_Terrain); material_compile; rvt_material_inspect → no type mismatches. 6) rvt_volume_build_streamed_mips → poll rvt_build_status until done. 7) vt_debug_capture(runtime_vt) → screenshot shows the RVT page coverage over the terrain (vision verify), then capture(none) to restore. 8) vt_validate(level) → expect pass:true; deliberately break it (unbind landscape) and confirm unsat_core names the missing writer. 9) SVT side: import/identify a 4K texture, svt_batch_convert(dry_run=true) lists it, run with dry_run=false, svt_report shows svt_count incremented and est VRAM drop; svt_revert one and re-check. 10) Idempotency/safety: re-run rvt_asset_create on same path (exists handling), run a destructive delete with dry_run=true first, confirm one Ctrl+Z undoes a full vt_pipeline_setup run. Cross-check every footprint/format read-back against texture_streaming_report and the editor's own RVT volume details panel.

domains.domain: DataTables / Curves / Gameplay Tags / Data Assets (structured-data authoring)
domains.summary: UE structured-data is a high-frequency authoring loop (game balance tables, AI/animation curves, ability tag taxonomies, config DataAssets) that today has only a 3-verb C++ stub (data_create/get/set, UDataAsset-only) and zero DataTable/Curve/GameplayTag coverage — asset-import handles FBX/USD/Datasmith but none of these. Nearly the entire surface is reachable through UE Python (DataTableFunctionLibrary fill/export CSV+JSON, RichCurve key APIs, GameplayTagsManager, AssetTools/AssetRegistry), so I deliver it as python_run-backed TS descriptors with no plugin rebuild, reserving only the existing C++ DataAsset reflection path. The moat plays are inspection-first (struct_inspect, *_inspect read tools so the agent knows columns/rowstruct/tag-tree before mutating), dry-run validation of CSV/JSON against the RowStruct before commit (PLUMB-style validate-before-mutate), and one-undo batch row/property writes. I prioritize the create + import + row-CRUD + introspection core (P0), then curve/curve-table + gameplay-tag management (P1), then batch/query/rename niceties (P2/P3). Every write verb pairs with a read-back verify and respects Plan-Mode for destructive ops.
dependencies: Existing C++ HaybaMCPToolkit DataAssetHandler (data_create/get/set) — surface as first-class descriptors and extend with data_set_many for the batch verb
Hardened python_run handler + runUePythonJson/_emit/_err harness (mcp-tools/hayba-mcp/src/tools/ue-python.ts) — the no-rebuild vehicle for ~32 of 37 tools

UE Python modules: DataTableFunctionLibrary (CSV/JSON fill+export, row names, curve-table eval), AssetTools+factories (DataTableFactory/CurveFloatFactory/CurveTableFactory), AssetRegistry, EditorAssetLibrary, GameplayTagsManager, AssetManager, RichCurve key API
Add-a-tool refactor (Theme 1) ToolDescriptor + pyTemplate factory — these all land as descriptors auto-collected into the data/structured-data pack
Transaction seam (4C ScopedEditorTransaction / C++ FScopedTransaction) for one-undo batch verbs and dry_run->commit generalization
Plan-Mode gate (bPlanApproved) for destructive verbs (remove/clear/delete)
PLUMB/validator wrap for dry_run schema validation of CSV/JSON against RowStruct/UScriptStruct
risks: GameplayTag ini authoring is the weakest Python path: IGameplayTagsEditorModule.AddNewGameplayTagToINI may not be reflected to Python in 5.7 — fallback is direct DefaultGameplayTags.ini edit + GameplayTagsManager reload, which risks config races and requires editor reload to fully propagate. Flag as engine-limit; may need a small C++ command in HaybaMCPToolkit.

Single-row DataTable CRUD has no direct Python add/remove-row API in all versions; implementing via export-to-JSON -> splice -> fill-replace is correct but O(table) per edit and loses any non-exported transient state — batch verbs mitigate, but very large tables (10k+ rows) may be slow.

fill_data_table_from_* replaces vs merges semantics differ by version; the replace?/merge behavior must be verified per engine version (pinned 5.7) or rows can be silently dropped — hence dry_run + read-back are P0.
RichCurve key handles in Python are fiddly (tangent/interp enums, auto-tangent recompute on PostEditChange); curve_float_set_keys must reset and re-add deterministically or tangents drift.

struct_inspect on Blueprint UStructs and instanced/EditInline DataAsset properties may hit FJsonObjectConverter '<unsupported:type>' fallbacks (already present in C++ data_get) — nested struct columns may not round-trip losslessly via CSV (JSON only).
Destructive verbs (remove/delete/clear) without the reference-aware scan can orphan GAS abilities or break cooked content — reference checks are mandatory, not optional.
DataTable/Curve fill on the game thread for big imports could approach the command timeout; align with job-envelope ceilings or chunk large imports.
domains.test_plan: Run against a live 5.7 editor with the toolkit plugin loaded. 1) struct_inspect a known native struct (e.g. a project FTableRowBase subclass) and confirm field list matches the C++ definition. 2) datatable_create with that row_struct, datatable_inspect to confirm columns, datatable_import_csv with a 3-row CSV (dry_run first -> expect zero mutation + warnings, then commit), datatable_export json and diff against input, datatable_list_rows + datatable_row_get to verify a specific row, datatable_row_set to update one field then row_get to confirm, datatable_rows_set_batch 5 rows then Ctrl+Z once and confirm all 5 revert (one-undo proof), datatable_row_remove + datatable_find_rows on a column predicate. 3) curve_float_create, curve_float_set_keys with 3 keys + tangents, curve_float_get to read back, curve_float_evaluate at intermediate times and assert interpolation matches expected; open the asset in Curve Editor and eyeball. 4) curve_table_create + curve_table_import + curve_table_evaluate_row. 5) gameplaytag_add a nested tag (A.B.C), gameplaytag_list with prefix='A', gameplaytag_query A.B to confirm child C, then gameplaytag_remove with dry_run reporting referencers; verify DefaultGameplayTags.ini updated and manager reloaded (Project Settings > GameplayTags shows it). 6) data_asset_create a PrimaryDataAsset Blueprint class, data_asset_get, data_asset_set a struct property, data_asset_set_batch then single undo, data_asset_list by class, primary_asset_query by type. 7) structured_data_delete with dry_run=true on a referenced asset -> expect blocked + referencers listed; force delete an unreferenced one. Throughout, confirm no editor freeze (commands return under timeout) and pair each write with its read-back verify tool. Capture before/after via editor_capture_viewport only where the asset is visibly placed; otherwise rely on JSON read-backs.

domains.domain: Water system (UE Water plugin) — WaterBody Ocean/Lake/River/Custom, WaterZone, Gerstner/spectrum waves, water + underwater materials, landscape carving brush
domains.summary: The UE Water plugin is fully worldbuilding-relevant (oceans, lakes, rivers carving into landscape, animated Gerstner waves) and is completely uncovered by Hayba and every surveyed competitor (Epic 5.8, Aura, Flop, GenOrca 253, ChiR24, remiphilippe) — none ship a single Water tool, so this is almost entirely net-new moat. Nearly all of it is reachable through UE Editor-Scripting Python (unreal.WaterBodyOcean/Lake/River, WaterBodyComponent.set_water_waves, GerstnerWaterWaveGeneratorSimple, AWaterZone, spline point metadata), so the domain ships as python_run-backed TS descriptors under src/tools/water/ with zero plugin rebuild — only the buffer-viz capture and the FScopedTransaction wrap reach into HaybaMCPToolkit C++. We lean into three moats: inspection-first paired read tools, PLUMB quantified validation (water-below-terrain, zone-covers-bodies, sane wavelength/steepness), and outcome-verbs (water_river_from_path, water_ocean_preset_apply) over low-level primitives per DCC best practice. Every mutating tool is transaction-wrapped, supports dry_run, and pairs with a *_inspect read-back so agents validate-before/after-mutate.
dependencies: Water plugin enabled in the project (preflight via water_check_plugin)
A Landscape actor present for lakes/rivers to carve terrain via WaterLandscapeBrush/WaterBrushManager
Rivers require a valid spline path; WaterBodyRiver carries per-point width/depth/velocity metadata
A WaterZone must exist and bound the bodies for rendering (5.7 uses bounded non-tiled zones)
Cross-cutting FScopedTransaction seam (Theme 4C / HaybaGameThread::RunSync) for one-Ctrl+Z bundling
PLUMB validator (validator_run / plumb_validate) for water_validate
Vision-capture domain (render_camera / editor_capture_viewport, orbit + buffer passes from 4B) for water_preview_capture
Actor + selection/batch infra (EditorActorSubsystem) for water_bodies_select / water_bodies_batch_set
runUePythonJson plumbing in src/tools/ue-python.ts (HAYBA_JSON contract) for all python-backed tools
Code-Mode / deferred routing + a 'water' pack so the ~30 tools land behind on-demand discovery, not the eager surface
risks: Water plugin not enabled → every unreal.WaterBody* class is missing; water_check_plugin must gate the whole pack and return an actionable enable hint instead of a Python ImportError

UE Python wave coverage is partial: GerstnerWaterWaveGeneratorSimple params are exposed but the spectrum (Phillips/JONSWAP) generator and per-wave arrays may be read-only or EditAnywhere-only — flag spectrum tools as engine-limited, fall back to template WaterWavesAsset instantiation
Editing river spline points + per-point metadata (WaterSplineMetadata) programmatically is fiddly; point count and metadata arrays must stay in lockstep or the body fails to build geometry

Terrain carving requires the WaterBrushManager to re-render the landscape brush; changes can appear stale until a rebuild/dirty — water_brush_rebuild + mark_package_dirty needed, and a full rebuild can be slow (watch the build-freeze class of bug — keep it off the 300s game-thread path or job-envelope it)
WaterZone in 5.7 is bounded/non-tiled and owns the water-info render target + MID; resizing or moving bodies outside the zone silently drops rendering — water_validate must assert zone coverage

Water Material/MID edits can hit the same NormalCodeChunk recompile crash class as the material domain; prefer set-on-instance (MID/material instance params) over editing the master water material graph

Spawning AWaterBody via Python may yield a placeholder-like partial actor if the WaterSubsystem/zone isn't initialized (cf. the Landscape spawn placeholder-stub memory) — verify component validity in the read-back, not just spawn success

Many properties are only meaningful at runtime/PIE (wave animation, fluid sim ripples); static editor capture won't show motion — water_preview_capture should note this and optionally drive a short PIE for wave verification
domains.test_plan: On a live editor with the Water plugin enabled and a Landscape present: (1) water_check_plugin → expect ok + plugin version; on a project without it, expect a clean 'enable Water plugin' error not a stack trace. (2) water_body_ocean_create at the landscape center, then water_body_inspect → assert AWaterBodyOcean spawned, has a valid WaterBodyComponent and is bound to a WaterZone. (3) water_zone_inspect → confirm the ocean is inside zone bounds; if no zone, water_zone_create then re-inspect. (4) water_waves_set_gerstner (wavelength/steepness/num_waves/seed), water_waves_inspect → read back the generator params match. (5) editor_capture_viewport / water_preview_capture orbit around the ocean → visually confirm water surface renders (and note motion only shows in PIE; optionally editor_start_pie for a wave screenshot). (6) water_body_river_create from a 4-point path over the landscape, water_river_spline_get → assert point count + per-point width/depth/velocity; water_brush_rebuild → screenshot the carved riverbed. (7) water_body_lake_create, then water_validate → expect green (water below terrain at shoreline, zone covers all bodies, wavelength/steepness in sane range); deliberately move the lake above terrain and re-run → expect a red unsat-core finding. (8) water_bodies_select(class=WaterBodyLake) + water_bodies_batch_set(target_wave_mask_depth) across selection, then Ctrl+Z once → assert all reverted in a single undo (transaction bundling). (9) every create/set tool with dry_run:true first → assert it reports the planned change and mutates nothing, then commit.

tools.name: water_body_inspect
tools.signature: (body_path) -> {ok, class, component_valid, waves, materials, affects_landscape, zone, properties}
tools.description: Deep read-back of one water body: component validity, depth/width, wave asset, MID params, physics/affects-landscape flags, owning zone. Why: paired read for validate-before/after-mutate and to catch placeholder-stub spawns.

tools.name: water_body_ocean_create
tools.signature: (location?, extent?, zone_path?, label?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, body_path, zone, planned?}
tools.description: Spawn an AWaterBodyOcean sized to the landscape/zone with sensible defaults and auto-bind to a WaterZone. Why: the single most common worldbuilding water op; outcome verb over raw actor_spawn.

tools.name: water_body_lake_create
tools.signature: (location, radius_or_points, water_z?, zone_path?, label?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, body_path, planned?}
tools.description: Spawn an AWaterBodyLake from a closed spline/footprint at a given water level, carving the shoreline into the landscape. Why: lakes are a core terrain-water feature, uncovered.

tools.name: water_body_river_create
tools.signature: (points:[vec3], width?, depth?, velocity?, zone_path?, label?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, body_path, point_count, planned?}
tools.description: Spawn an AWaterBodyRiver following a world-space path with default per-point width/depth/velocity. Why: outcome verb that hides spline+metadata wiring; rivers are the hardest water body to author by hand.

tools.name: water_river_from_path
tools.signature: (source_path|points, start_width?, end_width?, mouth_zone?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, body_path, sampled_points, planned?}
tools.description: High-level: build a river from an existing landscape spline, named actor path, or polyline, auto-sampling width from terrain and tapering to the mouth. Why: top-tier outcome verb (DCC outcome-over-primitive best practice).

tools.name: water_body_custom_create
tools.signature: (location, mesh?, water_z?, zone_path?, label?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, body_path, planned?}
tools.description: Spawn an AWaterBodyCustom (mesh-driven water, e.g. swimming pool/fountain pond) not tied to landscape carving. Why: covers bespoke water surfaces the ocean/lake/river verbs cannot.

tools.name: water_body_island_create
tools.signature: (location, radius_or_points, target_body?, label?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, island_path, planned?}
tools.description: Spawn an AWaterBodyIsland that pushes water away (raises terrain) within an ocean/lake. Why: islands and exclusion are the standard way to author coastlines.

tools.name: water_exclusion_volume_create
tools.signature: (location, box_extent, exclude_bodies?:[path], label?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, volume_path, planned?}
tools.description: Spawn an AWaterBodyExclusionVolume to cut holes in water (caves, boats, docks) for selected bodies. Why: required for believable water/structure intersection.

tools.name: water_river_spline_get
tools.description: Read back a river's spline: ordered points with per-point width/depth/velocity metadata. Why: paired read so wave/shape edits are verifiable and point/metadata arrays stay in lockstep.

tools.name: water_river_spline_set_points
tools.description: Replace/append/insert river spline points and keep WaterSplineMetadata arrays in lockstep, then mark the body dirty. Why: core river shaping; the metadata-lockstep risk makes a guarded tool essential.

tools.name: water_river_point_set
tools.signature: (body_path, index|range, width?, depth?, velocity?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, updated_indices, planned?}
tools.description: Set width/depth/velocity on a single river spline point (or a range) without touching geometry. Why: fine flow tuning (rapids, deltas) without rebuilding the whole spline.

tools.name: water_waves_inspect
tools.signature: (body_path) -> {ok, generator, num_waves, min_wavelength, max_wavelength, steepness, seed, direction, asset?}
tools.description: Read the wave setup of a body: generator type, wavelength range, steepness, num_waves, seed, direction, attached WaterWavesAsset. Why: paired read for the most-tuned water parameter.

tools.name: water_waves_set_gerstner
tools.signature: (body_path, num_waves?, min_wavelength?, max_wavelength?, steepness?, wind_dir?, seed?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, applied, planned?}
tools.description: Configure a body's GerstnerWaterWaveGeneratorSimple (num_waves, wavelength range, amplitude/steepness, wind direction, seed). Why: the primary knob for ocean look; flatten args + sane-range validate.

tools.name: water_waves_set_spectrum
tools.signature: (body_path, spectrum='phillips', wind_speed?, fetch?, peak_enhancement?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, applied|engine_limited, planned?}
tools.description: Configure the spectrum (Phillips/JONSWAP-style) Gerstner generator where the engine exposes it; flagged engine-limited with template fallback. Why: realistic open-ocean spectra; honest about UE Python ceilings.

tools.name: water_waves_asset_create
tools.description: Create a reusable UWaterWavesAsset (named wave preset) so multiple bodies share one wave definition. Why: DRY wave authoring across an ocean + connected seas.

tools.name: water_waves_assign
tools.description: Assign an existing WaterWavesAsset to one or many bodies (or detach to per-body waves). Why: share/swap wave presets in one call; pairs with batch.

tools.name: water_waves_reseed
tools.description: Re-randomize the wave seed(s) on selected bodies for variation while keeping wavelength/steepness. Why: cheap variety verb; common iteration step.

tools.name: water_body_set_property
tools.signature: (body_path, key:Literal, value, dry_run=false) -> {ok, old, new, planned?}
tools.description: Generic guarded setter for whitelisted WaterBody/WaterBodyComponent props (water_z, target_wave_mask_depth, river width/depth, collision, navigation, max_wave_height). Why: covers the long tail without a tool-per-field; validated enum of keys.

tools.name: water_body_set_material
tools.description: Set a body's water/underwater/HLOD material (prefer MID instance params over editing the master graph to dodge the recompile-crash class). Why: appearance control; safety-aware.

tools.name: water_set_underwater_post_process
tools.signature: (target_path, material_path?, fog_color?, extinction?, scattering?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, applied, planned?}
tools.description: Set/tune the underwater post-process material + fog/extinction/scattering on a body or zone. Why: underwater look is a distinct, commonly-requested water feature.

tools.name: water_body_set_landscape_affecting
tools.signature: (body_path, affects_landscape:bool, brush_priority?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, applied, needs_rebuild, planned?}
tools.description: Enable/disable terrain carving for a body and set its brush blend priority. Why: controls whether water cuts the landscape (the single biggest worldbuilding side-effect of water).

tools.name: water_brush_rebuild
tools.module: python_run-backed TS: src/tools/water/brush-rebuild.ts (job-envelope; C++ ticker path if slow)
tools.description: Force the WaterBrushManager/WaterLandscapeBrush to re-render so terrain carving and water-info reflect recent edits; job-enveloped to avoid the game-thread build-freeze. Why: edits look stale until this runs.

tools.name: water_zone_create
tools.signature: (location?, extent?, resolution?, label?, dry_run=false) -> {ok, zone_path, planned?}
tools.description: Spawn an AWaterZone sized to bound a set of bodies / the landscape, with default render-target resolution and tessellation. Why: bodies do not render without a covering zone (5.7 bounded zones).

tools.name: water_zone_inspect
tools.description: Read a WaterZone: bounds, render-target/water-info resolution, tessellation/LOD far distance, and which bodies it covers vs. orphaned. Why: paired read; surfaces the silent 'body outside zone' rendering drop.

tools.name: water_zone_set_property
tools.signature: (zone_path, key:Literal, value, dry_run=false) -> {ok, old, new, planned?}
tools.description: Set whitelisted WaterZone props: extent/bounds, water-info render-target resolution, tessellated-water tile size, LOD far distance, velocity/depth texture settings. Why: perf + quality tuning of the whole water render.

tools.name: water_zone_rebuild
tools.description: Mark the zone's water-info texture / MID dirty and trigger an update so depth/velocity/flow textures regenerate. Why: zone-level analogue of brush_rebuild for the render path.

tools.name: water_bodies_select
tools.parity: Roblox search_by_property / Unity select-by-query (net-new for Water)
tools.description: Selection management: select water bodies in the editor by class, tag, owning zone, or name query and return their paths. Why: feeds batch ops; matches the batch/selection mandate (4D).

tools.name: water_bodies_batch_set
tools.signature: (body_paths:[path]|selection, key:Literal, value, dry_run=false) -> {ok, changed, failed, planned?}
tools.description: Apply one whitelisted property (or wave preset) across many bodies in a single transaction. Why: mass tuning of an archipelago/river network; one Ctrl+Z (named differentiator vs Epic per-call undo).

tools.name: water_body_delete
tools.description: Delete one or many water bodies (and optionally orphaned islands/exclusions) inside an FScopedTransaction, with a dry_run that lists what would be removed. Why: safe destructive op respecting Plan-Mode.

tools.name: water_transaction_wrap
tools.description: Bundle a sequence of water mutations into ONE undo checkpoint (begin/commit/abort) via the C++ FScopedTransaction seam. Why: multi-step water authoring collapses to a single Ctrl+Z (moat 4C).

tools.name: water_validate
tools.description: PLUMB-style quantified check of the water scene: bodies below terrain at shoreline, every body inside a zone, wavelength/steepness/amplitude in physical range, river width/depth monotonic-ish, no overlapping zones; returns green/red + unsat-core. Why: closed-loop correctness engine, the worldbuilding moat.

tools.name: water_preview_capture
tools.module: MIX: python_run orbit/auto-frame (src/tools/water/preview-capture.ts) + HaybaMCPToolkit buffer-viz pass
tools.description: Vision read-back: auto-frame and orbit/turntable capture of a water body (plus optional depth/normal buffer pass), returning MIME-typed image blocks; notes that wave motion only shows under PIE and can drive a short PIE for a wave frame. Why: visual validate-after-mutate, extends the vision moat (4B).

tools.name: water_ocean_preset_apply
tools.description: Outcome verb: apply a named look preset (calm / choppy / stormy / tropical-lagoon / arctic) that sets waves, material/MID params, and underwater fog coherently on a body or zone. Why: one-call art direction; outcome-over-primitive, great agent ergonomics.

tools.name: water_zone_mesh_stats
tools.description: Introspect water render cost: quad-tree/tessellation tile counts, render-target memory, LOD distribution for a zone. Why: unglamorous perf read so agents can right-size resolution before shipping a world.
